rows.original: Anni smiles. "I know that our people — frost elves, not just valkyries — are mostly known for worshiping Lumia, and it's true, we do! A lot of the things that matter to us are the things she provides. Fertility of the soil, fertility of the body. Close-knit families. A safe, warm hearth to return to every evening. Battling darkness, protecting the innocent. And especially the light of the sun. It matters a lot in these lands, where days are likely to be overcast and snowy as anything else. There are even days in winter when the sun's light never quite shines up here in the Rift, so we have to bring it out ourselves — [flags.WC_BALL|as I'm sure you remember from our Festivus celebrations|we have a whole festival for it in midwinter]. "Here's the thing: our gods are gods. They answer prayers. We do things for them, and they do things for us that only they can do. For many peoples around the world, relationships with their gods are just that. You need to make sure your crops grow, so you pray to Lumia. You need success in the hunt, so you pray to Velun. You need talent at the forge, so you pray to Nareva. Like everybody else, we frost elves worship all the gods in their own measure, but Lumia most of all, because she gives us what we most need." [pc.dcb |"Give a little, get a little. I guess it's fair." "It goes beyond just fair," she adds. "There's always more to it. |"[pc.bg acolyte |Just like what the priests told us all back home |That all makes sense ]," you say thoughtfully. "But... it's not just a transaction for [pc.swornGod lumia |the likes of us |[pc.bg acolyte |us |you ] ][pc.bg acolyte |. |, is it ]? People don't care that much about just trading something for something." "You're absolutely right. |"She's really sweet like that." Then you tilt your head slightly and furrow your brow all thinky-like. "But wait a second. [pc.bg acolyte |I remember all the priest classes! We're |You're ] not just trading stuff[pc.bg acolyte |; we |! You ] care about her a lot more than that." "I do," she says, grinning. "You're absolutely right. ] Because our gods aren't just gods. They're people, with all of our good and bad. They incarnate among us, they help us. Sometimes they do things that don't help us so much, but they do care about us. Not to the point of controlling every part of our lives, pampering us, saving us from all harm or difficulty to let us live in a dream world... but ask, and they tend to answer. Whether with their own power or —" the grin gets a little bigger "— by sending people like me to help. "Our people don't just worship Lumia because she answers prayers about what we most need. Nor do we worship her just because our kings and queens tell us to. We worship her because she was there for us: she stood between us all and annihilation. We worship her because she's still there for us. And we worship her because she and our people have grown together. We're for her and she's for us. I don't know if every one of us would call it friendship, but it's something very close to family." She spreads her hands. "Besides, the festivals are fun, the camaraderie is lovely, and the temples feel as warm and welcoming as a family hearth. And, as a warrior, our lady kicks all kinds of butt." [pc.isSoulbound |[pc.swornGod lumia |"[pc.isBimbo |Hee hee. ]I wish I were as good at the pitch as you are[pc.isBimbo |!" |," you laugh. ] She dips her head in acknowledgment, still smiling. "You get better with practice, and I've had a lot of it. Still, like I said, being Lumia's Chosen doesn't mean that praying to other gods is off limits. Our lady helps with a lot, but she's not going to do much if you're fretting about a problem of, say, Narevan craft or Sorran seamanship. And we're very free to attend other gods' festivals, form close relationships with their own people — or their own chosen, even." |You [pc.isBimbo |giggle. "You make being a sun mommy sound like lots of fun! Someone else already has my soul |chuckle. "A persuasive pitch. I'm already spoken for ], though." "Don't worry," she laughs. "Pledging yourself to one god doesn't make the other six off limits — at least as far as prayers go. I've had plenty of fun at festivals of Velun and worshiped at altars of Nareva and Sorra, too, when I've needed them. Your soul is spoken for, but you're not married to [pc.swornGod keros nareva |Keros |Nareva ]." ] |[pc.dcb |You roll your eyes. "Going for the hard sell?" |"You're pretty good at that pitch," you laugh. |"Oooh! You make it sound so fun!" ] She holds up her hands, laughing. "I'm not trying to convert you[annika.kissed | any more than I already have, darling ]. Just trying to answer your question. Although I'd be remiss if I didn't tell you that even swearing your life to Lumia's service, let alone living among us and worshiping as we do, doesn't prevent you from worshiping other gods. She's the first of the Seven in our hearts, not the only one." ] "What about other deities or powers? Outside the Seven?" "It's not, mmm, recommended," she says carefully. "But unless that power is something dark and vicious and demanding violence from its worshipers, like the Khushkan Nightmare or an actual Wraith, we of the Order at least don't take issue with it. We're here to protect people, not convert them, and we've seen enough to know that spearpoint is a poor way to get people to join the faithful." [flags.ARCHWAY_BOTH_SAVED |You decide to pass over the 'actual Wraith' comment. ]"What about the druids and the schism?" At the sounds of those words, Anni grimaces. "That's... complicated. It's also one of the reasons that we're now very agreed that faith cannot be forced. Whatever the elves of centuries ago did to each other, none of us now want to perpetuate the sins of our mothers. It's a long road [party.has etheryn |you've set us on, [etheryn.crowned |Your Majesty |Lady Etheryn ]," she continues, turning to your [etheryn.married |nearby, attentively-listening wife |elven companion ], "but one we are prepared to walk, too." |[etheryn.crowned |Queen |Lady ] Etheryn has set us on, but we're prepared to walk down it with her." ]
rows.translation: 安妮微笑着说道：“我知道，我们族人——冰霜精灵，而不仅仅是女武神——大多以崇拜卢米娅而闻名，这确实是事实。对我们来说，她所提供的许多东西都至关重要：土壤的肥沃，人体的健康与活力。 关系紧密的家庭。每一个夜晚，都是可以回归的安全而温暖的港湾。与黑暗抗争，保护无辜的人们……尤其是阳光。在这些地方，阳光尤为重要，因为这里的天气往往阴沉多雪。 即使在冬天，也有某些日子里，裂谷这里的阳光根本不会照进来，因此我们就必须自己把光“请”进来才行—— [flags.WC_BALL|正如你们肯定还记得我们在Festivus庆典上的那些时光……|我们在仲冬时节会为这个活动举办一场盛大的庆典。]事情是这样的：我们的神明…… 神明它们回应人们的祈祷。我们为它们做事，而它们也会为我们做只有它们才能做到的事情。对世界上许多民族来说，他们与神明之间的关系就是这样的。当你需要庄稼顺利生长时，你就会向卢米娅祈祷；在狩猎中希望获得成功，你就会向维伦祈祷；在锻造工作中需要灵巧的手艺，你就会向纳雷瓦祈祷。和其他人一样，我们霜之精灵也会以自己的方式崇拜所有的神明，但其中最为重要的是卢米娅，因为她能给予我们最需要的东西。 [pc.dcb |付出一点，就能得到一点。我想这样挺公平的。” “其实这不仅仅是为了公平，”她补充道，“其中总隐藏着更多的意义。 |"[pc.bg acolyte |就像那些牧师在我们家乡告诉我们的那样。 |这一切都合情合理。 ]你是这么说的，”他若有所思地说道，“但是……这不仅仅是一笔交易而已。 [pc.swornGod lumia |像我们这样的人 |[pc.bg acolyte |我们 |你 ] ][pc.bg acolyte |. |是吗？ ]人们其实并不太在意用某样东西去交换另一样东西。” “你说得完全正确。 |她真的那么温柔。”然后你微微歪着头，皱起眉头，一副若有所思的样子。“不过等一下…… [pc.bg acolyte |我记得所有的牧师职业啊！我们…… |你真是…… ] 不仅仅是交易物品[pc.bg acolyte |我们 |! 你 ] 我对她的关心远不止于此。” “确实如此，”她笑着说，“你完全说得对。 ] 因为我们的神明并非仅仅是神明。他们也是人，拥有我们人类所有的优点与缺点。他们会降临到我们中间，帮助我们。有时候，他们所做的某些事可能并不会对我们产生太大的帮助，但他们确实是在关心我们。他们并不会控制我们生活的每一个方面，也不会过分溺爱我们，更不会把我们从一切伤害和困难中拯救出来，让我们生活在一个梦幻的世界里。但是只要去询问，他们通常都会给出答案。无论是依靠他们自己的力量，还是——”他的笑容变得更加灿烂——“通过派遣像我这样的人来提供帮助。” “我们的人民崇拜Lumia，并不仅仅是因为她能够回应我们最迫切的需求。 我们崇拜她，并不是因为我们的国王和王后命令我们这样做。我们崇拜她，是因为她在我们最需要的时候出现在我们身边——她站在我们所有人与毁灭之间，保护了我们。我们崇拜她，是因为她…… 仍然 她一直都在我们身边。我们崇拜她，因为她和我们的族人一起成长壮大。我们支持她，她也支持我们。虽然不是每个人都会将这种关系称为友谊，但它确实与亲情非常相似。”她摊开双手继续说道，“此外，这些节日非常有趣，大家之间的情谊也很深厚，而那些寺庙更是温暖如家。而且，作为一名战士，我们的这位女士确实非常厉害，能够战胜各种敌人。 [pc.isSoulbound |[pc.swornGod lumia |"[pc.isBimbo |嘿嘿。 ]我真希望自己在推销能力上能像你一样出色。[pc.isBimbo |!" |你笑了。 ] 她微微低头表示认同，脸上依然带着笑容：“多练习就会变好，而我练习的机会确实很多。不过，就像我之前说的，成为卢米娅的选民并不意味着不能向其他神明祈祷。我们的女神确实能提供很多帮助，但如果你在面对纳雷万工艺或索兰航海技术这类问题时感到困扰，她也无能为力。而且，我们完全可以自由地参加其他神明的庆典，与那些神明的信徒们建立亲密的关系——甚至与他们选中的使者们建立联系。 |你 [pc.isBimbo |咯咯笑起来，你说当‘太阳妈妈’听起来好像很有趣似的！其实已经有别人占据了我的心灵了…… |轻笑道：“说得很有说服力啊，我已经决定要买了。 ]不过，也没关系。” “别担心，”她笑着说，“只信仰一位神明，并不意味着其他六位神明就不能被祈求——至少在祈祷方面是如此。在维伦节期间，我也玩得很开心；而在需要帮助的时候，我也会在纳雷瓦和索拉的神坛前祈祷。你的灵魂已经得到了庇护，但你自己…… 已婚 向 [pc.swornGod keros nareva |Keros |纳雷瓦 ]." ] |[pc.dcb |你翻了个白眼：“打算强行推销吗？ |你在这方面做得相当不错啊，”你笑着说。 |哦哦！你说得听起来真有趣啊！ ] 她举起双手，笑着说：“我并不是想说服你改变主意。[annika.kissed | 亲爱的，我的拥有已经够多了。 ]我只是想回答你的问题。虽然如果我不告诉你这一点，那就算是失职了——即使你发誓要效忠于卢米娅，甚至像我们一样生活、像我们一样崇拜她，这也并不能阻止你崇拜其他神明。在她的心中，她是七位神明中的第一位，但并不是唯一的那一位。 ] 那其他的神灵或力量呢？除了那七位之外？” “嗯，我们并不推荐这些力量，”她谨慎地回答，“但除非这种力量具有邪恶的性质，会迫使信徒们使用暴力来崇拜它，比如库什坎噩梦或者真正的幽灵之类的存在，否则我们这个组织至少不会反对这些力量。我们的存在目的是保护人们，而不是强迫他们信仰某种东西。而我们的经验也告诉我们，用武力强迫人们加入信仰的行列，其实并不是一个好办法。 [flags.ARCHWAY_BOTH_SAVED |你决定忽略那条关于“真正的幽灵”的评论。 ]那德鲁伊们以及那场分裂又该如何解释呢？” 听到这些话，安妮露出了苦涩的表情：“那……很复杂。这也是我们如今都一致认同的一点：信仰是不能被强迫的。无论几个世纪前那些精灵们彼此之间做了什么，我们现在都没有人愿意继续重蹈那些过去的错误。这是一条漫长的道路…… [party.has etheryn |你让我们开始行动了。 [etheryn.crowned |陛下 |艾瑟琳女士 ]她继续说道，转向了你。 [etheryn.married |在一旁认真聆听的妻子 |精灵伙伴 ]但也是我们愿意去尝试的道路。 |[etheryn.crowned |女王 |女士 ] 埃瑟琳已经为我们指明了方向，但我们愿意和她一起走下去。 ]
rows.raw: ' Anni smiles. "I know that our people — frost elves, not just valkyries — are mostly known for worshiping Lumia, and it's true, we do! A lot of the things that matter to us are the things she provides. Fertility of the soil, fertility of the body. Close-knit families. A safe, warm hearth to return to every evening. Battling darkness, protecting the innocent. And especially the light of the sun. It matters a lot in these lands, where days are likely to be overcast and snowy as anything else. There are even days in winter when the sun's light never quite shines up here in the Rift, so we have to bring it out ourselves — [flags.WC_BALL|as I'm sure you remember from our Festivus celebrations|we have a whole festival for it in midwinter]. "Here's the thing: our gods are gods. They answer prayers. We do things for them, and they do things for us that only they can do. For many peoples around the world, relationships with their gods are just that. You need to make sure your crops grow, so you pray to Lumia. You need success in the hunt, so you pray to Velun. You need talent at the forge, so you pray to Nareva. Like everybody else, we frost elves worship all the gods in their own measure, but Lumia most of all, because she gives us what we most need." [pc.dcb |"Give a little, get a little. I guess it's fair." "It goes beyond just fair," she adds. "There's always more to it. |"[pc.bg acolyte |Just like what the priests told us all back home |That all makes sense ]," you say thoughtfully. "But... it's not just a transaction for [pc.swornGod lumia |the likes of us |[pc.bg acolyte |us |you ] ][pc.bg acolyte |. |, is it ]? People don't care that much about just trading something for something." "You're absolutely right. |"She's really sweet like that." Then you tilt your head slightly and furrow your brow all thinky-like. "But wait a second. [pc.bg acolyte |I remember all the priest classes! We're |You're ] not just trading stuff[pc.bg acolyte |; we |! You ] care about her a lot more than that." "I do," she says, grinning. "You're absolutely right. ] Because our gods aren't just gods. They're people, with all of our good and bad. They incarnate among us, they help us. Sometimes they do things that don't help us so much, but they do care about us. Not to the point of controlling every part of our lives, pampering us, saving us from all harm or difficulty to let us live in a dream world... but ask, and they tend to answer. Whether with their own power or —" the grin gets a little bigger "— by sending people like me to help. "Our people don't just worship Lumia because she answers prayers about what we most need. Nor do we worship her just because our kings and queens tell us to. We worship her because she was there for us: she stood between us all and annihilation. We worship her because she's still there for us. And we worship her because she and our people have grown together. We're for her and she's for us. I don't know if every one of us would call it friendship, but it's something very close to family." She spreads her hands. "Besides, the festivals are fun, the camaraderie is lovely, and the temples feel as warm and welcoming as a family hearth. And, as a warrior, our lady kicks all kinds of butt." [pc.isSoulbound |[pc.swornGod lumia |"[pc.isBimbo |Hee hee. ]I wish I were as good at the pitch as you are[pc.isBimbo |!" |," you laugh. ] She dips her head in acknowledgment, still smiling. "You get better with practice, and I've had a lot of it. Still, like I said, being Lumia's Chosen doesn't mean that praying to other gods is off limits. Our lady helps with a lot, but she's not going to do much if you're fretting about a problem of, say, Narevan craft or Sorran seamanship. And we're very free to attend other gods' festivals, form close relationships with their own people — or their own chosen, even." |You [pc.isBimbo |giggle. "You make being a sun mommy sound like lots of fun! Someone else already has my soul |chuckle. "A persuasive pitch. I'm already spoken for ], though." "Don't worry," she laughs. "Pledging yourself to one god doesn't make the other six off limits — at least as far as prayers go. I've had plenty of fun at festivals of Velun and worshiped at altars of Nareva and Sorra, too, when I've needed them. Your soul is spoken for, but you're not married to [pc.swornGod keros nareva |Keros |Nareva ]." ] |[pc.dcb |You roll your eyes. "Going for the hard sell?" |"You're pretty good at that pitch," you laugh. |"Oooh! You make it sound so fun!" ] She holds up her hands, laughing. "I'm not trying to convert you[annika.kissed | any more than I already have, darling ]. Just trying to answer your question. Although I'd be remiss if I didn't tell you that even swearing your life to Lumia's service, let alone living among us and worshiping as we do, doesn't prevent you from worshiping other gods. She's the first of the Seven in our hearts, not the only one." ] "What about other deities or powers? Outside the Seven?" "It's not, mmm, recommended," she says carefully. "But unless that power is something dark and vicious and demanding violence from its worshipers, like the Khushkan Nightmare or an actual Wraith, we of the Order at least don't take issue with it. We're here to protect people, not convert them, and we've seen enough to know that spearpoint is a poor way to get people to join the faithful." [flags.ARCHWAY_BOTH_SAVED |You decide to pass over the 'actual Wraith' comment. ]"What about the druids and the schism?" At the sounds of those words, Anni grimaces. "That's... complicated. It's also one of the reasons that we're now very agreed that faith cannot be forced. Whatever the elves of centuries ago did to each other, none of us now want to perpetuate the sins of our mothers. It's a long road [party.has etheryn |you've set us on, [etheryn.crowned |Your Majesty |Lady Etheryn ]," she continues, turning to your [etheryn.married |nearby, attentively-listening wife |elven companion ], "but one we are prepared to walk, too." |[etheryn.crowned |Queen |Lady ] Etheryn has set us on, but we're prepared to walk down it with her." ] '

rows.original: "Difficult, but good," Annika says, grinning. "Did you want a longer answer?" You narrow your eyes [pc.isDK |irritab |playful ]ly. "[silly |Let's be real. You were going to give one all along. I'm just waiting for it. |[pc.isBimbo |I meeeean, kinda, yeah! |I was kind of hoping for one, yeah. ] ]" "Okay, okay. Let's see. To start... I don't know if I'll ever fully get over that sense of wonder. The goddess I prayed to as a little girl, the one who sometimes had a comforting whisper that came out of nowhere, whose priestesses were always so welcoming and warm and kind — well, ever since I joined her service, I see her all the time. Her power flows through me when I fly to someone's aid. She's always happy to listen to me unburden my worries, or bounce ideas off of, or even just chat over a warm cup of mulled wine, and sometimes when I do that I just stop and remember just who it is that I'm talking to." The valkyrie smiles wanly at the thought. "She hates it when I do that, because I start treating her like a goddess again." [pc.dcb |"You still do that? You've been [pc.swornGod lumia |one of us |a valkyrie ] for a long time." |[pc.swornGod lumia |"She really does," you chuckle. "Still, someone like me, I mean — I just joined. You've had a long time to teach yourself not to do it. And you still do it anyway?" |"She gets like that with some non-valkyries, too." You grin. "Still, you've had a while to teach yourself not to be like that. Still do it anyway?" ] |"Hee hee. Yeeahhhhh. She really loves just bein' a friendly mama goddess lady. It's tough for me, too! But, like, you've been doing this forever and you still get all 'goddess' with her?" ] "I still do. That said, our gods are living gods, with all the foibles of any other living being. They're amazing, but also, they screw up sometimes. I've seen my lady at her best, and I've also seen her at her not-so-much. And you know? For me, at least, that helps. Lumia's still a goddess, but she's not ineffable. Mostly, she and we just try to do the right thing. That's the job: answer prayers for a good harvest and a safe pregnancy on the easy days, and on the difficult ones, be a light in the darkness and a shield for the innocent. And there are as many difficult days as easy ones." "A hundred years or so has an awful lot of easy days and difficult ones." Anni pretends to count on her fingers. "Let's see, if there are as many of the one as the other, that'd be fifty years of each — which, yes, is a long time to our people, too. There are those who've served Lumia for longer, but not many. I've lived a full life, and one with few regrets. I work hard to do what I do well, and I do it for a good cause alongside sisters I love dearly and who love me just as much. None of which makes it an easy life to live," she concedes, "but we all work hard at that part, too. Sisters are always at each other's side, whether in the ranks facing an onslaught of Wraiths... or kneeling on a battlefield, worrying about whether you really did all you could when a friend passes away. If there's anything I've learned over the last hundred years, it's that the best antidote for worries is the love of your shield-sisters.[pc.swornGod lumia | So, you know: whenever you need us, we'll be there. ]" [pc.swornGod lumia |"Aww, Anni." You grin. "Thanks. I'll let you know." |"Huh. That's pretty sweet." ] She nods, smiles, and spreads her hands. [party.has azyrran |"We're not all that different from Hive Knights, in our way." [azyrran.kdb |At that, the warrior-babe hornet accompanying you starts to disintegrate into a blushy mess. "Wow. Thank you. I... well, I mean, you're all, uh, you, and we're just..." "A brave, skillful Lumian warrior sisterhood?" "Well..." Azzy swallows. "Thanks. Again. Gosh..." "Oh Goddess, you are the most precious thing. [var0|Whatever cutie[var1|s] found you must be very, very happy.|I'm sure you have your pick of cuties, don't you?]"[azyrran.fucked | Anni punctuates that with a grin for Azzy and the same grin — and a knowing wink — for you. ] |Your magnificent dragoon of a hornet-[azyrran.fucked |lover |companion ] grins right back and sketches a rather dashing bow, too. "You're very gracious, Lady Seneschal. What I wouldn't give to see your sisters flying alongside mine [var2|again|sometime]." "I can safely say the same," Anni chuckles. "Both about your martial prowess and your grace." |"Aw, that's so sweet!" Unsolicited — but not, judging from Anni's smile, unwanted — Azyrran rushes up to the valkyrie for a big sticky hug. "This place does remind me so so so much of all my sweet adorable sisters and how brave and friendly and huggable they all are. Just like you[pc.swornGod lumia | and [pc.name] ]!" In exchange, she gets that hug returned. But Anni only uses one arm to hug the hornet. Her other is otherwise occupied... giving the vesparan a little ear-scruffle and a very pleased headpat. "I would love to visit your hive someday, dear," she murmurs. "If your sisters are half as brave and friendly as you are..." "Hee hee hee. You're gonna make me —" Then Azzy gasps and recoils, and with some difficulty extricates herself from the hug. The culprit? The fact that Lumia's seneschal's front is now utterly coated in sticky honey. "Aaaah! I'm sorry. It's okay! It's okay! I can fix it. I have some cleany cloths —" Before she can use them, though, Anni smiles and waves her hand, and every drop of honey magically flows into the air, then right onto Azzy's waiting cloth. "That's okay, sweetheart." "Ooooooh." The hornet stares delightedly at the now-sodden cloth, then turns back to the valkyrie. "That's so cool!" "So are you. You're an absolute angel to give such lovely hugs as that. And you're so responsible, carrying all those wipes just in case." Anni turns to you. "You have a very good girl on your hands, [pc.name]." ] [pc.isDK |Ha. Okay, okay. There's something else on your mind. |You have to smile at that. But there's something else on your mind, too. ] "[pc.isBimbo |Is it okay |Mind ] if I bring up a different valkyrie thing?" |"There it is. Is there anything else about [pc.swornGod lumia |our |the ] Order you'd like to know?" "Actually..." ] "Shoot." [pc.dcb |"You're old as shit," you say bluntly. "But you do a lot of fighting. Are you just incredibly lucky?" |"I'm just kind of amazed that your whole life is fighting, but you've been doing it for so long. Can't manage something like that without being lucky and good, right?" |"I just think it's super cool how long you've been doing valky stuff! Like, it's all fighty and scary and stuff but you've been doing it forever. So, like, you're really good at it. But also you're really lucky too, right?" ] "Watch out for the old woman in a young woman's career, hmm? I've seen some things, picked up a few stories, spent a lot of time training and a lot of time thinking about how fighting works, all of which definitely helps and none of which matters if your number's up. It's always better to be lucky than good. Or to have a goddess on one's side." [pc.dcb |"You've got the last one of those things covered at least," you joke. |"And even better to have all three." You nod sagely. |"Oooh! Haha. That's funny. It's like a joke because you're all three, right? I get it!" You grin and point back and forth between her eyes and yours: you see her! ] "So, a hundred years a valkyrie. Any crazy stories to tell?" "A few, like I said. I guess I wouldn't mind sharing some time; gods know many of [pc.swornGod lumia |our |my ] other sisters have asked me about them. They won't just be war stories, though. They need to be told, of course, but talking about battle inevitably means remembering past pains, the failures, the friends who aren't there anymore..." She pauses then, but you don't interrupt. Instead, you wait for her to finish her thought, and watch as the force of memory tears at her. Finally, Annika sighs, and manages to find her smile again. "But although they mean more to me than the war stories, tales about the women and men who've chosen to become my sisters and what led them to pledge themselves to the Order don't always have the same oomph. Nor do stories of everyday service to the goddess, like blessing a flock of sheep so that twenty become a hundred and twenty in a year's time, or assisting selkies and jotuns — from tribes that aren't in the alliance, or before it was formed — as they deliver their children. And it would be wrong of me to imply that being a valkyrie hasn't meant much war for me. Despite... no, because of the cost, the greater part of our task in this Order is to fight, or to prepare to fight. Not to, say, farm. I still have plenty to say about farming, though, if you want!" You seize on that last bit. "[pc.isBimbo |Farming stories from a big strong warrior sun mommy! That's... that's a teeny bit surprising, but also super cute! |I have to admit, I didn't think I was going to get farming stories from a valkyrie. ]" "Oh, a sister who's been in the Order as long as I have has more than a few. It's hard, messy, dirty work, to be sure, but you know... the idea of sowing seeds and helping them grow into something beautiful is very appealing to me. [annika.numKids 1 |Even if our little angel[annika.numKids 2 |s are | is ] very needy right now, I just look down and see those beautiful eyes and they make the sleepless nights seem completely worth it. Goddess, I know I sound like every other new parent, but it's true. |[annika.pregStage 1 |And now —" Her voice breaks like it always does when you and your baby-to-be come up. "And now we're finally going to be able to do that together. |But mostly I defend crops and the people who tend them; I've never actually planted any of my own. Who knows, though? Maybe someday I'll have the chance to see if I've got a green thumb. ] ]"
rows.translation: 有点难，但还不错，”安妮卡笑着说，“你是不是希望得到一个更长的回答呢？” 你眯起了眼睛。 [pc.isDK |容易恼怒的人 |充满趣味性的 ]ly.[silly |说实话，你本来就打算给的，我只是在等着而已。 |[pc.isBimbo |我是说，算是吧，没错！ |我其实是挺希望有这样的东西的，没错。 ] ]好吧，好吧。让我们想想。首先……我不知道自己是否能够完全摆脱那种惊叹之情。小时候我曾向那位女神祈祷，她有时会突然发出令人感到安慰的低语，她的祭司们总是那么热情、友善且充满关怀——自从我开始侍奉她之后，我就一直能见到她。 rows.raw: ' "Difficult, but good," Annika says, grinning. "Did you want a longer answer?" You narrow your eyes [pc.isDK |irritab |playful ]ly. "[silly |Let's be real. I don't know if I'll ever fully get over that sense of wonder. The goddess I prayed to as a little girl, the one who sometimes had a comforting whisper that came out of nowhere, whose priestesses were always so welcoming and warm and kind — well, ever since I joined her service, I see her all the time. Her power flows through me when I fly to someone's aid. She's always happy to listen to me unburden my worries, or bounce ideas off of, or even just chat over a warm cup of mulled wine, and sometimes when I do that I just stop and remember just who it is that I'm talking to." The valkyrie smiles wanly at the thought. "She hates it when I do that, because I start treating her like a goddess again." [pc.dcb |"You still do that? You've been [pc.swornGod lumia |one of us |a valkyrie ] for a long time." |[pc.swornGod lumia |"She really does," you chuckle. "Still, someone like me, I mean — I just joined. You've had a long time to teach yourself not to do it. And you still do it anyway?" |"She gets like that with some non-valkyries, too." You grin. "Still, you've had a while to teach yourself not to be like that. Still do it anyway?" ] |"Hee hee. Yeeahhhhh. She really loves just bein' a friendly mama goddess lady. It's tough for me, too! But, like, you've been doing this forever and you still get all 'goddess' with her?" ] "I still do. That said, our gods are living gods, with all the foibles of any other living being. They're amazing, but also, they screw up sometimes. I've seen my lady at her best, and I've also seen her at her not-so-much. And you know? For me, at least, that helps. Lumia's still a goddess, but she's not ineffable. Mostly, she and we just try to do the right thing. That's the job: answer prayers for a good harvest and a safe pregnancy on the easy days, and on the difficult ones, be a light in the darkness and a shield for the innocent. And there are as many difficult days as easy ones." "A hundred years or so has an awful lot of easy days and difficult ones." Anni pretends to count on her fingers. "Let's see, if there are as many of the one as the other, that'd be fifty years of each — which, yes, is a long time to our people, too. There are those who've served Lumia for longer, but not many. I've lived a full life, and one with few regrets. I work hard to do what I do well, and I do it for a good cause alongside sisters I love dearly and who love me just as much. None of which makes it an easy life to live," she concedes, "but we all work hard at that part, too. Sisters are always at each other's side, whether in the ranks facing an onslaught of Wraiths... or kneeling on a battlefield, worrying about whether you really did all you could when a friend passes away. If there's anything I've learned over the last hundred years, it's that the best antidote for worries is the love of your shield-sisters.[pc.swornGod lumia | So, you know: whenever you need us, we'll be there. ]" [pc.swornGod lumia |"Aww, Anni." "But although they mean more to me than the war stories, tales about the women and men who've chosen to become my sisters and what led them to pledge themselves to the Order don't always have the same oomph. It's hard, messy, dirty work, to be sure, but you know... the idea of sowing seeds and helping them grow into something beautiful is very appealing to me. [annika.numKids 1 |Even if our little angel[annika.numKids 2 |s are | is ] very needy right now, I just look down and see those beautiful eyes and they make the sleepless nights seem completely worth it. "And now we're finally going to be able to do that together. |But mostly I defend crops and the people who tend them; I've never actually planted any of my own. Who knows, though? rows.original: "Right now?" Annika gestures to her piles of papers. "Managing supply. It's something we've always had to do, but it's also been many decades since so much of the Order was in one place at one time. We're used to supporting multiple spaced-out war camps, not trying to bring everything into the Keep all at once. Now, to be fair, we still have a lot of those camps; the Wraithslaves haven't gone away, just been weakened. And we're looking into setting up places to stay further south to help us fight demons. It's just difficult to make all the preparations for feeding, housing, and commanding several hundred people change overnight[silly |, especially when the most advanced technology I have to do so is the hand-written, hand-delivered letter ]. And the records needed to make it work aren't much fun, either." "I, uh, hadn't really thought about food for the Keep," you admit. "Where does it all come from?" "It depends. Much — close to most — of what we eat here is fish. It's close at hand, there's a lot of it, and we can trade for it with elves, siorcanna, selkies, jotuns, even the avanai. We can also source venison and other hunted meats pretty easily. Cereals are harder, because they have to come from Njorhaalt, but we manage to keep up our stocks by being careful with them. The difference is that now, with more valkyries in the Keep, most of that food runs through me, instead of the sisters in the camps making what deals they need to make to get it." "[pc.isBimbo |The food runs... through you? How does that work? Is it a poop joke?" "Oh dear. No. It means that I'm the person who has to handle getting most of the Order's food, instead of everybody being responsible for it on their own." "Oh. Ohhhh!" You're such a silly goose. "I get it! So, like, do you have enough for everybody still? |Trade's still holding up with the rest of the Rift folk? ]" "Enough for the moment, though it'll be nice if we can have a formal meeting with the Alliance to finally do some horse-trading and defuse tensions. I think they're in the right place to think about making a deal, and goddess knows we are. We'll see where that goes. I hope everybody's — including both ourselves and the realm, not just these Alliance folk — willing to make concessions. But," she says wearily, "right now I'm focusing on food." "So, food's the biggest part of your job here." "That, healing, and weapons. All of us know enough magic to handle ordinary wounds, at least for a while, but it's here at the Keep that we can really take care of serious injuries. And we can work and repair some bronze equipment here, but the city's smiths can handle far more than we ever could alone. Both of those things mostly went through the Keep before, so we're more used to it." Annika sighs. "After those three things, everything else is organization. Who sleeps where. Who has what duties when. Staggering meals so that the kitchens don't get overwhelmed. I'm still not very good at that; the first several shifts were definitely chaos, and every day it feels like there are still some people who miss — or weren't told — of a duty. We haven't been as regimented as most military orders elsewhere, so there's an adjustment period, but ultimately the mistakes have to be on me. I need to organize better. "Sometimes I wonder why..." "Why what?" you ask. She grimaces. "Why Lumia chose me. This is all good and necessary work, but I — I'd have thought I was better suited to battle than administration. I want to be out saving people. Seeing my sisters return to the Keep wounded[annika.kissed | or, goddess forbid, you ]..." [pc.dcb |[annika.kissed |"Hey, don't you dare worry about me. I can handle myself." "Sorry, sweetie, but that's what I do," she murmurs, placing her hand on yours. "I worry about you." |"They're big girls," you grunt. "They can handle themselves." "Won't ever stop me from worrying about them, dear." ] |"No one can protect everybody." You try to say it with as much reassurance as you can muster. "But I could still protect somebody," she says[annika.kissed | fiercely, taking your hand in hers |, frowning ]. "I... I guess we'll see." |"Aw, Anni!" You hug her once again, because of course you do. What better to do under the circumstances? "That's so sweet. I wish I could help you not worry so much about [annika.kissed |me |[pc.swornGod lumia |us |them ] ]." "Mmm. Thank you. This... this helps." ]
rows.translation: 现在吗？”安妮卡指了指自己那一堆堆文件，“管理物资供应啊。这是我们一直以来都必须做的事情，但已经有好几十年没有出现过这样的情况了——曾经有那么多的成员集中在一个地方。我们现在已经习惯了为分散在各个地方的军营提供支援，而不是试图一次性把所有东西都运送到总部来。说实话，现在…… 拥有 那些营地里的很多人；那些被恶魔控制的奴隶并没有消失，只是力量被削弱了。我们正在考虑在更南边的地方建立一些居住点，以便帮助我们对抗恶魔。不过，要为几百人同时解决食物、住所以及指挥管理等问题，确实需要花费大量的时间和精力来进行准备工作。[silly |尤其是当我所能使用的最先进的技术，竟然只是一封手写、亲手送去的信件时。 ]而且，为让这一切运转起来所需的那些记录工作，也并不是一件有趣的事情。” “呃，我其实还没认真考虑过要为这个基地准备食物……这些食物都是从哪里来的呢？” “这要看具体情况。我们在这里吃的东西，有很大一部分——几乎是大部分——都是鱼。 这种资源就在我们身边，数量也非常丰富。我们可以用它来与精灵、西奥卡娜、人鱼、巨魔，甚至阿瓦奈人进行交易。猎获的鹿肉和其他肉类也相当容易获得。不过谷物就比较难搞了，因为它们必须从尼约哈尔特进口，但只要我们谨慎管理库存，还是能够保证有足够的供应的。 不同之处在于，现在由于堡垒里有了更多的女武神，那些食物大多都通过我这个渠道被分发出去，而不是由营地的那些姐妹们去进行各种交易来获取它们了。[pc.isBimbo |食物是直接通过你身体输送到各处的吗？这是怎么运作的？难道这是个关于排泄物的笑话吗？” “哦，天哪。不是的。这意味着我需要负责为整个组织采购大部分食物，而不是让每个人自己来承担这个责任。” “哦……原来如此！那你现在还有足够的食物供应给所有人吗？ |Trade还和Rift的其他人一起坚持着吗？ ]暂时就到这里吧。不过，如果我们能与联盟举行一次正式会议，进行一些谈判并缓解紧张局势，那就再好不过了。我认为他们现在处于一个可以考虑达成协议的合适时机，而我们也确实如此。让我们看看事情会如何发展吧。我希望所有人——包括我们自己以及这个王国，而不仅仅是联盟的那些人——都愿意做出让步。但是，”她疲惫地说道，“目前我首要关心的还是食物问题。 所以，提供食物是你在这里工作的主要职责。” “还有治疗和武器。我们所有人都会一些魔法，至少可以用来处理普通的伤口，但只有在这个要塞里，我们才能真正处理严重的伤势。 我们在这里可以修理一些青铜制设备，但这座城市的铁匠们所能处理的量，远远超过了我们单独所能完成的。之前那些东西大多都是通过那座堡垒来运输的，所以我们已经对此习以为常了。”安妮卡叹了口气说道。 在解决了这三件关键事情之后，剩下的就是安排各项事务了。比如谁该睡在哪里，谁在什么时间应该负责什么工作，以及如何合理安排用餐时间以避免厨房过于忙碌。我在这方面还是不太在行；刚开始工作的那几段时间简直是一片混乱，而且每天似乎都有人会忘记自己的职责，或者根本没有被告知应该做什么。 我们的管理方式并没有像其他地方的军事组织那样严格，因此需要一段时间来适应，但最终，这些失误都应该由我来承担。我需要更好地组织工作。 有时候我会想，为什么……” “为什么什么？”你问道。 她皱了皱眉头：“为什么Lumia会选择我。这些工作固然重要且必要，但我觉得，我更适合参与战斗，而不是从事管理工作。我想要出去…… 保存 人们看到我的姐妹们受伤地回到了城堡。[annika.kissed | 或者，但愿诸神不会允许这种事情发生…… 你 ]..." [pc.dcb |[annika.kissed |嘿，你千万别担心我，我完全有能力照顾好自己。” “对不起，亲爱的，但我就是会担心你，”她轻声说道，然后将手放在你的手上。“我就是会为你担心。 |她们都是大姑娘了，”你嘟囔道，“她们自己能照顾好自己。” “不过，这还是无法阻止我为她们担心啊，亲爱的。 ] |没有人能够保护所有人。”你尽力用最让人安心的语气来说出这句话。 “但我仍然可以尝试去保护…… 一些身体，”她说。[annika.kissed | 紧紧地握住你的手。 |皱着眉头 ]我……我想我们到时候就知道了。 |哎呀，安妮！”你又一次拥抱了她，因为在这样的情况下，你当然会这么做。还有什么比这更合适的呢？“你真是太贴心了。真希望自己能帮你减轻这些担忧…… [annika.kissed |我 |[pc.swornGod lumia |我们 |他们 ] ]嗯，谢谢。这……真的帮了大忙。 ]

rows.original: As soon as you ask the question, you get a frown and a sigh from your valkyrie interlocutor. "We've already been over this, haven't we? I thought that the schism was ending. Why dredge up bad old stories?" [pc.dcb |"Because I want to know more, and because you're the oldest elf I've met so far. Duh." You roll your eyes. "Maybe you didn't live through this shit, but you knew people who did." |"Yes, okay," you admit, "but you lived it — or close to it, anyway. And I'm curious to know more." |"I meeean, I didn't want it to be bad old stories!" [pc.hasEmoteEars |Your ears droop right along with your head |You hang your head slightly ]. "I was just curious! 'Cause, like, you'd know lots of stuff about it, right?" ] "I can understand that, but will it really help the cause of peace?" Anni folds her arms reproachfully. "I may not live in the city anymore, but I've come to terms with the druids' return. Why relive my parents' memories?" [silly |"But the lore!" you plead. "I need to know every little bit so I can make my decision about which elf team is right." "Our people have stopped arguing about that — mostly," she points out. "Why should you?" "Spoilsport. Pleeeeeeease?" |[party.has etheryn |[etheryn.highConfidence |"I've... been reluctant to speak about it, too," Ryn admits, "and for the same reason. I don't want you to feel uncharitable toward the people we're accepting back, [etheryn.fucked |my love |[pc.name] ]." [pc.dcb |"You guys need to get over it. C'mon. It's just history." |You spread your hands. "I get that. But hopefully what happened back then is mostly on the people who were alive back then, though, right? It's all just history." |"It's sweet of you to think of that! But I'm still super curious, and besides," you point out, "it's all just history, right?" ] Ruefully, she says, "Nothing's ever 'just' history. But I see what you mean. I guess it can't hurt, Annika." |Ryn's ears noticeably droop down, too; as ever, she's a little unhappy about any sort of confrontation. "I... I kind of think the same," she says. [pc.dcb |"It's all just history and it's been two hundred years. Sounds like something for you all to get over." |"Hey, even if I'm not going to pick a side or anything, I'd still like to know more about why the Lumians did what they did. Even if the past's past, I guess I'm just curious." |"Aww, poor bean! I promise I'm not tryna get people mad. Like I said, I'm just curious! Is that okay?" ] ] |[pc.dcb |"Look, if you're all afraid to talk about this shit, you're never gonna get over it." You irritably wave your hand. "Just nut up, damn." |You try for a charming smile. "At this point, I'm not trying to interfere, and I doubt anything I learn will make me angry at the druids of today. Besides, it's not going to change the outcome of the peace, either. I get that you're all trying to move past it, but I'm curious about how it all started." |"I don't wanna start a fight or anything! I'll stay... um... what's the word for not taking sides? Neutral! That." ] ] ] "All right," comes the valkyrie's cautious answer. "I suppose that question was for the sake of my own thoughts more than yours. I don't like dwelling on my parents' old tales about the schism, and I don't enjoy how angry they can make me. I'm ready for peace, too. So I'll try not to get too emotional about these things." [pc.dcb |"Yeah, yeah. Just get on with it, already." |"I appreciate that. Like I said, I'll try to keep an open mind." |"Thanks, sweetie! I'll listen like a good [pc.boyGirl], I promise." ] She [pc.isDK |sighs again. "Fine. |nods gratefully. "Okay, then. ] Here we go."
rows.translation: 你一提出这个问题，对方就会皱起眉头，叹一口气：“我们不是已经讨论过这个话题了吗？我本来以为那些旧事已经结束了，为什么还要再翻出来呢？ [pc.dcb |因为我想了解更多，而且你是我目前遇到的最年长的精灵。这还用说。”你翻了个白眼，“也许你没有亲身经历过这些事情，但你肯定认识经历过的人。 |是的，好吧，”你承认道，“但你确实经历过那些事情——或者至少非常接近那些经历。我真的很想了解更多。 |我的意思是，我并不想让这些故事变得老套无聊！ [pc.hasEmoteEars |你的耳朵会跟着头部一起耷拉下来。 |你微微低下了头。 ]我只是好奇而已！因为你知道的关于这个的事情肯定很多，对吧？ ] 我能够理解你的感受，但这样做真的有助于促进和平事业吗？”安妮责备地双臂交叉说道，“虽然我不再住在城里了，但我已经接受了德鲁伊们回归的事实。为什么还要去重温我父母那些痛苦的记忆呢？ [silly |但是那些背景故事啊！”你恳求道，“我必须了解每一个细节，这样才能决定该支持哪支精灵队伍。” “我们族人已经不再争论这些了——至少大部分人都不再争论了，”她指出，“你为什么还要争论呢？” “太破坏气氛了……求求你吧？ |[party.has etheryn |[etheryn.highConfidence |我也……一直不太愿意谈论这个话题，”莱恩承认道，“原因也是一样的。我不想让你对我们决定接纳回来的人产生负面看法。 [etheryn.fucked |我的爱人 |[pc.name] ]." [pc.dcb |你们大家都该放下这件事了。拜托，那只是过去的事罢了。 |你摊开双手说道：“我明白。不过，希望当时发生的事情主要应该由那些当时在场的人来承担责任，对吧？这一切都只是历史罢了。 |你能想到这一点，真是太贴心了！不过我还是很好奇，而且，”你接着说道，“这一切都只是过去的事情罢了，对吧？ ] 她懊悔地说道：“没有什么事情仅仅是‘历史’而已。不过我明白你的意思了。我想，尝试一下也没坏处，安妮卡。 |瑞恩的耳朵也明显耷拉了下来；像往常一样，她对于任何形式的冲突都显得有些不高兴。“我……我也觉得差不多是这样，”她说。 [pc.dcb |这一切都已经成为历史了，而且已经过去两百年了。这件事应该很容易让你们都释怀吧。 |嘿，虽然我并不打算站在任何一方，但我还是想了解更多关于卢米安人为什么会做出那样的选择。虽然过去的事情已经过去了，但我就是觉得好奇而已。 |哎呀，可怜的豆豆！我保证我不是想惹大家生气的。就像我说的，我只是好奇而已！这样可以吗？ ] ] |[pc.dcb |听着，如果你们都不敢谈论这种事情，那就永远无法克服它。”你恼怒地挥了挥手，“有种就勇敢面对吧，该死的。 |你努力露出一丝迷人的微笑，说道：“在这个时候，我并不打算干涉，而且我也怀疑，无论我了解到什么，都不会让我对那些德鲁伊产生愤怒。 今天此外，这也不会改变和平进程的结果。我明白你们都在努力克服这些困难，但我很好奇这一切究竟是如何开始的。 |我并不是想惹麻烦或者打架什么的！我只是想保持中立……嗯，该怎么说呢？就是不偏袒任何一方，保持中立立场而已。 ] ] ] 好吧，”女武神谨慎地回答道，“我想那个问题更多的是为了让我自己思考，而不是为了满足你的好奇心。我不想一直回想父母们关于那场分裂的旧事，也不想因为他们的话而感到愤怒。我也渴望和平，所以我会努力不要让这些事情影响到我的情绪。 [pc.dcb |是啊，是啊。赶紧开始吧。 |我很感激。就像我说的，我会尽量保持开放的心态。 |谢谢，亲爱的！我会认真听的。 [pc.boyGirl]我保证。 ] 她 [pc.isDK |又叹了口气。“好吧。 |他感激地点了点头。“好吧，那就这样吧。 ] 我们开始吧。

That." ] ] ] "All right," comes the valkyrie's cautious answer. "I suppose that question was for the sake of my own thoughts more than yours. I don't like dwelling on my parents' old tales about the schism, and I don't enjoy how angry they can make me. I'm ready for peace, too. So I'll try not to get too emotional about these things." [pc.dcb |"Yeah, yeah. Just get on with it, already." |"I appreciate that. Like I said, I'll try to keep an open mind." |"Thanks, sweetie! I'll listen like a good [pc.boyGirl], I promise." ] She [pc.isDK |sighs again. "Fine. |nods gratefully. "Okay, then. ] Here we go." '

rows.original: "Remember how I told you about sacrifice and worship, trading something for something?" Anni asks. "For some people, it's more than that, but it doesn't have to be. I mean, Lumia would prefer that we be kind, Keros that we be interesting, Nareva that we be clever, and so on, but they don't force that on us, and they don't force us to love them. What the gods do demand in exchange for their blessings is sacrifice and ritual. The act of worship or of service, the trade of something for something. This is what most other powers, natural or otherwise, Wyld and spirits and minor gods, have asked since the beginning of time. [silly |Do ut des: y |Y ]ou give, so that they might give. You pray and your prayers are answered. And the reason the Seven are so popular and so loved is because they answer those prayers. "People, places, even things that are beloved of the gods sometimes get more than that, of course. The people of Sartanni have always been in tune with wildlife and nature more than most places, and so Velun holds them very dear. And because they're so close to his ideal, because of his love for them, he helps them ensure that their land is so unusually lush, wild, and beautiful. The gods are living gods, and they care for us, and that care has a real meaning. But even if you turn against them or what they stand for, it's almost impossible to lose the ability to draw on their power at all. They will answer prayers offered in the appropriate way by nearly anyone, even the truly despicable. Even the gods tend to live by rules." "Okay." You frown. "[pc.isBimbo |Okay, I get the god stuff, kinda. Trades are fun! Especially sexy trades. But what does this have to do with sun mommy and droopy-druid stuff? |[pc.isCunning |Applied deiology is |Definitions of god stuff makes for ] a bit of a left turn from the schism... ]" She holds up a hand. "Not as much as you'd think. The point is that the gods don't demand belief, let alone love. They will still be there tomorrow if you don't like them today. They asked only for our worship when they incarnated in the Godswar, not our love, and that's what they still ask now. So when Lumia appeared to the good people of Njorhaalt — to my parents and thousands of others — and saved them from the abyss, that's what was at stake. Sacrifice and worship to her, in exchange for which she would empower our people to save the world, for themselves and for their children. Like I said, something for something. She didn't demand love, only worship. And almost everybody in the city was willing to make that trade wholeheartedly." "[pc.dcb |Almost doesn't quite cut the mustard. |That 'almost' ended up causing a lot of problems, though. |Uh oh! 'Almost' isn't good. ]" "[pc.isDK |No |That's right ]. Before the war, the druids ruled, and the people worshiped the Wyld through them. Communing with the Old Wyld was simply what everybody did. But when some found the spirits of the jotuns, or the dragons, or the gods of the southerners more to their liking, the druids... reacted badly. Those executions helped bring the Empire's wrath on the old elven realm. The druids lost that war — not so badly as to lose great cities or become a protectorate, but badly enough for them to have to promise toleration of other faiths, and that made them seethe with rage. They seethed all the more when the Second Princess went to Belhar to marry a southerner and came back with a Lumian spouse on her arm and a love of the Dawn Maiden in her heart. I know that the same story becomes treason against the true ideals of one's people in different hands, but who gets to choose what those are? And whom did those ideals actually help? "When the druids' Wyld-granted powers were shown to be for naught during the Wraith invasion, they[var0 | didn't know to blame the blight. Instead they ] blamed worshipers of the Seven for not sacrificing to the Old Wyld. While the queen was away trying to hold back the Void, while our people died in droves, while our realm collapsed around our ears, the druids launched a fresh round of persecutions and executions in the Winter City. And this time, there was no imperial army free to march north and rescue the faithful." She grimaces. "As it turned out, the prayers of those who were executed for worshiping the wrong gods ended up doing more good for our people than every offering given to the trees." "[pc.dcb |So in this telling, the druids were just worried about losing their gravy train. |So according to Lumian elves, the druids were just powerful and afraid of losing that power? |That kinda makes it sound like the sun mommy elves think the druids were just being stinky and holding onto power. ]" "No. Not just. That's unfair." Deep pain contorts Annika's face. "Remember what I told you before? Even if the gods don't demand an emotional connection, we make one all the same. That's what people do. That was true of Wyld-worshiping druids as much as it is of those of us who now follow the Seven. For them, that was what being an elf was. And that's lovely, and romantic, but it had horrifying consequences for everybody who didn't follow their gods any longer. Never mind that, as far as I know, Lumia never sought to wipe out the Wyld spirits or their worship; she was simply offering power for worship and primacy. Cutting the druids out completely would have been — was — a disaster. There was still a war to win, and it served no one's interests, least of all our goddess's, to split our people when annihilation still threatened us all."
rows.translation: 还记得我跟你讲过关于牺牲与崇拜的事情吗？用某样东西去换取另一样东西？”安妮问道，“对有些人来说，这不仅仅是一种交易，但也不一定非得如此。我的意思是，卢米娅希望我们善良，凯罗斯希望我们有趣，纳雷瓦希望我们聪明，等等，但他们并不会强迫我们这样做，也不会强迫我们去爱他们。而神明们要求我们为获得他们的祝福而付出的，只是牺牲与仪式而已。 行动 无论是用于崇拜还是服务，亦或是用一种东西换取另一种东西。从古至今，大多数其他的力量——无论是自然的还是其他形式的，无论是野兽、精灵还是低等神明——所追求的也都是这一点。 [silly |以德报德：y |Y ]你给予，这样他们才能给予你。你祈祷，而你的祈祷也会得到回应。七神之所以如此受欢迎、如此受人喜爱，正是因为他们能够回应这些祈祷。 “当然，那些受到神明眷顾的人们、地方，甚至物品，有时也会得到更多的恩赐。 萨塔尼的人们一直以来都比其他地方的人更与野生动物和大自然保持着和谐的关系，因此维伦非常珍视他们。正因为他们如此符合他的理想，也正因为他对他们的喜爱，他才会帮助他们保护自己的土地，让这片土地保持如此茂盛、原始且美丽的状态。 这些神明是真实存在的，他们关心着我们，而这种关怀是真实而有力的。但即便你与他们或他们所代表的理念背道而驰，你也几乎不可能失去利用他们力量的能力。 一点也不几乎任何人，哪怕是那些真正卑鄙的人，他们所献上的祈祷都会得到相应的回应。就连神明们，也往往遵循着一定的规则行事。” “好吧。”你皱了皱眉头。[pc.isBimbo |好吧，我大概明白那些关于神灵的事情了。交易确实很有趣！尤其是那些有趣的交易。但这一切和“太阳妈妈”以及“那个软弱的德鲁伊”有什么关系呢？ |[pc.isCunning |应用神学就是 |对于那些堪称“神级”的东西的定义，往往会…… ] 这与最初的分歧方向有些不同…… ]她举起一只手：“并没有你想象中的那么重要。关键在于，神明并不要求人们相信他们，更不需要人们爱他们。即使你今天不喜欢他们，明天他们依然会在那里。当他们在‘神战’中降临人世时，他们只要求人们崇拜他们，而不是爱他们，而现在他们依然只要求这一点。 所以，当卢米娅出现在尼奥哈尔特的善良人们面前——出现在我的父母以及成千上万人面前——并将他们从深渊中拯救出来时，这一切其实就是一场关乎生死与信仰的抉择。人们向她献上牺牲与崇拜，作为交换，她便会赋予我们的人民力量，让他们能够为自己和自己的后代拯救这个世界。 正如我所说，凡事都要有所交换。她并不要求爱情，只要求崇拜。而这座城市里的几乎所有人，都愿意全心全意地接受这种交换。[pc.dcb |差不多还算凑合吧。 |不过，那个“几乎”最终还是引发了很多问题。 |哦不！“差不多”这个说法可不行。 ]" "[pc.isDK |不行。 |没错。 ]在战争之前，德鲁伊们掌权，人们通过他们来崇拜大自然。与古老的自然力量交流，是每个人都会做的事情。但当有些人发现，与侏儒、巨龙或是南方人的神灵交流更合他们的心意时，德鲁伊们………反应非常激烈。那些处决行为使得帝国对古老的精灵王国发起了猛烈的报复。德鲁伊们在这场战争中失败了——虽然没有失去重要的城市，也没有沦为附庸国，但失败的结果是他们不得不承诺容忍其他信仰的存在。 那个 这让他们怒火中烧。而当二公主前往贝尔哈尔与一位南方人结婚，归来时不仅带着一位卢米安人作为配偶，心中也怀揣着对“黎明少女”的爱意时，他们的愤怒更是达到了顶点。我知道，同样的事情在不同的手中，可能会被视为对一个民族真正理想的背叛，但究竟谁有权利来定义这些理想是什么呢？而这些理想，又真正帮助过谁呢？ “当德鲁伊们所拥有的、由自然之力赋予的力量在‘幽灵入侵’中被证明毫无用处时，他们……[var0 | 根本不知道该把责任归咎于那种灾祸。相反，他们…… ] 他们指责那些崇拜七神的人没有向旧荒野献祭。当女王远赴他乡试图阻止虚无的侵袭时，当我们的同胞成群结队地死去时，当我们的王国在转眼间分崩离析时，德鲁伊们却在冬城再次发动了迫害和处决行动。 而这一次，再也没有帝国军队可以北上去拯救那些忠诚的子民了。”她苦涩地说道，“事实上，那些因为崇拜错误的神明而被处决的人们的祈祷，反而为我们的人民带来了比所有献给那些神树的祭品还要多的好处。" "[pc.dcb |在这个故事中，德鲁伊们只是担心会失去他们现有的利益来源罢了。 |所以根据卢米安精灵的说法，德鲁伊们只是因为拥有强大的力量而害怕失去这种力量而已？ |这样听起来，好像那些太阳之母精灵认为德鲁伊们只是贪图权力、不愿放弃自己的地位罢了。 ]不。不仅仅是这样。那样太不公平了。”安妮卡的脸上浮现出痛苦的表情。“还记得我之前跟你说过的话吗？即使神明并不要求我们建立情感上的联系，我们还是会主动去建立这样的联系。人类就是这样的。 对于那些崇拜荒野之神的德鲁伊来说，这一点同样适用；对于我们这些如今追随七神的人来说，也是如此。对他们而言，这就是身为精灵的意义所在。这种信仰确实美好而浪漫，但对于那些不再信仰他们的神明的人来说，却会带来可怕的后果。 不过，据我所知，Lumia从未试图消灭那些野性精灵或他们对这些精灵的崇拜；她只是提供力量，让人们能够进行崇拜并确立某种主导地位。如果彻底消灭德鲁伊，那将会是一场灾难。 我们仍然有一场战争需要打赢，而在这种灭顶之灾仍然威胁着我们所有人的时候，分裂我们的人民对任何人都没有好处，尤其是对我们的女神来说更是如此。

rows.translation: 下一步

rows.original: "So how did the split happen?" Anni sighs. "I can't give you a blow-by-blow account. I know many druids refused to cooperate; the same die-hards that had sun-worshipers executed insisted that they would abandon us all to the devouring Void before letting our children worship Lumia or any other of the Seven. I know the queen, campaigning far and wide against the Wraiths and their monsters alongside allies from north and south, returned home to find a city divided against itself, with the archdruid leading his faithful and even some of her own family in refusing to lend arms to the war, let alone sacrifice to Lumia. I know that there were riots. I know that my parents and many ordinary people felt betrayed by the druids who still fruitlessly tried to sacrifice to the Old Wyld, throwing the wealth of our people down a rat hole instead of offering a single prayer to Lumia, no matter how they felt about her. And I know that the blood of the martyrs was still fresh in Lumians' minds. "Eventually, as far as the queen and most of our people were concerned, Lumia worship became a mark of loyalty. It didn't start out that way, but..." She shrugs her shoulders helplessly. [pc.dcb |"Huh. And what else did the Lumians say about the druids? According to them, were all the druids all '[silly |liever Turks dan Paaps |better death for all than salvation for some ]'?" |"If those are the Lumian stories about druids, they certainly do paint the druids in a bad light." As promised, you try to withhold judgment on one side or the other. "But surely not every Wyld-worshiper was a hardliner." |"But, like, there's no way every druid was all mean and threaty and stuff!" ] "Maybe. I wasn't there, but there are always moderates. But as the arguments got worse and the hardliners got more heated and riots started to spread, the people who tried to just make things work for everybody can't have had many options. At any rate, what I do know is that the whole thing wasn't an ultimatum from Lumia, followed immediately by schism. People tried to find compromises, and it took months before it became clear that people couldn't find a way to make those compromises actually hold." [flags.LUMIA_TALK_REPUTATION |"She blames herself, not the elves." Anni sighs before answering. "She would, wouldn't she? The gods make mistakes, just like everybody else, but unless she was planning to make everybody in the Winter City accept everybody else at swordpoint, I don't see how she'd have prevented it. And there's a reason the gods don't do that. No, this is our fault. We did it to ourselves. All the compromises fell apart because of us, druid and Lumian, not her." "And what happened when everybody figured that out?" |"And once everybody realized that they wouldn't work?" ] "The druids left. As angry as we had all become at each other, as much rioting had happened in the streets, there was still a war with the Wraiths. The fate of life itself was at stake. No one could afford an actual conflict. One of the few things that the queen and the archdruid could agree on was that the two sides needed to be separated. So the druids — a part of the old religious aristocracy, their retainers, and those few common folk who couldn't bring themselves to worship a different goddess — took their skills and their things and returned to the forest[var0| and, as you've discovered, watched their holy places succumb to the fungus before retreating into even deeper woods]. We divided the Frostwood among us, and after the war that division held... not without a lot of friction, but we weren't about to start killing them and I hope to Lumia they didn't want to kill us either. Tense moments, skirmishes, wounds, but no inquisition. This Order crusades against Wraiths and their slaves. We're not here to convert or kill druids, and neither was the royal guard." [pc.dcb |"If you say so," you say diffidently. "So now that they're all coming back? No problems with the whole 'no conversions' thing that the palace has decided on?" |"What about now that they're coming back? Ryn and El aren't demanding Lumia worship as the price of peace anymore." |"That's good! Not so many frowny faces and all that. There are better ways to solve these things! Sexier ways, too." And after imagining some of those sexy ways to solve problems, you manage to get back on track: "Sooo, like, Ryn-Ryn[party.has etheryn | here i |' ]s okay with not making the druids worship Lumia. What about you?" ] "Yes, I agree with that choice, like I said before." There's no hesitation in her voice. "Those were our parents' problems. In my case, my actual parents. [silly |There's a song about this: i |I ]t's not our fault that the world is the way it is, but it is our fault if bad things stay bad. I won't lie: it's not easy to let bygones be bygones. After all, some of these scars —" she runs her fingers down one arm "— come from druids. But the ones who are alive now have said that they want to come back to us, and [var0|now that they've started figuring out how to make that work|if that's the case] I know I'll try to meet them halfway. The hard part is the [silly |bits and pieces, and all the pieces |details, and the details ] matter. But I think we can solve them." [flags.WC_BALL |[pc.isDK | |"At least there are the beginnings of some new, better memories," you offer. "Good times can help make trust easier, too. The Midwinter Ball[pc.isBimbo | was tons of fun! |... ]" "I wish I'd been able to attend," comes Anni's warm reply. "Because you're right. Watching children play together regardless of whom they worship, listening to our music, sharing some fish, doing the dance around the tree — that would've gone a long way. Next year, though. Next year for sure." [pc.isCunning |Although you don't say it out loud, you notice that she didn't add in anything about 'if it holds.' Maybe she thinks that this peace really [pc.isBimbo |could work! |does have legs. ] ] ] ]
rows.translation: 那么，这种分裂究竟是如何发生的呢？” 安妮叹了口气：“我无法详细地告诉你整个过程。我知道有很多德鲁伊拒绝合作；那些曾经坚持处决崇拜太阳神的人，也坚决表示，除非我们的孩子们开始崇拜卢米娅或七神中的其他神明，否则他们就会让我们所有人陷入那吞噬一切的虚无之中。 我知道，那位女王曾与来自南北方的盟友一起，四处奔走，共同对抗那些幽灵及其怪物。然而当她回到家乡时，却发现整座城市已经分裂成对立的两派。那位大德鲁伊带领着他的追随者，甚至包括她自己的一些家人，拒绝为这场战争提供支持，更不愿向卢米娅献祭。 我知道当时发生了暴动。我也知道，我的父母以及许多普通人都觉得那些德鲁伊背叛了他们——那些德鲁伊仍然徒劳地试图向古老的荒野献祭，将我们民族的财富浪费在无用的事情上，却从未向卢米娅祈祷过，无论他们对她怀有怎样的感情。 我知道，对于卢米亚人来说，那些烈士的鲜血至今仍历历在目。 “最终，对女王以及我们的大多数人民而言，崇拜卢米亚神明已经成为一种忠诚的象征。虽然一开始并非如此，但事实就是如此。……”她无奈地耸了耸肩。 [pc.dcb |嗯。那么卢米安人还说了些什么关于德鲁伊们的呢？据他们所说，是怎样的呢？ 所有 所有的德鲁伊们……[silly |宁愿选择土耳其人也不愿选择荷兰人 |对所有人来说，死总比只有部分人得救要好。 ]'?" |如果这些确实是关于德鲁伊的卢米安传说，那么它们确实把德鲁伊描绘成了负面的形象。”正如你承诺的那样，你努力不对任何一方妄下论断。“但想必，并非所有的崇拜自然之力的人都是强硬派吧。 |但是，真的，这根本不可能。 每个 那些德鲁伊全都凶神恶煞的，满口威胁之词，真是让人害怕！ ] 也许吧。我当时并不在场，但总会有那些试图调和各方矛盾的人。然而，随着争论愈演愈烈，强硬派的态度也变得越来越激烈，骚乱开始蔓延，那些试图让所有人都能达成共识的人肯定没有太多选择。无论如何，我可以肯定的是，整个事件并不是Lumia方面发出了最后通牒，然后各方立刻分道扬镳的。 人们 人们尝试寻找折中的办法，但过了好几个月，才终于明白： 人们 找不到任何办法让这些妥协真正得到落实。 [flags.LUMIA_TALK_REPUTATION |她责怪的是自己，而不是那些精灵。” 安妮叹了口气，然后回答道：“她肯定会这么做的，不是吗？神明也会犯错，和其他人一样。但除非她打算用武力强迫整个冬之城的人都接受这一切，否则我实在想不出她还能怎样阻止这件事的发生。而且，神明们这么做肯定也有他们的原因…… 别那么做。不，这是我们的错。是我们自己造成的。所有的妥协方案都因为我们而失败了，是德鲁伊和卢米安，而不是她。” “那么，当大家都明白这一点的时候，发生了什么呢？ |而当所有人都意识到这些方法根本行不通的时候？ ] 德鲁伊们离开了。尽管我们彼此之间充满了愤怒，街道上也发生了许多骚乱，但与幽灵们的战争依然在进行中。生命的命运正处于危险之中，没有人能够承受真正的冲突。 女王与大德鲁伊为数不多的共识之一，就是必须将双方分开。于是，这些德鲁伊——作为古老宗教贵族的一部分，以及他们的追随者，还有那些实在无法接受崇拜其他女神的普通民众——带着自己的技艺和财产，回到了森林中。[var0| 正如你们所看到的，那些生物眼睁睁看着自己的圣地被真菌侵蚀，随后便退入了更加幽深的森林之中。]我们把弗罗斯特伍德分成了几块，战争结束后，这种划分依然有效……虽然其间发生过不少摩擦，但我们并没有打算互相杀戮；我也希望卢米亚他们也不会想要杀死我们。有过紧张的时刻，也有过小规模的冲突，有人受了伤，但并没有有人被处决。我们这个组织是为了对抗幽灵及其奴仆而存在的，我们的目的并不是去转化或消灭德鲁伊，皇家卫队也是如此。 [pc.dcb |如果你这么说的话……”你有些迟疑地回答，“那么现在他们都要回来了吗？宫廷制定的‘不允许转换’的政策，现在也没有什么问题了吧？ |那么现在他们回来了，情况又会怎样呢？Ryn和El不再要求以崇拜Lumia作为换取和平的条件了。 |太好了！这样就不用再有那么多愁眉苦脸的表情了。其实有很多更好的方法来解决这些问题，而且这些方法还更加……有趣呢。”在想象了一些这些有趣的方法之后，你终于重新回到了正轨上：“所以，比如说，Ryn-Ryn……[party.has etheryn | 我在这里。 |' ]我并不介意不让德鲁伊们崇拜卢米娅。你呢？ ] 是的，我同意那个选择，就像我之前说的那样。”她的声音里没有丝毫犹豫，“那些都是我们父母的问题。就我而言，指的是我的亲生父母。 [silly |有一首歌是关于这个的：i |我 ]世界变成如今这个样子，这不是我们的错，但…… 是 如果坏事依然持续下去，那肯定是我们的错。说实话，让过去的事情成为过去并不容易。毕竟，这些伤痕中有些——”她用手指轻轻触摸着自己的手臂——“确实是由德鲁伊造成的。但是那些现在还活着的人表示，他们想要回到我们身边来。 [var0|现在他们已经开始研究如何让这个方案得以实施了。|如果是那样的话……] 我知道我会尝试与他们达成妥协。真正困难的部分在于…… [silly |零零碎碎，所有的那些碎片 |细节，以及那些细节。 ] 当然，这些问题确实存在。但我觉得我们能够解决它们。 [flags.WC_BALL |[pc.isDK | |至少，一些新的、更美好的回忆已经开始了，”你说道，“美好的时光也有助于增进信任。冬日舞会……[pc.isBimbo | 太有趣了！ |... ]真希望自己当时能参加，”安妮温暖地回答道，“因为你说得对。看着孩子们不分彼此地一起玩耍，一起聆听我们的音乐，一起分享食物，一起围着树跳舞——这些真的意义非凡。不过，明年吧。明年肯定能参加。 [pc.isCunning |虽然你没有把这句话说出来，但你注意到她并没有提到“如果这种情况持续下去会怎样”这种可能性。也许她认为，这种平静真的会持续下去。 [pc.isBimbo |这个办法可行！ |确实有可行性。 ] ] ] ]
rows.raw: ' "So how did the split happen?" Anni sighs. "I can't give you a blow-by-blow account. I know many druids refused to cooperate; the same die-hards that had sun-worshipers executed insisted that they would abandon us all to the devouring Void before letting our children worship Lumia or any other of the Seven. I know the queen, campaigning far and wide against the Wraiths and their monsters alongside allies from north and south, returned home to find a city divided against itself, with the archdruid leading his faithful and even some of her own family in refusing to lend arms to the war, let alone sacrifice to Lumia. I know that there were riots. I know that my parents and many ordinary people felt betrayed by the druids who still fruitlessly tried to sacrifice to the Old Wyld, throwing the wealth of our people down a rat hole instead of offering a single prayer to Lumia, no matter how they felt about her. And I know that the blood of the martyrs was still fresh in Lumians' minds. "Eventually, as far as the queen and most of our people were concerned, Lumia worship became a mark of loyalty. It didn't start out that way, but..." She shrugs her shoulders helplessly. [pc.dcb |"Huh. And what else did the Lumians say about the druids? According to them, were all the druids all '[silly |liever Turks dan Paaps |better death for all than salvation for some ]'?" |"If those are the Lumian stories about druids, they certainly do paint the druids in a bad light." As promised, you try to withhold judgment on one side or the other. "But surely not every Wyld-worshiper was a hardliner." |"But, like, there's no way every druid was all mean and threaty and stuff!" ] "Maybe. I wasn't there, but there are always moderates. But as the arguments got worse and the hardliners got more heated and riots started to spread, the people who tried to just make things work for everybody can't have had many options. At any rate, what I do know is that the whole thing wasn't an ultimatum from Lumia, followed immediately by schism. People tried to find compromises, and it took months before it became clear that people couldn't find a way to make those compromises actually hold." [flags.LUMIA_TALK_REPUTATION |"She blames herself, not the elves." Anni sighs before answering. "She would, wouldn't she? The gods make mistakes, just like everybody else, but unless she was planning to make everybody in the Winter City accept everybody else at swordpoint, I don't see how she'd have prevented it. And there's a reason the gods don't do that. No, this is our fault. We did it to ourselves. All the compromises fell apart because of us, druid and Lumian, not her." "And what happened when everybody figured that out?" |"And once everybody realized that they wouldn't work?" ] "The druids left. As angry as we had all become at each other, as much rioting had happened in the streets, there was still a war with the Wraiths. The fate of life itself was at stake. No one could afford an actual conflict. One of the few things that the queen and the archdruid could agree on was that the two sides needed to be separated. So the druids — a part of the old religious aristocracy, their retainers, and those few common folk who couldn't bring themselves to worship a different goddess — took their skills and their things and returned to the forest[var0| and, as you've discovered, watched their holy places succumb to the fungus before retreating into even deeper woods]. We divided the Frostwood among us, and after the war that division held... not without a lot of friction, but we weren't about to start killing them and I hope to Lumia they didn't want to kill us either. Tense moments, skirmishes, wounds, but no inquisition. This Order crusades against Wraiths and their slaves. We're not here to convert or kill druids, and neither was the royal guard." [pc.dcb |"If you say so," you say diffidently. "So now that they're all coming back? No problems with the whole 'no conversions' thing that the palace has decided on?" |"What about now that they're coming back? Ryn and El aren't demanding Lumia worship as the price of peace anymore." |"That's good! Not so many frowny faces and all that. There are better ways to solve these things! Sexier ways, too." And after imagining some of those sexy ways to solve problems, you manage to get back on track: "Sooo, like, Ryn-Ryn[party.has etheryn | here i |' ]s okay with not making the druids worship Lumia. What about you?" ] "Yes, I agree with that choice, like I said before." There's no hesitation in her voice. "Those were our parents' problems. In my case, my actual parents. [silly |There's a song about this: i |I ]t's not our fault that the world is the way it is, but it is our fault if bad things stay bad. I won't lie: it's not easy to let bygones be bygones. After all, some of these scars —" she runs her fingers down one arm "— come from druids. But the ones who are alive now have said that they want to come back to us, and [var0|now that they've started figuring out how to make that work|if that's the case] I know I'll try to meet them halfway. The hard part is the [silly |bits and pieces, and all the pieces |details, and the details ] matter. But I think we can solve them." [flags.WC_BALL |[pc.isDK | |"At least there are the beginnings of some new, better memories," you offer. "Good times can help make trust easier, too. The Midwinter Ball[pc.isBimbo | was tons of fun! |... ]" "I wish I'd been able to attend," comes Anni's warm reply. "Because you're right. Watching children play together regardless of whom they worship, listening to our music, sharing some fish, doing the dance around the tree — that would've gone a long way. Next year, though. Next year for sure." [pc.isCunning |Although you don't say it out loud, you notice that she didn't add in anything about 'if it holds.' Maybe she thinks that this peace really [pc.isBimbo |could work! |does have legs. ] ] ] ] '

rows.original: "Ah. Yes." Annika's lips purse. "I knew your grandmother; I like to think I knew her very well. She was there when I took my vows to the Dawn Maiden." Etheryn closes her eyes in some pain. "I... I don't know if word has reached up here, but..." Word of your journey into the crypt, presumably — and of discovering the ghosts of both of Ryn's grandmothers, not laid to rest until you, Elthara, and Hethia helped Ryn [var0|reconcile|banish] them. You hold your tongue, though[pc.isDK |; this is their shit to sort out |, only willing to share what Ryn is ]. "It has," says the valkyrie; El must have let the Keep know. Hesitantly, she reaches out for Ryn's shoulder. "Are you — ?" Instead of answering, the other woman looks down at the ground, then sighs before meeting Annika's gaze again. "C[etheryn.lowConfidence |-c ]ould you tell me what she was like when you knew her?" "I can." She takes a deep breath. "When I was in the guard, the queen did more than just learn my name. She didn't just spend time with the other valkyries, even though she led both the Order and the realm. She had time for servants, guards; she especially had time for her daughter, whom she loved more than life itself. Maybe she wasn't the kind of person who would hug you and tell you everything would be all right, nor was she the kind to throw her warriors a party and liven things up with us. But she was the kind who would ask after you and your family, and to remember everything you said about them and follow up later. She was the kind to tell you when you'd done well, to not be too harsh with you over little mistakes and failures — and to spend time helping you figure out the right way to do things. She was a bluff, big-hearted amazon who could inspire you to be the best you that you could be. And she was the greatest warrior I'd ever seen." [pc.dcb |Your voice goes a little sour and exasperated — well, more so than usual. "Sounds like hero worship." |"You wanted to be like her, too," you say quietly. |"Awww, that's kind of cute! You had a hero to look up to." ] Anni[pc.isDK | doesn't take it as a jab, though; instead she ] smiles at the memory: "She figured it out just as quickly as you did. We had a lot of long conversations about what it meant to be a sister in the Order. Eventually, she helped guide me through the things I needed to do to take my vows, and after that, I was by her side for most of the rest of her reign. In battle, she always loved to attack from the sky with the sun at her back to blind our foes; that way, Lumia would be on our side in more ways than one. But she wasn't afraid to get on the ground, stand in formation, and hold the line with spear and shield, shouting encouragement to those around her. We'd have followed her into hell... and actually did, more than once." Ryn's sapphire eyes are wide and a little shimmery. "Did she ever talk about the schism?" "One of the only times I ever saw her angry was before I took my vows; my patrol had just come back from the Frostwood, and we'd been in a skirmish with the druids. It was my fault. We were chasing a drider and didn't pay attention to where we were going, ended up running her right into a druid encampment. They were... not happy to see any of us." She sighs. "We got away with injuries, but no dead. Same for them. When we got back to the city, the queen made sure my warriors were receiving proper healing, then chewed into me for several minutes about breaking the truce and getting both my subordinates and the druids hurt. 'They' were still 'us', after all. And she did harbor hopes of them converting and rejoining the rest of our people — as a small trickle did from time to time, especially in those early years." [pc.dcb |"And this," you say skeptically, "is the same angry ghost we met in the palace?" |You can't keep a little skepticism out of your voice. "That doesn't sound like the ghost from the crypt." |"Wow. She sounds kind of nice. You know, in a teensy bit scary but also super cool and kind of sexy kind of way." You pause. "That's... that's not the way she was when we met her." ] She spreads her hands. "It wasn't a side of herself that she showed everybody, but she spent a great deal of time alone and in mourning. When I was still in the guard, I saw her rise every morning before the sun came up to be alone in the palace crypt; when she came out, the skin around her eyes was always soft and puffy from shedding tears. Even in public, she'd talk about how bringing the light of the Sun to our people and saving us all was her proudest moment, but the schism was her greatest failure. I didn't know that her spirit had stayed behind after she passed, but after what happened with her consort, I can understand why she might've thought she had unfinished business." [var0 |"They remembered their love eventually." Ryn's voice quavers as she looks at you, then back at Annika. "I heard," comes the valkyrie's kindly answer. "I'm glad you were able to help them find peace, Etheryn. Keep that memory of your grandmothers. Atheldred was someone who cared a great deal about a great many people, and she saved the world. Everything else about her is true, too, but make sure you remember that." |"At least they both passed on eventually." Ryn's voice is little more than a whisper. "That's what they needed," comes the kindly answer. "If I could leave you with a memory of your grandmother, take this one: Atheldred cared a great deal about a great many people, and she saved the whole world despite a gaping hole in her heart. Remember that." ] "I... I will." Ryn swallows hard. "Could I[etheryn.lowConfidence |, um, ] go for a little walk? Just to th[etheryn.lowConfidence |-th ]ink about all this." [var1 |"A breath of fresh air might be good," you say, rubbing her ear gently. "Did you want company[pc.isBimbo |, cutie ]?" "Thank you." She comes in for a hug and a gentle kiss, then says quietly, "I needed that. But I think... I think I'd just like to be alone for a few minutes. I'll be right back." "Sure." |"Clear your head? Seems fair. Catch up with us whenever." "I will." ]
rows.translation: 啊，是的。”安妮卡的嘴唇微微抿紧，“我认识你的祖母，我以为自己和她非常熟络。在我向黎明少女宣誓结婚的时候，她也在场。” 埃瑟琳痛苦地闭上了眼睛，“我……我不知道这个消息是否已经传到了这里，但是……” 大概是指你前往地窖的这件事，以及你发现了莱恩两位祖母的鬼魂吧——直到你、埃尔塔拉和赫西娅帮助莱恩，她们才得以安息。 [var0|使协调一致|驱逐] 他们。不过你最好还是闭嘴吧。[pc.isDK |这是他们自己需要解决的问题。 |只愿意分享关于Ryn的信息。 ]他已经知道了，”女武神说道，“埃尔肯定已经把消息传给了城堡里的人。她犹豫了一下，然后伸手触了触瑞恩的肩膀：“你……” 然而，对方并没有回答，而是低头看着地面，叹了口气，才再次抬起头与安妮卡对视。“C[etheryn.lowConfidence |-c ]你能告诉我，当你认识她的时候，她是一个什么样的人吗？” “可以。”她深吸一口气，继续说道：“在我加入卫队的时候，女王不仅仅记住了我的名字。她并没有只是和其他女武神们一起消磨时间，尽管她同时负责领导着整个卫队以及这个王国。 她有时间照顾仆从和卫兵；尤其是她的女儿，她对女儿的爱超过了生命本身。也许她不是那种会拥抱你并告诉你一切都会好起来的人，也不是那种会为她的战士们举办聚会、用欢乐来营造气氛的人。 但她就是那种会关心你和你的家人，会记住你关于他们所说的一切，并在之后跟进的人。她会在你做得好的时候给予表扬，不会因为一些小错误或失败而对你过于严厉，还会花时间帮助你找到正确的做事方法。 她是一位豪爽、心胸宽广的女性，她的存在能激励你成为最好的自己。她也是我见过的最伟大的战士。 [pc.dcb |你的声音听起来有点酸涩，还带着些无奈——嗯，比平时更加明显。“听起来就像是盲目崇拜英雄罢了。 |你也曾想成为像她那样的人，”你轻声说道。 |哇，真是太可爱了！你有一个可以仰望的英雄啊。 ] 安妮[pc.isDK | 不过，她并没有把这当作一种嘲讽；相反，她…… ] 回想起那些往事，她微笑着说道：“她和你一样，很快就明白了其中的含义。我们曾经进行过许多长谈，探讨在‘姐妹会’中作为姐妹意味着什么。最终，她帮助我完成了宣誓所需的一切手续，从那以后，在她统治的绝大部分时间里，我始终陪伴在她身边。 在战斗中，她总是喜欢背对太阳从空中发动攻击，以此使敌人陷入视线盲区；这样一来，卢米娅就能在很多方面为我们提供帮助。不过，她也不畏惧下到地面，加入战斗队伍，手持长矛和盾牌坚守防线，同时还会激励身边的战友们。 我们甚至愿意跟随她下地狱……事实上，我们也真的这么做了，而且不止一次。” 莱恩那双蓝宝石般的眼睛睁得大大的，眼中还闪烁着些许光芒。“她有没有提到过那次分裂事件？” “我唯一几次看到她发火，都是在我宣誓成为骑士之前。当时我的巡逻队刚刚从冰霜森林回来，我们与德鲁伊们发生了一场小冲突。 这是我的错。我们当时在追捕一个飞龙骑士，却没注意自己走到了哪里，结果直接跑进了一个德鲁伊的营地。他们……看到我们这些人，显然很不高兴。”她叹了口气，“我们虽然受了伤，但没有人死亡。 对他们来说也是如此。当我们回到城市后，女王首先确保我的战士们得到了妥善的治疗，然后就我违反停战协议以及让我的下属们陷入危险这一事，训斥了我好几分钟。 以及 德鲁伊们确实令人痛心。毕竟，他们曾经也是“我们”中的一员。她确实曾抱有希望，希望他们能够改变想法，重新加入我们族人的行列——就像那些偶尔出现的个别例子一样，尤其是在那些早期岁月里。 [pc.dcb |那么，”你带着怀疑的语气问道，“这就是我们在宫殿里遇到的那个愤怒的幽灵吗？ |你的语气中难免会带有一丝怀疑：“那听起来可不像是从地窖里出来的鬼魂啊。 |哇，她听起来还挺不错的。就是有点让人有点害怕，但同时又超级酷，还带着一种性感的魅力。”你停顿了一下，“不过……我们第一次见到她的时候，她可不是这样的。 ] 她摊开双手说道：“那并不是她向所有人展示的一面，她其实花了很多时间独自一人，沉浸在悲痛之中。当我还在卫队服役的时候，我常常看到她每天清晨在太阳升起之前就来到宫殿的地窖里独自待着；当她出来时，她眼圈周围的皮肤总是因为流泪而变得红肿柔软。 即使在公共场合，她也会谈到将太阳的光芒带给我们的人民、拯救我们所有人是如何让她感到最自豪的事情，但那次分裂却是她人生中最大的失败。我之前并不知道，在她去世后，她的精神依然留在了这个世界上，但经历了她伴侣所遭遇的一切之后，我终于能够理解为什么她会觉得自己还有未完成的事。" [var0 |他们最终想起了彼此之间的爱。”瑞恩的声音有些颤抖，她先看着你，然后又转向安妮卡。 “我听说了，”这位女武神温柔地回答道，“我很高兴你能帮助他们找到内心的平静，埃瑟琳。请永远铭记你祖母们的事迹。阿瑟尔德雷德是一个真正关心许多人的女性，她拯救了这个世界。关于她的其他一切，也都是真实的，请一定要记住这一点。 |至少他们最终都离开了这个世界。”瑞恩的声音几乎只是轻声的低语。 “这正是他们所需要的。”一个温柔的声音回答道，“如果我能让你留下关于你祖母的回忆，那就请记住这一点：阿瑟德雷德非常关心许多很多人，尽管她的心中有一道深深的伤痕，但她还是拯救了整个世界。请永远记住这一点。 ] 我……我会的。”瑞恩艰难地咽了口唾沫，“可以让我……先想想吗？[etheryn.lowConfidence |嗯， ] 去散散步怎么样？就随便走走而已……[etheryn.lowConfidence |-th ]关于这一切，我真是无话可说。 [var1 |呼吸一些新鲜空气可能会对你有好处，”你轻柔地揉着她的耳朵说道，“你想要有人陪陪你吗？[pc.isBimbo |可爱啦~ ]谢谢。”她走进来，给了他一个拥抱和一个轻柔的吻，然后轻声说道：“我需要这个。但是我想……我想我只想独自待几分钟。我马上就回来。” “当然。 |清理一下思绪？听起来挺合理的。有空随时来找我们吧。” “我会的。 ]
rows.raw: ' "Ah. Yes." Annika's lips purse. "I knew your grandmother; I like to think I knew her very well. She was there when I took my vows to the Dawn Maiden." Etheryn closes her eyes in some pain. "I... I don't know if word has reached up here, but..." Word of your journey into the crypt, presumably — and of discovering the ghosts of both of Ryn's grandmothers, not laid to rest until you, Elthara, and Hethia helped Ryn [var0|reconcile|banish] them. You hold your tongue, though[pc.isDK |; this is their shit to sort out |, only willing to share what Ryn is ]. "It has," says the valkyrie; El must have let the Keep know. Hesitantly, she reaches out for Ryn's shoulder. "Are you — ?" Instead of answering, the other woman looks down at the ground, then sighs before meeting Annika's gaze again. "C[etheryn.lowConfidence |-c ]ould you tell me what she was like when you knew her?" "I can." She takes a deep breath. "When I was in the guard, the queen did more than just learn my name. She didn't just spend time with the other valkyries, even though she led both the Order and the realm. She had time for servants, guards; she especially had time for her daughter, whom she loved more than life itself. Maybe she wasn't the kind of person who would hug you and tell you everything would be all right, nor was she the kind to throw her warriors a party and liven things up with us. But she was the kind who would ask after you and your family, and to remember everything you said about them and follow up later. She was the kind to tell you when you'd done well, to not be too harsh with you over little mistakes and failures — and to spend time helping you figure out the right way to do things. She was a bluff, big-hearted amazon who could inspire you to be the best you that you could be. And she was the greatest warrior I'd ever seen." [pc.dcb |Your voice goes a little sour and exasperated — well, more so than usual. "Sounds like hero worship." |"You wanted to be like her, too," you say quietly. |"Awww, that's kind of cute! You had a hero to look up to." ] Anni[pc.isDK | doesn't take it as a jab, though; instead she ] smiles at the memory: "She figured it out just as quickly as you did. We had a lot of long conversations about what it meant to be a sister in the Order. Eventually, she helped guide me through the things I needed to do to take my vows, and after that, I was by her side for most of the rest of her reign. In battle, she always loved to attack from the sky with the sun at her back to blind our foes; that way, Lumia would be on our side in more ways than one. But she wasn't afraid to get on the ground, stand in formation, and hold the line with spear and shield, shouting encouragement to those around her. We'd have followed her into hell... and actually did, more than once." Ryn's sapphire eyes are wide and a little shimmery. "Did she ever talk about the schism?" "One of the only times I ever saw her angry was before I took my vows; my patrol had just come back from the Frostwood, and we'd been in a skirmish with the druids. It was my fault. We were chasing a drider and didn't pay attention to where we were going, ended up running her right into a druid encampment. They were... not happy to see any of us." She sighs. "We got away with injuries, but no dead. Same for them. When we got back to the city, the queen made sure my warriors were receiving proper healing, then chewed into me for several minutes about breaking the truce and getting both my subordinates and the druids hurt. 'They' were still 'us', after all. And she did harbor hopes of them converting and rejoining the rest of our people — as a small trickle did from time to time, especially in those early years." [pc.dcb |"And this," you say skeptically, "is the same angry ghost we met in the palace?" |You can't keep a little skepticism out of your voice. "That doesn't sound like the ghost from the crypt." |"Wow. She sounds kind of nice. You know, in a teensy bit scary but also super cool and kind of sexy kind of way." You pause. "That's... that's not the way she was when we met her." ] She spreads her hands. "It wasn't a side of herself that she showed everybody, but she spent a great deal of time alone and in mourning. When I was still in the guard, I saw her rise every morning before the sun came up to be alone in the palace crypt; when she came out, the skin around her eyes was always soft and puffy from shedding tears. Even in public, she'd talk about how bringing the light of the Sun to our people and saving us all was her proudest moment, but the schism was her greatest failure. I didn't know that her spirit had stayed behind after she passed, but after what happened with her consort, I can understand why she might've thought she had unfinished business." [var0 |"They remembered their love eventually." Ryn's voice quavers as she looks at you, then back at Annika. "I heard," comes the valkyrie's kindly answer. "I'm glad you were able to help them find peace, Etheryn. Keep that memory of your grandmothers. Atheldred was someone who cared a great deal about a great many people, and she saved the world. Everything else about her is true, too, but make sure you remember that." |"At least they both passed on eventually." Ryn's voice is little more than a whisper. "That's what they needed," comes the kindly answer. "If I could leave you with a memory of your grandmother, take this one: Atheldred cared a great deal about a great many people, and she saved the whole world despite a gaping hole in her heart. Remember that." ] "I... I will." Ryn swallows hard. "Could I[etheryn.lowConfidence |, um, ] go for a little walk? Just to th[etheryn.lowConfidence |-th ]ink about all this." [var1 |"A breath of fresh air might be good," you say, rubbing her ear gently. "Did you want company[pc.isBimbo |, cutie ]?" "Thank you." She comes in for a hug and a gentle kiss, then says quietly, "I needed that. But I think... I think I'd just like to be alone for a few minutes. I'll be right back." "Sure." |"Clear your head? Seems fair. Catch up with us whenever." "I will." ] '
