rows.original: Once she's out of earshot, you [pc.breastRange DD |put your hands on your hips |fold your arms ] and glance sidelong at Annika. "[pc.dcb |Okay, that story was fine and whatever, but you can't expect me to swallow the same shit Ryn did. How the hell does your sob story match all the stuff I saw? Every damn thing down there was Atheldred's fault. |Thanks for comforting Ryn, but the way you talk about Atheldred... I don't know how to reconcile that with the person I met in the crypt. It felt like so much of what happened there was her fault. |That was sweet, to be so nice to Ryn, but are you sure about her grammama? Like, it felt like sooo much of what happened was still her fault. ]" "A lot of it was indeed her fault," she agrees. "It's a terrible thing to imprison the ones you love, no matter the reason. I think she'd have agreed with you." "[pc.isBimbo |But, like, s |S ]he didn't agree, down in the crypt. Most of what she was talking about[var0 | — before she and Synne finally started listening to us and to each other, anyway — ] was worshiping Lumia." "In life, she did care very deeply about it, but not to the point of murder. She was, after all, the same woman who agreed with Archdruid var Xadaron to let the druids leave for the Frostwood in peace, and who preserved that peace for the rest of her reign," the valkyrie points out. "She always wanted Synneva to convert, to be with her, to save the world alongside her; even when she was still alive, her consort's death was simply the latest in a long string of failures Atheldred saw herself responsible for. In death... well, it sounds like she couldn't let herself die with that failure on her conscience. Being a shade, being immersed in the evidence of your mistakes for decades on end, isn't something even the strongest of people handle well. And when all that tethers you to the living world is a single mission, maybe the love that was the reason for the mission in the first place can get all twisted inside." [pc.dcbc |You frown. "Not buying it. Hethia said Synne was a martyr. All that lovey-dovey shit doesn't mix with a lady who never let her wife go with the rest of the druids and imprisoned her until she died." |"I guess that makes sense, but if she loved Synneva so much..." Your eyebrows furrow in thought. "Hethia said that Synne was a martyr. Why did Atheldred imprison her until she died, instead of letting her leave the city with the rest of the druids?" |Your voice quavers as you follow the thread of Anni's thought. "I... I get it. And, um... I think I get why she was so sad after her wife and all the other elves died. Like, she brought them all back to the family burial place too, and you don't do that if you hate someone. She didn't want them to die, but they... awww, no. Poor... poor everybody! That's so awful!" |"That makes sense. So Atheldred was broken up about it, brought them back to the palace to be interred with honor in the family crypt, blamed herself for what happened, peacefully separated from the druids afterward, so —" And then your mind connects the last dots. "Oh. I get it. She didn't want them to die, but they must've made their own choice. Poor things. That... that's awful." ] [var1 |Anni closes her eyes and nods. "It was." "Does Ryn know?" "I'm... pretty sure she does. It's history. It was one of the things that shocked everybody, druid and Lumian, into finally agreeing to separate. It's not exactly a secret. Or a matter of dispute; even the druids knew that Atheldred wouldn't have martyred her family herself." She puts her hand on your shoulder. "It's just... not something we talk about casually." "[pc.isBimbo |That's okay. With things like these, I'm a li'l better at knowing what the right time is. |Yeah. I understand. ]" |Lumia's seneschal frowns[pc.isDK | right back at you ]. "Not let her leave? When and how did you think Synneva passed away? Why do you think the queen was so heartbroken afterward, why she brought them back to the city for an honored burial alongside the rest of the family? If you spoke to them, did they not tell— oh." She purses her lips for a long time, then takes a deep breath before speaking again. "I don't think that this is something that you should hear from me. If Etheryn wants to talk to you about it, she will, but sharing something like that about the family is her decision, not mine. And before you ask her... maybe hold back for a bit. We've had more than enough sadness for one day's conversation." ] Right on cue, Ryn arrives. Her little constitutional's done wonders for her; the tears are gone, and she's even managing a little smile. Anni's probably right to tell you to hold off. [var1 |You can talk about it with her later, if at all. |Maybe Ryn will share with you someday, if it's the kind of thing she ever feels like sharing. ] Otherwise — well, it doesn't matter, does it? "Thank you. I feel much better." "That's good! A nice walk is just the thing," the valkyrie says. She opens her palm. "Would you like to stay in touch? I'd love to share more stories about your [silly |mormor |grandmother ], if you'd like to hear them." "I would, thank you!"
rows.translation: 等她走远，你…… [pc.breastRange DD |双手叉腰 |交叉双臂 ] 然后侧眼瞥了安妮卡一眼。[pc.dcb |好吧，那个故事还算可以，但你们总不能指望我会像Ryn那样轻易相信那些鬼话吧。你们的哭诉究竟怎么就能和我看到的那些事实对得上号呢？所有那些事情，其实都是Atheldred的错。 |谢谢你安慰了Ryn，但你对Athedred的描述……我实在无法将这与我在地窖里遇到的那个人联系起来。在那种情况下发生的许多事情，似乎都应该归咎于她。 |你对Ryn这么好，真是太贴心了。不过，你确定她的妈妈没有责任吗？因为感觉发生的大部分事情其实都是她的妈妈造成的。 ]确实，很多责任都在她身上，”她承认道，“无论出于什么原因，将你所爱的人关起来，都是件可怕的事情。我想她也会同意你的看法的。”[pc.isBimbo |但是，嗯，就是这样的。 |S ]他 没有 同意，完全同意。她所说的那些内容，大部分都是正确的。[var0 | ——至少在她和辛恩最终开始倾听我们的话语，也开始互相倾听之前—— ] 她曾经崇拜Lumia。” “在现实生活中，她确实非常在意这件事，但并没有到了要为此杀人地步。毕竟，她就是那个同意让德鲁伊们平静地前往Frostwood，并在她的统治期间一直维护着这种和平的女性，”这位女武神指出。 她一直希望辛妮娃能够皈依宗教，与她在一起，共同拯救这个世界；即使在她还在世的时候，她配偶的死亡也只不过是阿瑟尔德雷德认为自己应当负责的一连串失败事件中的又一起罢了。 在死后……嗯，听起来她就是无法接受带着这样的失败感去离开人世。成为一种“阴影”，长期被自己犯下的错误的证据所困扰，即便是最坚强的人也难以应对这种处境。 当所有将你与这个现实世界联系在一起的纽带都仅仅是一个任务时，或许最初促使你去完成这个任务的那份情感，也会因此而变得扭曲不堪。 [pc.dcbc |你皱起了眉头：“我才不信呢。赫西娅说辛妮是个殉道者，但那些甜言蜜语根本说不通——一个从来不让自己的妻子和其他德鲁伊们在一起，反而把她囚禁起来直到她去世的女子，怎么可能被称作殉道者呢？ |我想这也说得通，但如果她真的那么爱辛妮瓦的话……”你皱起眉头思考着，“赫西娅说过辛妮是个殉道者。那为什么阿瑟尔德雷德要把她关起来直到她死去，而不是让她和其他德鲁伊一起离开这座城市呢？ |当你跟随安妮的思绪继续思考时，你的声音开始颤抖：“我……我明白了。而且，嗯……我想我也能理解为什么在她的妻子和其他精灵们去世后，她会那么难过。她甚至把他们全都安葬在了家族的墓地，而如果一个人真的恨某人，是不会这么做吧。她并不希望他们死去，但他们……唉，太可怜了！真的太可怕了！ |这样想确实有道理。所以阿瑟雷德因为这件事而非常痛苦，把他们带回了宫殿，希望他们能得到家族墓穴中的尊贵安葬；她也为发生的一切感到内疚，之后便与那些德鲁伊们和平地分开了……”然后你突然明白了全部真相。“哦，我明白了。她其实并不希望他们死去，但他们肯定做出了自己的选择。可怜的孩子们……真是太可怕了。 ] [var1 |安妮闭上眼睛，点了点头：“是的，确实如此。” “雷恩知道吗？” “我……很确定她知道。这是历史事实。这件事确实让所有的人，无论是德鲁伊还是卢米安人，都感到震惊，最终促使他们同意分开。这根本不是什么秘密，也不是什么有争议的事情；就连德鲁伊们也知道，阿瑟德雷德是不会牺牲她的家人的。 她自己她把手放在你的肩上，说道：“这只是……有些事情，我们不会随便谈论的。[pc.isBimbo |没关系。对于这类事情，我倒是比较擅长判断什么时候才是合适的时机。 |是的，我明白了。 ]" |卢米娅的管家皱起了眉头。[pc.isDK | 你也有同样的问题 ]不让她离开？你究竟认为辛内瓦是在什么时候、以什么方式去世的？为什么你会认为女王在之后会如此悲痛欲绝，为什么她会把他们带回城里，让他们与家族的其他成员一起接受尊贵的安葬？如果你和他们谈过的话，他们难道没有告诉你吗——哦。她沉默了很长时间，然后深吸一口气才再次开口：“我觉得这件事不应该由我来告诉你。如果埃瑟琳想和你谈这件事，她自然会去谈的。不过，关于家族这样的隐私，是否要告诉你，这是她的决定，而不是我的。 在你想问她之前……或许先等等吧。今天这一天的谈话已经让我们够难过了。 ] 恰在这时，Ryn出现了。她的身体调理方法确实发挥了效果——泪水已经止住，她甚至还能露出一丝微笑。Anni让你暂时别采取行动，或许是对的。 [var1 |如果你觉得有必要的话，可以稍后和她谈谈这件事。 |也许有一天，如果瑞恩觉得有必要分享的话，她会告诉你这件事的。 ] 否则的话——嗯，也没关系吧？”“谢谢，我现在感觉好多了。” “太好了！适当的散步正是你需要的。”女武神说道，然后摊开了手掌。“你想继续保持联系吗？我很乐意继续为你分享更多故事。 [silly |莫莫尔 |祖母 ]如果你想听的话，可以听哦。” “我当然想听，谢谢！

"Thank you. I feel much better." "That's good! A nice walk is just the thing," the valkyrie says. She opens her palm. "Would you like to stay in touch? rows.original: "Ah. This one goes back. It's a little silly. You remember how I told you about blessing sheep?" "[pc.isBimbo |Yeah! ]So that twenty become a hundred and twenty?" She nods, impressed. "Good memory. Yes, exactly. Not all of the meat in the Winter City comes from fish! There are herds of swine kept on the edge of the Frostwood, and herds of sheep that graze in the tundra. Going off to bless them is one of the tasks that Lady Elthara and the other priestesses often set for younger initiates. Extend Lumia's blessing to those who need it, make sure the shepherds have a flock, make sure there's plenty of food to go around. After all..." Her eyes go distant and cloudy for a little bit. "It's been a long time since there were enough people around to run the grazing down too low. So, well, we aren't too worried about too many mouths to feed, and we can expand the herds quite a bit whenever we need more food." [pc.bg acolyte |"That [pc.isBimbo |makes me think |brings back memories ] of other blessings," you murmur. "[pc.isBimbo |God magic |Theurgy ]'s just that [pc.isBimbo |teeeeensy |little ] bit different from other kinds of magic. Do you lay on hands as part of the ritual here?" [party.has cait |Cait beams. "I'm sure they do! You lay on hands for almost all theurgical rituals. Which is a pretty dry and clinical way of talking about something really intimate and trusting, but, you know." "I see I'm dealing with a pair of acolyte veterans! Yes, absolutely. Touch is very important." |"Oh! You were an initiate yourself. Yes, of course. Even if the ritual is to soothe a colicky baby or ease the pain of the wounded, you need physical contact. Touch is important." ] |You nod. "How do they do the blessing?" [party.has cait |"I bet you need to touch, right?" Cait says excitedly. "That's like most of the theurgy I've ever studied. It's about calmness, and feeling, and flow, and that personal connection and conduit..." "Absolutely right. Touch is as important to Lumian ritual as it is to Mallach's." |"It's theurgy," she says, "like a lot of the other things we do. Draw on the power of our goddess. But there's a ritual; you have to lay your hands on the sheep or the pig. Physical contact. Touch is important." ] ] [annika.fucked |"[pc.isBimbo |Hee hee |Oh ], it definitely is." You throw in an eyebrow-waggle for good measure. "Down, [pc.boyGirl]," she laughs. |"[pc.isBimbo |Ooooh, touch. Yeah, that's suuuper important. So long as the thingies you're supposed to touch stand still, anyway. I guess that doesn't happen with farm animals! |That makes sense. You know, sometimes laying on hands isn't the easiest thing in the world. ]" "No, it [pc.isBimbo |doe |i ]s not," she laughs. ] "Anyway. You get all kinds when you're in Lumia's service. Our people live on the edge of the Frostwood, along the great fjords, in the tundra, in the Rift, and in the Winter City itself. They all have different experiences to bring to the table..." "[pc.isBimbo|Oooh, oooh! Let me guess! Do some of those experiences not include cuddly sheepies and oinky little piggies?"|... which is code for 'not all of them know how to deal with sheep and pigs'," you finish.] "Thaaaaat would be correct." She shakes her head. "So this was the first time I saw this particular ritual. There I was, a freshly minted valkyrie, taking a gaggle of young men and women to bless a herd of swine with a pair of priestesses from the Cathedral. I don't want to make myself sound perfect; I was only in my sixties, and I'd spent enough time patrolling the [silly |Mojave |Frostwood ] in the queen's service to [silly |wish for a nuclear winter |be a little jumpy ], even on a perfectly normal walk to a farm with no danger involved at all. But I wasn't the one who had the biggest problems that day. Those acolytes and the pigs..." [pc.bgMulti noblescion acolyte |You wince, remembering the ear-splitting squalling of the herds around your family's property. "[pc.isBimbo |Yeah, they're super loud and annoying. |Not easy on the best of days. ] Who had the most trouble with them?" Annika shrugs. "Can't keep pigs in the Rift. What would they eat? The city boys and girls and the ones who lived on the edge of the Frostwood were familiar enough, but those who came from [silly |the land of the ice and snow with the midnight sun where the hot springs flow |around here in the Rift ] didn't know a hog from a horse." |"Oh no." And while you never blessed pigs yourself, you can imagine the potential catastrophe. There was one daughter of a noble family in particular who you're sure would've been absolutely miserable... "[pc.isBimbo |I bet the richy-rich elves had a hard time, huh? |I can only imagine what it would've been like for the aristocratic initiates. ]" "Hm? No, they were fine. Was it different down south? You can't feed pigs up there in the snow." |"It was the noble kids who had the most trouble, right?" "Actually, no." Annika shrugs. "I don't know if it's like this where you come from, but swine are kept pretty close to the city. [pc.isBimbo |"Awww, did they go for the wrong legs? They did, didn't they! See, that's just silly. I mean, I guess I can be a li'l bit silly sometimes too, but... aw. Anni sighs. "We tried to warn them, but sometimes you need to do something before you really understand the instructions. And of course, there's only so much room for elves and pigs in the sty; the most the priestesses and I could do was try not to embarrass them too much while they figured it out. You've gotta do your part if you're ordained!" |"[pc.dcb |Got it. |You're fair game. |You have to do your part! ]" ] "Anyway, we made sure everybody got cleaned up all right, then we shared a lunch with the swineherds. But there's a ritual; you have to lay your hands on the sheep or the pig. Physical contact. Touch is important." ] ] [annika.fucked |"[pc.isBimbo |Hee hee |Oh ], it definitely is." You throw in an eyebrow-waggle for good measure. "Down, [pc.boyGirl]," she laughs. |"[pc.isBimbo |Ooooh, touch. Yeah, that's suuuper important. So long as the thingies you're supposed to touch stand still, anyway. I guess that doesn't happen with farm animals! |That makes sense. You know, sometimes laying on hands isn't the easiest thing in the world. ]" "No, it [pc.isBimbo |doe |i ]s not," she laughs. ] "Anyway. You get all kinds when you're in Lumia's service. Our people live on the edge of the Frostwood, along the great fjords, in the tundra, in the Rift, and in the Winter City itself. They all have different experiences to bring to the table..." "[pc.isBimbo|Oooh, oooh! Let me guess! Do some of those experiences not include cuddly sheepies and oinky little piggies?"|... which is code for 'not all of them know how to deal with sheep and pigs'," you finish.] "Thaaaaat would be correct." She shakes her head. "So this was the first time I saw this particular ritual. There I was, a freshly minted valkyrie, taking a gaggle of young men and women to bless a herd of swine with a pair of priestesses from the Cathedral. I don't want to make myself sound perfect; I was only in my sixties, and I'd spent enough time patrolling the [silly |Mojave |Frostwood ] in the queen's service to [silly |wish for a nuclear winter |be a little jumpy ], even on a perfectly normal walk to a farm with no danger involved at all. But I wasn't the one who had the biggest problems that day. Those acolytes and the pigs..." [pc.bgMulti noblescion acolyte |You wince, remembering the ear-splitting squalling of the herds around your family's property. "[pc.isBimbo |Yeah, they're super loud and annoying. |Not easy on the best of days. ] Who had the most trouble with them?" Annika shrugs. "Can't keep pigs in the Rift. What would they eat? The city boys and girls and the ones who lived on the edge of the Frostwood were familiar enough, but those who came from [silly |the land of the ice and snow with the midnight sun where the hot springs flow |around here in the Rift ] didn't know a hog from a horse." |"Oh no." More memories flood into your mind, of fish-out-of-water initiates flailing around in the gods' service; the cloister wasn't your whole life any more than it was these frost elves.' And while you never blessed pigs yourself, you can imagine the potential catastrophe. There was one daughter of a noble family in particular who you're sure would've been absolutely miserable... "[pc.isBimbo |I bet the richy-rich elves had a hard time, huh? |I can only imagine what it would've been like for the aristocratic initiates. ]" "Hm? No, they were fine. Was it different down south? We keep pigs pretty close to the city, so even well-to-do elves are more or less familiar with them." Annika grimaces. "It was the Rift elves who had the most trouble. You can't feed pigs up there in the snow." |"It was the noble kids who had the most trouble, right?" "Actually, no." Annika shrugs. "I don't know if it's like this where you come from, but swine are kept pretty close to the city. The initiates who grew up inside the walls, whether they came from the elite or from families like mine, knew how to handle pigs. No, it was the Rift children who had the most trouble." ] "What'd they do wrong?" "Well," the valkyrie says, "the task was to go in and bless juvenile pigs. Less than a year old; about two feet or so long. Very loud, but more importantly, surprisingly strong... at least in their hind legs. And from the way they moved around in the mud, basically every initiate had to pick up a pig to hold it for someone else to bless. Some of them were better at it than others. They picked up the pigs by the hind legs, and since the pigs' front legs were weaker, the little things couldn't get a grip. But those Rift kids..." She buries her head in her hands. [pc.isBimbo |"Awww, did they go for the wrong legs? They did, didn't they! See, that's just silly. I mean, I guess I can be a li'l bit silly sometimes too, but... aw. Did they get all muddy and stuff?" |"Let me guess," you chuckle. "They went for the front legs, and the little pigs were strong enough to drag them down facefirst into the muck." ] "Poor things." Anni sighs. "We tried to warn them, but sometimes you need to do something before you really understand the instructions. And of course, there's only so much room for elves and pigs in the sty; the most the priestesses and I could do was try not to embarrass them too much while they figured it out. One of them in particular, a muscular young man who insisted on trying to grapple with the things, got absolutely covered in mud and... filth before he learned his lesson. Never try to mud-wrestle a pig." That sparks an elven grin. "Lest you think that that was unusual, I've done it many times since, with many other acolytes, and there's always one in every group." [pc.dcb |"Sounds like a shit job that the important priests and priestesses push off to the ones who're too new to say no." |"They don't just farm that job out to the initiates because it's gross, right?" |"Is it always acolytes? Or do the fancy priests and priestesses like Elthara have to bless the herds, too?" ] "I don't think there's any place in the world where people won't at least try to get out of the dirty jobs if they can," she admits, "but even the matrons have to at least do their turn blessing fields or flocks every year, and everybody helps melt the snow in the city after particularly big blizzards. Usually we just try to make sure we aren't making you stay on your feet too long or bend down too far if you're expecting, but otherwise..." [party.has cait |Cait nods. "Yeah! Some people will always try to get over, but most of the priestesses back home really wanted to make sure people felt Mallach's love. You've gotta do your part if you're ordained!" |"[pc.dcb |Got it. |You're fair game. |You have to do your part! ]" ] "Anyway, we made sure everybody got cleaned up all right, then we shared a lunch with the swineherds. Not a bad day's work!" She spreads her hands. "Can't be afraid to get yourself dirty in the goddess's service." '

rows.original: "Pretty much anywhere grapes are grown, there are festivals for both Lumia and Velun. You know, fertility of the soil, lushness of the vine. And, ah, more than a little debauchery. People like to let themselves go; I'm sure you know how it is." Annika grins. "Valkyries don't always attend those events. If we sent a delegation to every festival of Lumia, we'd never have any warriors to actually do warrior-ing. Usually it's the paladin orders and priesthoods from the area who handle all that. But there was one time, about, goddess, eighty years ago or so, when an older valkyrie named Celedis asked me to come along with her to the Anthekaraia, one of the wine-festivals in Sartanni." "'One of' the wine-festivals?" Visions of utter drink-soaked debauchery dance through your head. "[pc.isBimbo |Are there a bunch more than that |How many do they have ]?" "Four every year," she says, "and that was part of the problem. See, we were there to help dedicate a shrine to Lumia, but the reason that they were putting the shrine in was a bit awkward. Several months earlier, the previous wine festival, the Lanteia, went a little awry. Sartanni doesn't have much space for vine-growing, what with all the thick forests about, but the grapes they do make turn into extremely potent wine. Normally, they cut it with water, but someone snuck everybody the uncut stuff mid-celebration. It was an absolute mess. Half the people at the festival ended up getting into fights and a few almost died. The other half, well, they did what the Sartannians normally do at such events, just with even less self-control. And the priestesses of Lumia and Velun were all so smashed that they mayyyy have gone a little wild with their fertility blessings." [party.has cait |Next to you, Cait erupts in a fountain of giggles that soon gets you following along, too. |That last gets your attention. "Oh my." ] Anni grins and spreads her hands. "By all accounts, they were so drunk that it wasn't even fun. Between that and the violence, they were happy to have us around to make sure that the Anthekaraia didn't turn into a similar mess." "And did you?" "Well, it didn't get violent again. Mostly. There were a few almost-fights that broke out, and I... well, I lost my temper. To indulge like that, after what a disaster the last time was — ugh! They were being so irresponsible." Then she shakes her head. "Sorry. Me putting the fear of the gods into a few ruffians isn't the story. Here's the real story. You see, thanks to what happened before, there were several priestesses who were now expecting for the first time and didn't know who was responsible, and now they weren't even allowed to drink with the rest of the festival goers. You can imagine how unhappy they were about everything." [pc.isDK |"Yeah, I bet it sucked," you mutter. |"Poor things," you say sympathetically. ][var0| Then you look down at your own baby bump. "I know what that's like."] [annika.pregStage 1 |She reaches for your arm and meets your gaze with a reassuring smile. "Hey, if you're feeling left out, let me know." [pc.isBimbo |"Never ever! But I might wanna fuck anyway, hee hee. Oooh! Is that |"I may," you murmur, biting your lip, "take you up on that." Then you raise an eyebrow. "Is that ] what you did for those priestesses?" |"Yeah. It's not easy, having a baby." "And how did you handle it? Satisfy some of their, mmm, cravings?" ] "Well," Annika says, "most of them just wanted hugs and reassurance, conversation, a sense that someone cared about them and that they were being included; I'm sure you can imagine. I liked spending time with them better than with all of the people who were getting sloshed, so that wasn't hard. Besides, most weren't in the mood." She coughs, then adds, "Most doesn't mean all, though, and some of the priestesses really needed to feel loved. That was... tricky for me, but I wasn't with anybody at the time, and they were a little bit wantsome, and, well, if a single Lumian is going to have sex with anybody..." [pc.dcb |"So you got laid good and proper." |"So everybody had fun," you chuckle. |"Hee hee hee. Sounds like you enjoyed yourself too!" ] "I'll just say that it was a lovely festival." Then her smile gets a little more rueful. "It definitely brought home just how careful someone like me needs to be, though. [annika.pregStage 1 |If we hadn't made a plan, I..." You stop that line of thought right there. "But we did. Now we're [annika.numKids 1 |making our family a little bigger |starting a family ], and we're doing it together. I like the way it turned out." Her ice-eyes go glassy and her ears twitch once, then again, and then she folds you into a tight hug. "So do I," she whispers. |[annika.numKids 1 |Before I found someone who was ready to start a family, I..." You smile right back. "[pc.dcb |Hey, you don't need to rehash it. We did things right. I liked that. |I know. You stayed safe until we made a plan together. And you know how much that means to me. |Aww, don't worry, sweetie! We did everything right. We stayed safe, we talked about it, we made a plan, and then we did the thing. And you know just how amazing it was for me! ]" "[pc.isBimbo |For |To ] me, too," the valkyrie says feelingly. |Being a single parent is something I don't want to make anybody go through. And imagine not knowing if you have a child out there somewhere... no. I couldn't do that. Wine festivals are fun and all, but you've always got to keep the consequences in mind." ] ]
rows.translation: 几乎在任何种植葡萄的地方，都会举行庆祝卢米亚和维伦的节日。你知道的，这些节日都是为了纪念土壤的肥沃和葡萄藤的茂盛。当然，也会有一些热闹的庆祝活动……人们都会尽情享受这些时刻，我相信你也很明白这种感觉吧。安妮卡笑了笑道：“女武神并不总是会参加那些活动。如果我们每次卢米亚的节日都派代表团去参加，那我们就根本不会有战士可以去执行战斗任务了。通常都是当地的圣骑士团和神职人员来处理这些事情的。 但有一次，大概是在八十年前吧，一位名叫塞莱迪斯的年长女武神邀请我和她一起参加萨塔尼举行的葡萄酒节之一——安塞卡里亚节。你脑海中不断浮现出那些喝得酩酊大醉、纵情狂欢的场景。[pc.isBimbo |还有更多的吗？ |他们一共有多少个？ ]每年有四次，”她说，“而这正是问题所在。你看，我们本来是去帮忙为Lumia建立一座神龛的，但他们之所以要建立这个神龛，原因其实有点尴尬。几个月前，在上一次葡萄酒节——Lanteia上，发生了一些意外。 萨塔尼地区由于周围环绕着茂密的森林，其实并没有太多适合种植葡萄的土地，但他们种植出来的葡萄确实能酿成味道极其醇厚的葡萄酒。通常情况下，人们会用水将这种葡萄酒稀释后饮用，但在庆祝活动进行到一半时，有人偷偷地将未稀释的原酒分发给了大家。 场面简直是一团糟。节日上有一半的人发生了斗殴，还有几个人差点丢了性命。而另外一半人呢，他们也就只是做了萨坦尼亚人会做的事情而已。 通常情况下 在这样的场合下，人们的自制力会更加薄弱。而卢米娅和维伦的女祭司们当时都喝得酩酊大醉，以至于在施展生育祝福时，可能会有些失控吧…… [party.has cait |在你旁边，Cait突然爆发出一阵阵咯咯的笑声，很快你也跟着笑了起来。 |最后那句话确实吸引了你的注意。“哦，我的天。 ] 安妮咧嘴一笑，摊开双手说道：“据大家所说，他们喝得烂醉如泥，根本没有什么乐趣可言。再加上那些暴力行为，他们其实很庆幸有我们在场，这样才能确保安塞卡里亚不会变成同样的混乱局面。” “那么你们真的做到了吗？” “嗯，至少没有让事情变得更糟。 暴力 又一次。基本上，还是发生了几次差点打起来的冲突，而我……嗯，我失去了控制。在上次发生了那么严重的灾难之后，他们还继续这样胡闹——真是太不负责任了。然后她摇了摇头。 抱歉，让那些恶棍们感到恐惧其实并不是真正的事情。真正的故事是这样的：由于之前发生的一些事情，有几位女祭司现在第一次怀孕了，但却不知道是谁造成的，而现在她们甚至不被允许和其他参加庆典的人一起喝酒。 你可以想象，他们对这一切该有多不满。 [pc.isDK |是啊，肯定很糟糕吧，”你低声说道。 |可怜的家伙们，”你满怀同情地说道。 ][var0| 然后你低头看着自己凸出的腹部，心想：“我明白那种感觉是什么了。] [annika.pregStage 1 |她伸出手握住你的手臂，用一个让人安心的微笑与你的目光对视。“嘿，如果你觉得被冷落了，一定要告诉我。 [pc.isBimbo |绝对不会！不过我可能还是想做那件事吧，嘿嘿。哦哦！是这样吗…… |我也许……”你咬着嘴唇低声说道，“会答应你的请求。”然后你挑了挑眉毛，“真的吗？ ] 你为那些女祭司做了些什么？ |是啊，生孩子确实不容易。” “那你是怎么应对的？是怎么满足他们的一些需求的呢？ ] 嗯，”安妮卡说道，“他们大多数人其实只是需要拥抱、安慰、交谈，只是希望有人关心他们，让他们感受到自己是被重视的；我相信你能够理解这种感受。比起那些喝得酩酊大醉的人，我更喜欢和他们在一起，所以这对我来说并不难。不过，大多数人都没这个心情……”她轻咳了一声，接着补充道：“不过，‘大多数’并不意味着‘全部’，有些女祭司们…… 真的 人总是需要感受到被爱的。这对我来说……有点困难，不过当时我并没有和任何人在一起，而那些人又表现得有点主动……嗯，如果非要有一个卢米安人发生性关系的话，那应该就是这种情况吧。 任何身体…… [pc.dcb |所以你终于得到了你应得的报应。 |所以大家都玩得很开心，”你笑着说。 |嘻嘻嘻，看来你也很开心吧！ ] 我只想说，那确实是一个很美好的节日。”她的笑容中带着一丝怅惘，“不过，这也让我更加意识到，像我这样的人确实需要格外小心。 [annika.pregStage 1 |如果我们没有制定计划的话，我…… 算了，别再想下去了。“但我们制定了计划，现在我们…… [annika.numKids 1 |让我们的家庭变得更加圆满 |组建家庭 ]我们正在这么做。 一起我喜欢最终呈现出来的效果。” 她的冰冷的双眼突然变得湿润起来，耳朵也抽动了几下，然后她紧紧地将你拥入怀中。“我也是，”她轻声说道。 |[annika.numKids 1 |在我遇到那个愿意与我一起组建家庭的人之前，我……” 你也会微笑着回应我：[pc.dcb |嘿，你没必要再重复那些事了。我们做得没错，我很满意。 |我知道。在我们一起制定计划之前，你一直保持着安全。你也知道，这对我来说意味着多少。 |哎呀，别担心，亲爱的！我们一切都做得很好。我们注意了自己的安全，也认真讨论过这个问题，还制定了计划呢。 然后 我们真的做到了。你知道，这对我来说有多么不可思议、多么令人兴奋吧！ ]" "[pc.isBimbo |为了 |为了 ] 我也是，”这位女武神满怀感慨地说道。 |作为单亲父母，这是我绝不希望任何人经历的事情。想象一下，永远不知道自己的孩子是否还活在世上……不，我无法承受这样的痛苦。葡萄酒节固然有趣，但人们始终必须牢记这些行为可能带来的后果。 ] ]

rows.translation: 节日庆典

rows.original: "I'm sure you've seen pilgrims down south — maybe even been on pilgrimage yourself! One of the things that the military orders are responsible for doing is keeping pilgrims safe. Even if they don't always have that much money, they're usually easy targets for bandits and unscrupulous warlords... that is, unless there are some holy warriors accompanying them on the journey!" You cock your head. "[pc.dcb |You said |I thought |Wait, I thought ] this wasn't going to be a war story." "It isn't!" she says in her cheerful elven singsong. "Usually, the sight of golden wings is enough to warn the bad guys away. When I went along on pilgrimage in the southlands, I mostly ended up swapping stories with those making their way to the Lumian shrines or heading back home after the festivals." "[pc.dcb |Probably super fuckin' chatty, huh? |Good conversationalists, I hope. |Oooh! Do they have good stories? ]" She grins. "They do okay! [silly |Pardon me if you've already heard this one, but one pilgrim told me this story about three brothers who set out to slay Tira and — um, spoiler alert, I guess? — ended up getting tricked into murdering each other over treasure. |There was one pilgrim from a very long way away — beyond Jassira, even — who told a story about a common woman who married a king, but the king was cursed to forget their marriage, and both of them had to battle evil spirits and counselors before the queen and her young son could be reunited with her husband. ] And the teller really made it pop. She used the shadows around the campfire to give herself that extra bit of mystery, and she did the voices just perfectly; I can still hear them even though it's been many years. "The Order of the Oriflamme, the Lumian paladins in Yvennes and eastern Belhar, take protection very seriously, and not just for Lumian pilgrims but for all who visit the shrines of the Seven in the land of their remit. A few decades ago, one of the Oriflamme paladins, a grim, bearded mountain of a man named Gistemar, joined the group I was escorting, bringing with him Karim, an adorable little catboy priest from Jassira. Turned out some Mallachite pilgrims on their way to the home of an ancient Yvennese poet had been robbed by some bandits in the area, and they wanted my help to find their lair." [var0 |"Huh. rows.translation: 我敢肯定，你在南方肯定见过那些朝圣者——甚至可能自己也参加过朝圣之旅吧！军队的一项重要职责就是保护这些朝圣者的安全。尽管他们通常没有太多的钱，但他们很容易成为强盗和无良军阀的目标……当然，如果他们有神圣战士陪同的话，情况就会不同了！” 你歪了歪头，似乎在思考着什么。[pc.dcb |你是这么说的。 |我想。 |等等，我本来还以为…… ] 这本来不会成为一个战争故事。” “确实不是！”她用那种欢快的精灵式唱腔说道，“通常，金色的翅膀就已经足以吓退那些坏人了。当我去南方朝圣的时候，我遇到的大多数人都在和那些前往卢米安神庙的人，或者是在节日结束后回家的人聊天、交换故事呢。[pc.dcb |大概会变得超级爱闲聊吧，对吧？ |希望你们都是擅长交谈的人。 |哦哦！他们的故事很精彩吗？ ]她咧嘴笑了：“它们表现得还不错！ [silly |如果你们已经听过这个故事，还请见谅。有位朝圣者给我讲过这样一个故事：三个兄弟一起出发，打算杀死提拉，但是——嗯，这里应该算是剧透吧——最终他们却因为争夺财宝而互相残杀。 |有一位远道而来的朝圣者——甚至来自贾西拉以外的地方——他讲述了一个故事：一个普通的妇女嫁给了国王，但国王被诅咒，忘记了这段婚姻。因此，这对夫妇不得不与邪恶的精灵和阴谋者展开斗争，直到王后和她年幼的儿子才能够与丈夫重逢。 ] 那位女演员的表演确实令人印象深刻。她利用营火周围的阴影为自己增添了一层神秘感，而且她的配音也做得非常完美；即使过了很多年，我仍然能够清晰地回想起那些声音。 “奥里弗拉姆骑士团——那些驻扎在伊文尼斯以及贝尔哈尔东部的卢米安圣骑士们——非常重视保护工作。他们保护的对象不仅仅是卢米安的信徒，还包括所有来到他们管辖范围内、那些七大圣所所在之地的人们。 几十年前，一位名叫吉斯泰玛尔的魁梧男子加入了我们护送的队伍。他面容严肃，留着胡须，看起来像一座山一样高大。他还带着一位来自贾西拉的可爱小猫人牧师——卡里姆。原来，一些前往一位古代伊文尼斯诗人家中的马拉基特朝圣者在途中遭到了当地强盗的抢劫，他们希望我能帮助他们找到这些强盗的藏身之处。" [var0 |哈。 [pc.isBimbo |等等，安妮——等一下。 |D ]他们不是有自己的圣骑士来帮忙处理这些事情吗？毕竟，你曾经见过其中一位。” “他们确实有；我过去也和玛拉基特的圣骑士们合作过，他们的实力不容小觑。不过，我们都属于同一个信仰，因此经常会进行合作——而且合作的方式也多种多样。[silly |当然，我不会透露故事的结局或其他任何细节。 ]我想，卡里姆肯定是想找一个当地人来帮他对付这些强盗。 ] [pc.dcb |你眯起了眼睛：“这话听起来又像是在讲战争故事了。 |等等，”你反驳道，“这听起来越来越像一个战争故事了。 |等等等等，强盗？我以为这不会是一个战争故事啊，安妮！ ] 不是这样的！”她向你保证，“一切都是经过精心策划的。没错，发光的翅膀确实不太符合‘隐秘行动’的特点，但我们的确想得很周全！那些朝圣者们在海边扎营，离一些悬崖并不远，而我帮助吉斯泰马尔和卡里姆找到了那处像洞穴一样裂开的悬崖边缘。 那些强盗都躲在里面，他们显然还没有准备好进行真正的战斗。”她犹豫了一下，然后承认道：“其中有些人确实试图冲上来攻击我们，我也确实用拳头打了他们。还有一个人试图用刀刺向卡里姆，但吉斯泰马尔把那个强盗甩来甩去，威胁说要把他甩成薄饼。 [silly |为了阻止其他人跟进。 |为了阻止其他人也这么做 ]从那以后，他们的声音都小了很多。 “但事情并不是这样的。总之，在那之后，我仔细检查了他们的藏身处，那些洞穴里…… 有库存那里有一堆堆朝圣者留下的施舍物，还有旅行者用的衣物可以用来伪装，甚至还有几个贾西兰地区的男孩女孩，他们大概是想把他们卖为奴隶。” “哇，”你低声惊叹道，“真是收获颇丰啊。” “但这还不是最精彩的部分，”安妮卡笑着说，“你知道吗，原来卡里姆来伊文尼斯其实是为了寻找别的东西，一些特别的东西——马拉克的神圣遗物。而我们真的找到了它。[pc.isBimbo |嘿嘿，我打赌肯定是这样吧。 |什么？ ] 他那神圣的乳头链[pc.isBimbo |! |? ]" [party.has cait |你的小猫伙伴的眼睛瞪得大大的。“嘿！”，然后她歪了歪头，嘴角浮现出一丝微笑，“那个东西在贾西拉被妥善保存了几个世纪。 ] 你差不多猜对了：那是一个镀金、镶嵌宝石的肛门塞。”女武神的笑容更加灿烂了。“我只能猜测，为何‘激情王子’会需要这样的东西，但我确实知道，那件物品肯定蕴含着他的神圣力量。而且，那也是一个相当漂亮的玩具呢…… [party.has cait |哈哈！我都有点嫉妒了。”凯特笑着说，“你们自己用过这个吗？ |你必须问：[pc.isBimbo |你用过它吗？ |以我的个人经验来说…… ]?" ] 哦，对于吉斯泰马尔和卡里姆在旅途剩下的时间里在帐篷里做了些什么，我实在无法证实，”安妮卡一本正经地说。“不过，从那晚开始，我确实知道那个小家伙每晚都会在篝火旁讲一些最浪漫、最撩人的故事。简直就好像他…… 接收 就在他坐在那里的时候，获得了神圣的灵感。[party.has cait | 还有凯特 ] 听到这个，真让人忍不住发笑。[pc.dcb |讨厌的家伙。看来结果还不错吧？ |哦，天哪。听起来他的旅行很愉快吧。你们其他人呢？只要结局好，一切都无所谓吧？ |嘻嘻，不知道他还坐在别的什么东西上面呢！想到这里，你忍不住咬了咬嘴唇，然后才把思绪重新拉回到正轨上。“那么，你们大家都安全回到了吧？ ]没错！我们救出的贾西拉人最终都安全地完成了他们的朝圣之旅，而我和卢米安人一起旅行时，有几位前强盗帮忙搬运行李，所以我们去太阳花园的路上也顺利多了。吉斯泰马尔还把卡里姆带回了贾西拉，而且他还带着一件神圣的遗物呢。”她的眼睛闪闪发亮，“对卡里姆来说，那次长途航海一定非常辛苦吧……毕竟离家那么远，而且环境也不熟悉。” 你也对她眨了眨眼，说道：“是啊。[pc.isBimbo |嗯，我在想有没有机会能用一下那个插头…… |哦，我敢肯定肯定是这样的。 ]"

rows.translation: 朝圣者

rows.original: "Oh, certainly," Annika assures you. "I've traveled a great deal. These wings make it a little easier for me than most, and in Lumia's service we often go very far afield.[annika.numKids 1 | Perhaps less often for me now," she chuckles wryly, looking down at the ever-present bassinet, "but I've put enough journeying into the last hundred years to be content with that. ]" [annika.numKids 1 |"[pc.isBimbo |Maybe we could go somewhere with the bab[annika.numKids 2 |ies |y ] later! |I wouldn't rule out a family trip somewhere. ]" You grin down at your little angel before turning back to Anni. ]"Any[pc.isBimbo |, like, super weird | particularly unusual ] places? Places most people in our part of the world don't get to visit?" She raises her hands toward the roof. "You mean how like this very keep, even Njorhaalt itself, hadn't been seen by southern eyes before [etheryn.crowned |Her Majesty |Lady Etheryn ] brought you here?" Then she sets her gently-amused expression aside. "I understand. Hmm. Well, [party.has cait |may I assume that, unlike Caitriss here, you've never been to Jassira?" "N[pc.isBimbo |aaah. I'd love to visit, though! |o. Well, not yet, anyway. ]"[var0| You [cait.fucked |lace your fingers in Cait's and give her a smooch |smile fondly at the beaming kitty in question, who's been your friend through thick and thin ]. "Maybe someday, when all this is over."] "Oh, there's not even a question about it!" Cait giggles. "We're going to have so much to show you." Then she turns to Anni: "So, you've been there?" |I guess we could start with Jassira! I don't... believe you've been, have you?" "[pc.isBimbo |Nuh-uh! But |No, never — although ] I do know [var1|many Jassirans living in the Marches|[flags.FARRAH_WAYFORT|a few Jassirans|someone from there]]. [pc.isBimbo |Wait." You pause. "Does that mean that y |Y ]ou have?" ] "Of course! I know it's not exactly the kind of climate you'd expect for, you know, a frost elf, but we're actually not that bad at dealing with the sun — here at home, whenever the clouds move off, the sun shining off all the snow and ice can be blinding. Our people were used to it even before most of us turned to Lumia. And as for the heat, well, that part's not so easy, but we can learn to manage." Anni takes hold of her cheek thoughtfully. "That said, Jassirans themselves know the value of staying in the shade as much as possible." [party.has cait |"Absolutely." Your kitty companion exaggeratedly wipes some nonexistent sweat off her brow. "So, what were you doing in Jassira, anyway? I don't remember ever hearing about valkyries spending much time back home." "We didn't — not for long, anyway. We were on our way to somewhere else." |"[pc.dcb |No shit. You probably don't last long down there if you don't." You yawn. "So, why were you actually there? |I bet." You manage a low whistle. "Anything in particular you were doing there? |I guess it'd be cooler there for sure! Makes it super tough to work on a tan, though. Gotta get those rays on vacay!" Then you frown. "Wait, were you on vacay? Or were you, like, there for some other reason? ]" [pc.isBimbo |The seneschal shakes her head, smiling. "Oh, not a vacation. We were on our way to someplace else. |"Stopping in on our way to go somewhere else, honestly. ] Jassira was beautiful, but it wasn't the reason we crossed the ocean." ] "Beyond Jassira? I thought it was all[pc.isBimbo |, like ]... more desert.[pc.bg scholar | Nobody's been able to go beyond the desert in hundreds of years. All we've got are myths like 'The Wonders Beyond the Sands' and a few disconnected stories. ][var0| Or... wait. Were you just going up the coast, to where Cait's family was from?]" "[pc.bg scholar |We were indeed going beyond the desert," Anni confirms, grinning. "And yes, some of those stories are more than just stories. |Not quite just desert," Anni corrects. "There used to be old myths about what lay beyond the sands. Most of them aren't true. Some, though... some are. ] The great trackless dunes extend for many days' travel, and few who can't fly can make the journey, given how few oases there are. There is no regular trade, as far as I know, no ancient caravanserais for travelers to shelter in. It's truly [silly |an empty quarter of the world |the most empty land I've ever seen ]. Beyond the dunes, for those lucky few who can find the way and survive the trip, lies the high desert, and then the mountains, each a difficult journey in itself. But on the other side of the mountains, there are green rolling uplands leading down to enormous river valleys, lush forests, actual rain. The people there in the uplands and the alluvium call their home the land of a thousand cities. I... didn't have the time to count," she laughs, "but whenever my sisters and I were flying, we could see many built-up places, walled settlements, bustling marketplaces." [party.has atugia |"Wow," Tui breathes. "I've read books about this[pc.bg scholar | too ], but never actually met anyone who'd been there. What was it like? Nothing I've ever read gave many details — at least, not reliable ones." |That's enough to raise your eyebrow. "[pc.dcb |You're pulling my [pc.hasRealCock |dick |leg ]. |Wow. |Gosh! ] [pc.bg scholar |You actually made it to the civ[pc.isBimbo |... sevulla... people |ilization ] beyond the sands. |A whole civ[pc.isBimbo |... sevulla... whole bunch of people |ilization ] and no one knows about [pc.isBimbo |them |it ]? ]" ] "There's more than one civilization out there, and their peoples are very similar to those of the south: orcs, humans, catfolk, and more. First beyond the mountains is Ariana, a vast land with a proud harpy queen. She — if she still rules, at any rate, because this journey was decades ago — claims descent from the majestic bird-women the Arianans worshiped as gods long ago, before they changed their ways and came to honor the Seven. Quick-slithering snake-folk, manticores, 'taurs with the lower bodies of sharp-clawed lions — all mingle in the markets there with salamanders, humans, and elves. "How does one sum up whole cultures from first impressions? Hmm. They burn a local sweet-smelling seed for good luck, they never turn their backs on each other, and whenever they tell you 'no', they always make a tutting sound with their tongue." She tries to imitate the tongue-click: "A little like that. Goddess, it's been ages. Oh, and they don't shy away from praising those they admire. There are carved images in the walls of the mountains that honor heroic panther-warriors of times past, but the greatest rock reliefs of all are reserved for the queen and her avian ancestors." [party.has agnimitra |"Huh. Harpy queens?" Agnimitra frowns. "I can't... remember ever traveling beyond the Jassiran desert, but that... that doesn't mean much at this point. Did they — not just the queens, but any harpies you saw over there — have red feathers?" "When I was there, the queen did not. I don't really remember if I saw any other red-feathered harpies... but what I do remember is that most of the harpies there had more, mmm, elaborate plumage than the harpies around here. If you're related, it would have to be very far back." The valkyrie spreads her hands. "I don't know if they have stories about you; it's not something I thought to ask about. But I do know that the Arianans, harpy and otherwise, use fire magic in their worship and everyday lives a great deal. I wouldn't be surprised if you made a home there at one time." "Neither would I." Her eyes look away at something else for a long time before she starts to speak again. "I — I don't know if I want to know, at this point. Maybe... sorry, I don't want to interrupt the story. What else did you find?" |[agni.recruited|Huh. You wonder if Agnimitra's related to that queen, or any of the other Arianan harpies, somehow. You wouldn't put it past her.|Wow. That's quite the variety.] ] [party.has agnimitra|The encouraging smile Anni was wearing droops a little bit, but she restores it quickly enough. "Well, b|"B]eyond Ariana is Xenaspa, nestled in an even higher mountain range than the one separating Ariana from the desert. In those cities, rife with intrigue, there are elven warriors who claim descent from lost Belharan armies, antlike myrmarcs with engineering talent to match anything in Khor'minos, nagas of great age and wisdom, roc-riders like the avanai of the Rift, long-necked traders from a land I'd never heard of before, and more great leothran-like felines, striped and orange with tremendous fangs. To govern them all, a great code of laws stands in the marketplace of Ortosina, one of the cities we visited, written in a dozen languages; one of them looks like a very, very old Belharan script which seems to call the city 'Ediveia [silly |Eschate |the Furthest ].' Some of the people there truly did have ancestors in your lands, and one of the languages they speak isn't that far away from Belharan itself. That's how we were able to get by." You hold your tongue, not wanting to interrupt too much, but it's kind of amazing to think of how many places Belharans ended up during the imperial era. How many other undiscovered places have bits and pieces of their — your — culture even to this day? "Goddess, the marvels of Xenaspa..." Besides, Anni's on a roll. Why stop her? "Like the myrmarcs — the things they can engineer, the wonders they can build, simply have to be seen to be believed. These ones were different than the ones in southern Belhar, at least as far as I know. But like their Belharan cousins, they mine vast amounts of gold[silly |, just like Herodotos said! He wasn't lying! He just got the size of the ants wrong ]. Between myrmarcs and dust elves, Xenaspa has mines to rival Khor'minos, if not surpass it. And, unique to the great mountains that ring Xenaspa, they also mine a mysterious, beautiful blue stone that can be used in art, sculpture, and even makeup. "The earth's bounty commands princely sums from the traders of a multitude of lands, but the Xenaspans keep the best for themselves, using it to decorate colossal temples to the Seven to rival any in Belhar. I remember the sanctuary to Nareva in Amoltos, with its vast libraries overseen by gorgeous, sinuous naga priestesses, where local gold-flecked blue was worked into the traditional black and white decorations so beautifully..." Then she holds up her hands. "I don't want to exaggerate too much — Ortosina, Gapakoana, Amoltos, and the other cities we saw weren't literally made of gold or anything. But Xenaspa is a populous and wealthy land, with fertile soil and great stores of minerals, and those who enjoy its riches face steep competition to control them. "There are other lands beyond, places we were never able to visit, and of which we only heard stories and rumors. More mountains, like the whole continent has a great rocky spine stretching up to the sky. Plateaus with vast, deep lakes, home to an even wider variety of harpyfolk. Frozen forests not unlike ours even higher up in the mountains, full of game and so much gold that it sits in the creeks and streams there for you to just pick up with your bare hands. And even further east: jungles, warm plains, coastlands along a beautiful blue sea full of enormous oysters and siorcanna in a riot of colors that rival the shark-folk here in the rift..." She sighs. "Would that we could have simply traveled instead. But we had a task to complete for the Lumian faithful there, and by the time we felt it complete, we had already stayed too long and suffered too much to continue. But I can tell you this: there are indeed lands beyond the desert, and more elsewhere. This world has more secrets in it than even the old Belharans knew." That it does. [flags.ANNIKA_TALK_TRAVEL||That said, you do notice that she was very sketchy on the details of what she did in the lands of Xenaspa and Ariana. Maybe you should ask if she has a war story about it.]

agnimitra|安妮脸上那鼓励人心的微笑稍微黯淡了一下，但很快就又恢复了。“好吧，b……|B]在阿里亚纳之外，还有塞纳斯帕，它坐落在比那片将阿里亚纳与沙漠分隔开来的山脉还要高的地方。在那些充满阴谋与诡计的城市里，居住着自称继承了早已消失的贝尔哈兰军队的精灵战士们；还有那些拥有与科尔米诺斯相媲美的工程技术的蚁族；以及那些古老而智慧的娜迦族；还有像裂谷地区的阿瓦奈人那样的巨鸟骑手；还有那些来自我从未听说过的土地的、长着长脖子的商人们；此外，还有更多那些体型庞大、身披条纹与橙色皮毛、拥有凶猛獠牙的、类似利奥斯兰猫科动物的生物们。 据我所知，这些与贝尔哈尔南部的那些有所不同。但和他们的贝尔哈尔同胞一样，他们也会开采大量的黄金。[silly |正如希罗多德所说！他并没有撒谎！只是他搞错了蚂蚁的实际大小而已。 ]在蜜蚁族和尘精灵之间，塞纳斯帕的矿场规模即便不比霍尔米诺斯更庞大，也至少可以与之相媲美。而环绕塞纳斯帕的那些巍峨山脉中，还蕴藏着一种神秘而美丽的蓝色宝石——这种宝石不仅可以用于艺术创作和雕塑，甚至还可以用来制作化妆品。 地球上的这些珍稀资源为许多地区的商人带来了巨额利润，但泽纳斯潘人却将这些最珍贵的资源据为己有，用它们来装饰那些规模庞大的神庙，其华丽程度足以与贝尔哈尔的任何神庙相媲美。我还记得阿莫尔托斯地区那座供奉纳雷瓦的神庙——那里有庞大的图书馆，由那些美丽而婀娜多姿的娜迦女祭司负责管理；当地的蓝色金属上点缀着金色的纹饰，这些传统意义上的黑白装饰元素被运用得如此巧妙，实在令人赞叹不已。然后她举起了双手，继续说道：‘我并不想夸大其词——奥托西纳、加帕科阿纳、阿莫尔托斯，以及我们看到的其他那些城市，其实并不是真的由黄金或其他稀有物质建造而成的。但是克萨内斯帕却是一片人口众多、资源丰富的土地，那里拥有肥沃的土壤和大量的矿产资源，而那些想要占有这些财富的人，将会面临激烈的竞争。 在远方还有其他的土地，那些我们从未有机会前往的地方，我们只能通过故事和传闻来了解它们。那里有更多的山脉，整个大陆仿佛都有一条巨大的岩石脊柱，直通天空；还有高原上广阔而深邃的湖泊，那里生活着种类更加繁多的鹰身女妖。 在更高的山区，也有与我们类似的冰封森林，那里充满了各种猎物，还有大量的黄金——这些黄金就沉淀在溪流中，你可以直接用双手将它们捡起来。而再往东去，就是丛林、温暖的平原，以及沿着蔚蓝大海分布的沿海地带。那里有巨大的牡蛎，还有色彩斑斓的西奥卡纳生物，它们的美丽程度甚至可以与裂谷地区的鲨鱼族相媲美。……”她叹息道，“要是我们当初直接选择旅行的话该多好。但我们当时有任务要为那里的卢米安信徒完成，等到我们觉得任务已经完成时，我们已经在那里待得太久了，也经历了太多苦难，再继续下去已经变得不可能了。 但我可以告诉你：沙漠之外确实存在着其他土地，其他地方也一样。这个世界上隐藏的秘密，甚至比那些古老的贝拉尔人所知道的还要多。 确实如此。 [flags.ANNIKA_TALK_TRAVEL||话虽如此，你还是能察觉到，她在描述那些细节时显得非常含糊其辞。 做了 在克萨纳帕与阿里亚娜的土地上。 也许你应该问问她，她是否有关于这件事的战斗经历或故事。]

Well, not yet, anyway. ]"[var0| You [cait.fucked |lace your fingers in Cait's and give her a smooch |smile fondly at the beaming kitty in question, who's been your friend through thick and thin ]. "Maybe someday, when all this is over."] "Oh, there's not even a question about it!" Cait giggles. "We're going to have so much to show you." Then she turns to Anni: "So, you've been there?" |I guess we could start with Jassira! I don't... believe you've been, have you?" "[pc.isBimbo |Nuh-uh! But |No, never — although ] I do know [var1|many Jassirans living in the Marches|[flags.FARRAH_WAYFORT|a few Jassirans|someone from there]]. [pc.isBimbo |Wait." You pause. "Does that mean that y |Y ]ou have?" ] "Of course! I know it's not exactly the kind of climate you'd expect for, you know, a frost elf, but we're actually not that bad at dealing with the sun — here at home, whenever the clouds move off, the sun shining off all the snow and ice can be blinding. Our people were used to it even before most of us turned to Lumia. And as for the heat, well, that part's not so easy, but we can learn to manage." Anni takes hold of her cheek thoughtfully. "That said, Jassirans themselves know the value of staying in the shade as much as possible." [party.has cait |"Absolutely." Your kitty companion exaggeratedly wipes some nonexistent sweat off her brow. "So, what were you doing in Jassira, anyway? I don't remember ever hearing about valkyries spending much time back home." "We didn't — not for long, anyway. We were on our way to somewhere else." |"[pc.dcb |No shit. You probably don't last long down there if you don't." You yawn. "So, why were you actually there? |I bet." You manage a low whistle. "Anything in particular you were doing there? |I guess it'd be cooler there for sure! Makes it super tough to work on a tan, though. Gotta get those rays on vacay!" Then you frown. "Wait, were you on vacay? Or were you, like, there for some other reason? ]" [pc.isBimbo |The seneschal shakes her head, smiling. "Oh, not a vacation. We were on our way to someplace else. |"Stopping in on our way to go somewhere else, honestly. ] Jassira was beautiful, but it wasn't the reason we crossed the ocean." ] "Beyond Jassira? I thought it was all[pc.isBimbo |, like ]... more desert.[pc.bg scholar | Nobody's been able to go beyond the desert in hundreds of years. All we've got are myths like 'The Wonders Beyond the Sands' and a few disconnected stories. ][var0| Or... wait. Were you just going up the coast, to where Cait's family was from?]" "[pc.bg scholar |We were indeed going beyond the desert," Anni confirms, grinning. "And yes, some of those stories are more than just stories. |Not quite just desert," Anni corrects. "There used to be old myths about what lay beyond the sands. Most of them aren't true. Some, though... some are. ] The great trackless dunes extend for many days' travel, and few who can't fly can make the journey, given how few oases there are. There is no regular trade, as far as I know, no ancient caravanserais for travelers to shelter in. It's truly [silly |an empty quarter of the world |the most empty land I've ever seen ]. Beyond the dunes, for those lucky few who can find the way and survive the trip, lies the high desert, and then the mountains, each a difficult journey in itself. But on the other side of the mountains, there are green rolling uplands leading down to enormous river valleys, lush forests, actual rain. The people there in the uplands and the alluvium call their home the land of a thousand cities. I... didn't have the time to count," she laughs, "but whenever my sisters and I were flying, we could see many built-up places, walled settlements, bustling marketplaces." [party.has atugia |"Wow," Tui breathes. "I've read books about this[pc.bg scholar | too ], but never actually met anyone who'd been there. What was it like? Nothing I've ever read gave many details — at least, not reliable ones." |That's enough to raise your eyebrow. "[pc.dcb |You're pulling my [pc.hasRealCock |dick |leg ]. |Wow. |Gosh! ] [pc.bg scholar |You actually made it to the civ[pc.isBimbo |... sevulla... people |ilization ] beyond the sands. |A whole civ[pc.isBimbo |... sevulla... whole bunch of people |ilization ] and no one knows about [pc.isBimbo |them |it ]? ]" ] "There's more than one civilization out there, and their peoples are very similar to those of the south: orcs, humans, catfolk, and more. First beyond the mountains is Ariana, a vast land with a proud harpy queen. She — if she still rules, at any rate, because this journey was decades ago — claims descent from the majestic bird-women the Arianans worshiped as gods long ago, before they changed their ways and came to honor the Seven. Quick-slithering snake-folk, manticores, 'taurs with the lower bodies of sharp-clawed lions — all mingle in the markets there with salamanders, humans, and elves. "How does one sum up whole cultures from first impressions? Hmm. They burn a local sweet-smelling seed for good luck, they never turn their backs on each other, and whenever they tell you 'no', they always make a tutting sound with their tongue." She tries to imitate the tongue-click: "A little like that. Goddess, it's been ages. Oh, and they don't shy away from praising those they admire. There are carved images in the walls of the mountains that honor heroic panther-warriors of times past, but the greatest rock reliefs of all are reserved for the queen and her avian ancestors." [party.has agnimitra |"Huh. Harpy queens?" Agnimitra frowns. "I can't... remember ever traveling beyond the Jassiran desert, but that... that doesn't mean much at this point. Did they — not just the queens, but any harpies you saw over there — have red feathers?" "When I was there, the queen did not. I don't really remember if I saw any other red-feathered harpies... but what I do remember is that most of the harpies there had more, mmm, elaborate plumage than the harpies around here. If you're related, it would have to be very far back." The valkyrie spreads her hands. "I don't know if they have stories about you; it's not something I thought to ask about. But I do know that the Arianans, harpy and otherwise, use fire magic in their worship and everyday lives a great deal. I wouldn't be surprised if you made a home there at one time." "Neither would I." Her eyes look away at something else for a long time before she starts to speak again. "I — I don't know if I want to know, at this point. Maybe... sorry, I don't want to interrupt the story. What else did you find?" |[agni.recruited|Huh. You wonder if Agnimitra's related to that queen, or any of the other Arianan harpies, somehow. You wouldn't put it past her.|Wow. That's quite the variety.] ] [party.has agnimitra|The encouraging smile Anni was wearing droops a little bit, but she restores it quickly enough. "Well, b|"B]eyond Ariana is Xenaspa, nestled in an even higher mountain range than the one separating Ariana from the desert. In those cities, rife with intrigue, there are elven warriors who claim descent from lost Belharan armies, antlike myrmarcs with engineering talent to match anything in Khor'minos, nagas of great age and wisdom, roc-riders like the avanai of the Rift, long-necked traders from a land I'd never heard of before, and more great leothran-like felines, striped and orange with tremendous fangs. To govern them all, a great code of laws stands in the marketplace of Ortosina, one of the cities we visited, written in a dozen languages; one of them looks like a very, very old Belharan script which seems to call the city 'Ediveia [silly |Eschate |the Furthest ].' Some of the people there truly did have ancestors in your lands, and one of the languages they speak isn't that far away from Belharan itself. That's how we were able to get by." You hold your tongue, not wanting to interrupt too much, but it's kind of amazing to think of how many places Belharans ended up during the imperial era. How many other undiscovered places have bits and pieces of their — your — culture even to this day? "Goddess, the marvels of Xenaspa..." Besides, Anni's on a roll. Why stop her? "Like the myrmarcs — the things they can engineer, the wonders they can build, simply have to be seen to be believed. These ones were different than the ones in southern Belhar, at least as far as I know. But like their Belharan cousins, they mine vast amounts of gold[silly |, just like Herodotos said! He wasn't lying! He just got the size of the ants wrong ]. Between myrmarcs and dust elves, Xenaspa has mines to rival Khor'minos, if not surpass it. And, unique to the great mountains that ring Xenaspa, they also mine a mysterious, beautiful blue stone that can be used in art, sculpture, and even makeup. "The earth's bounty commands princely sums from the traders of a multitude of lands, but the Xenaspans keep the best for themselves, using it to decorate colossal temples to the Seven to rival any in Belhar. I remember the sanctuary to Nareva in Amoltos, with its vast libraries overseen by gorgeous, sinuous naga priestesses, where local gold-flecked blue was worked into the traditional black and white decorations so beautifully..." Then she holds up her hands. "I don't want to exaggerate too much — Ortosina, Gapakoana, Amoltos, and the other cities we saw weren't literally made of gold or anything. But Xenaspa is a populous and wealthy land, with fertile soil and great stores of minerals, and those who enjoy its riches face steep competition to control them. "There are other lands beyond, places we were never able to visit, and of which we only heard stories and rumors. More mountains, like the whole continent has a great rocky spine stretching up to the sky. Plateaus with vast, deep lakes, home to an even wider variety of harpyfolk. Frozen forests not unlike ours even higher up in the mountains, full of game and so much gold that it sits in the creeks and streams there for you to just pick up with your bare hands. And even further east: jungles, warm plains, coastlands along a beautiful blue sea full of enormous oysters and siorcanna in a riot of colors that rival the shark-folk here in the rift..." She sighs. "Would that we could have simply traveled instead. But we had a task to complete for the Lumian faithful there, and by the time we felt it complete, we had already stayed too long and suffered too much to continue. But I can tell you this: there are indeed lands beyond the desert, and more elsewhere. This world has more secrets in it than even the old Belharans knew." That it does. [flags.ANNIKA_TALK_TRAVEL||That said, you do notice that she was very sketchy on the details of what she did in the lands of Xenaspa and Ariana. Maybe you should ask if she has a war story about it.] '

rows.original: "Ah," she murmurs, her grin turning to a bit of a grimace. "There's this one. I don't know if I can convince you that it really happened, but it did. I was there." [pc.dcb |"Really. A no-shit-there-I-was story from a valkyrie." "Oh, I like that," Anni laughs in her slightly singsongy, accented voice. "No shit, there I was. That's perfect! Vulgar, but perfect." "Yep. So: the story?" |"I wouldn't expect a Lumian warrior to begin her story with 'no shit, there I was'." You raise an eyebrow. "Must be a wild one." "Oh, I like that," Anni laughs in her slightly singsongy, accented voice. "No shit, there I was. That's perfect! Vulgar, but perfect." "What can I say? I've got my moments. But the story?" |"Gosh," you whisper. "I bet you've seen some really crazy things! But I'd believe the stories if you're telling them, Anni." "Aw. Thank you, sweetheart. I appreciate that." "Hee hee. Of course! Sooo? What's the story?" ] "Right. This was about ten, eleven years back. A particularly nasty group of Wraith-touched monsters was attacking outlying minotaur settlements, and I was sent to help figure out what was going on and work with the legions to push the enemy back. Turned out that it was a bigger job than we were expecting. Hundreds of the things swarming through the mountains, seeking all manner of openings and trying to find the minotaurs' weak spots. They raided and raided and finally the minos got so fed up with trying to defend everything that they launched an attack to try to snuff out the Wraithslaves' camps. It was a tough call, one with no easy solutions. You need to attack to win, but were these raids the bait for a trap?" "[pc.isBimbo |That does sound like a toughy." You frown. "War choices are haaaard. |Not the easiest of decisions to make ]." "[pc.isBimbo |They certainly are, sweetie. |No. ] Fortunately, I wasn't the one who had to make it — and I was able to send for backup. More valkyries and, once we figured out the extent of the task before us, more legions, too. We were all to take separate tunnels and unite on the battlefield, far south of Khor'minos at the ruin of an ancient Minoan queen's palace." [party.comp brint brienne |"Oh hey," Brint chuckles. "I've heard this story before. It's not just you who's got a 'no shit, there I was' story about this fight. Feels like half the legion does, too. I won't spoil the details — they're too fuckin' good." Annika nods gently. "I appreciate it... and yes, I'm sure they do. Enough craziness for a pale elven lifetime. |"Oooh!" Brienne says excitedly. "I know people who were there — well, other people who were there, counting you. The stories they had were crazy; I can't wait to hear what yours is! Don't worry, I won't spoil things for [pc.name]." Annika nods indulgently. "I appreciate it, sweetie. It's not an experience that anyone who went through it will soon forget. |You think you remember hearing about something like that somewhere, but everything you heard was shy on details. "Good," Annika says, the corner of her mouth curving up just a little bit more. "That way you won't be spoiled on what's to come. ] I spent my day with the Second Legion, marching hard, or in my case flying fast to cut off the Wraithslaves' retreat. The Minoan legate, a big, gruff bull by the name of Hillus, had his blood up and wanted to get into the fight as soon as possible, the better to save the forces fighting on the main front. He was a good soldier and a better leader, one who could claim his warriors' respect through a long history of service and comradeship, and they marched as fast and as far as he could ever reasonably ask for. We emerged from the tunnels right on the Wraiths' flank while the creatures' attention was mostly far away with the other legions. With the creatures distracted, it wasn't hard for us to push into the ruins of a village right astride their only escape tunnel from the fighting elsewhere in the caverns. "Which meant that we were right in the path of about half their army as soon as they realized that something was amiss." [pc.isBimbo |"Oh no! So they all came straight at you?" |"Wow. They just threw everything they could take away from the fight at the front right at you." ] Anni nods. "Yes. The bulls fought hard. They gave ground like misers, even at the cost of their lives, and for good reason; if we could hold the village, we would be the cork in the bottleneck. The Wraith-touched wouldn't be able to get out, and we could keep them from preying on any other of the good people of the deeps. So the thralls came on again and again, hurling magic against the shields to break the formation, howling with uncanny ferocity, searching for any vulnerability they could find. Every time their charge failed, we'd lose a few more of our warriors, and down the tunnel, our foes would rally up again with the desperate mindlessness that they're so known for." "After three hours, even though the ground before us was strewn with monstrous corpses, we were perilously low on uninjured warriors. Half of the soldiers still alive couldn't stand up to take their place in the line. The charges had whittled away at our numbers, little by little, and the next one would leave us unable to block the tunnel for certain." Her eyes lose a little of their glow, gaining shadows entirely appropriate for the scene. "By then, of course, Hillus had been in the line with us for several charges; there was no point in staying out of the battle, no orders to issue that wouldn't be superfluous, and everyone simply had to do their part. And when the Wraithslaves formed up again, he gritted his teeth just like we did and prepared to do what he needed to do. "It was in that charge, amid the crashing of line against line, the swirling of the melee as the formation started to lose cohesion, that Hillus slew a being that had once been a lupine, paused, listened, then shouted as loud as he could that we were saved, that everything was going to be all right. And it was. Because at the back of the pile, behind the thralls, I could finally see the other legions' horns, and the glow of my sisters' wings." [party.has arona |"Not a bad fuckin' job," Arona chuckles. |"[pc.swornGod lumia nareva keros |By Lumia |By Nareva |By Keros |Gods ], that was close." ] "It was," she agrees, before pausing. "And seconds later, a chimaera killed him." [pc.isDK |"Oh, fuck that." You shake your head. "You're pulling my [pc.hasRealCock |dick |leg ]." |"What?" you yelp. "There's no way[pc.isBimbo |! |. ]" ] Her face hardens again, all deadly serious. "Yes. Had someone sung of it, I'd have thought it too contrived to believe. But it genuinely happened, almost as fast as a blink. He wasn't distracted or anything; the chimaera simply landed a blow that he couldn't get up from — and he didn't. Only those of us who stood near him knew. Nobody else found out until we counted the dead and dying at the end of the battle." [pc.dcb |"Sounds like a fuckin' bloodbath. Ah, well. He and his guys won. That's all that really matters." |You close your eyes pensively. "He and his soldiers didn't die in vain, though." |"Oh, Anni." You reach out for her shoulder. "That's awful." ] "[pc.dcb |That was the important thing |No, he didn't |It... it was, sweetie. But at least we won ]," Annika says, grimly shaking her head. "With us in front and the main army behind, few of the Wraithslaves escaped. It was as close to a clean sweep as anyone's likely to get in war. As far as outcomes go, it's the one you hope for. If only it could have been purchased with fewer lives, but, well..." She closes her eyes, sighs, and slowly opens them again. "There are a lot of things that I wish could have been purchased at a lower price in blood."
rows.translation: 啊，”她轻声说道，脸上的笑容渐渐变成了苦笑，“有这样一件事……我不知道能否说服你相信它确实发生过，但事实就是如此。我当时就在现场。 [pc.dcb |真的啊，一个来自女武神的真实故事。” “哦，我喜欢这个，”安妮用她那带着轻微口音的歌唱般的声音笑着说，“真的啊，事情就是这样的。太棒了！虽然有点粗俗，但确实很棒。” “没错，那么，这个故事到底是怎样的呢？ |我真没想到一个卢米安战士会用‘果然如此，我就在那儿’这样的开头来讲述自己的故事。”你挑了挑眉毛，“她肯定是个很特别的人。” “哦，我喜欢这个说法，”安妮用她那带着些口音、略带歌唱性的声音笑着说，“果然如此，我就在那儿。太完美了！虽然有点粗俗，但确实很完美。” “我还能说什么呢？我也有我的闪光点嘛。不过这个故事…… |天哪，”你轻声说道，“我敢打赌你一定见过一些非常离奇的事情吧！不过如果你是亲口告诉我的，我相信你的话，安妮。” “哎呀，谢谢你，亲爱的。我真的很感激。” “呵呵，当然啦！那么，快说说吧，是什么故事呢？ ] 没错。那是大约十到十一年前的事了。有一群被‘怨灵’影响的怪物正在袭击米诺陶洛斯的边远定居点，我被派去协助调查事情的真相，并与军队一起将敌人击退。 结果发现，这项任务比我们预想的要复杂得多。有成百上千的生物在山间四处游荡，它们试图寻找各种入口，进而找到那些米诺陶洛斯的弱点。它们不断地发动攻击，最终米诺陶洛斯们受够了不断防御这些攻击，于是决定发起反击，试图消灭那些“怨灵奴隶”的营地。 这确实是一个艰难的决定，没有简单的解决办法。你必须进攻才能取胜，但这些袭击难道只是某个陷阱的诱饵吗？[pc.isBimbo |那确实听起来是个棘手的问题。”你皱起了眉头，“在战争中做出选择确实非常困难。 |这确实不是一个容易做出的决定。 ]." "[pc.isBimbo |他们当然是，亲爱的。 |不。 ] 幸运的是，并不是我必须去完成这项任务——我能够派人去寻求支援。我们调来了更多的女武神，而且一旦弄清了眼前任务的艰巨程度，还召集了更多的军团。我们所有人都会通过不同的通道前往，在霍尔米诺斯南部那座古代米诺斯女王宫殿的废墟处会合，然后在战场上共同作战。 [party.comp brint brienne |哦，嘿，”布林特轻笑道，“这个故事我以前听过。不止你有一个关于这场战斗的‘果然如此’的故事，感觉半数军团成员都有类似的经历。我就不透露细节了——那些故事实在太他妈精彩了。” 安妮卡轻轻点了点头：“我很感激……没错，我相信他们的故事确实都很精彩。对于一个苍白精灵来说，这样的疯狂经历已经够够一辈子的了。 |哦哦哦！”布蕾妮兴奋地叫道，“我认识一些当时在场的人——嗯， 其他 包括你在内，那些在场的人。他们讲述的故事简直太离奇了；我迫不及待想听听你的故事是什么！别担心，我不会把剧情透露出来的。 [pc.name]安妮卡宽容地点了点头。“我很感激你，亲爱的。这种经历，任何经历过的人都不会轻易忘记的。 |你觉得自己好像在某个地方听说过类似的事情，但当时听到的描述都缺乏细节。 “很好，”安妮卡说道，她的嘴角又微微上扬了一些。“这样你就不会提前知道后续会发生什么了。 ] 我一整天都在与第二军团一起行军，要么是拼命奔跑，要么是迅速飞行，目的是切断那些“幽灵奴隶”的退路。米诺斯的使者名叫希卢斯，他是个身材高大、性格粗犷的人，他迫不及待地想要投入战斗，因为只有这样才能更好地帮助主战线的部队。 他不仅是一名出色的士兵，更是一位优秀的领导者。凭借长期以来的服役经历与战友情谊，他赢得了战士们的尊敬；而他要求的行军速度与距离，战士们也总是能够毫无怨言地遵守。当我们从隧道中出来时，那些怪物们的注意力大多都集中在其他军团那里，因此我们正好从它们的侧翼发动了攻击。 趁着那些生物们分心之际，我们轻松地进入了那个村庄的废墟——那里正是它们从洞穴其他地方的战斗中逃出来的唯一通道。 “这意味着，一旦它们察觉到有什么不对劲，我们就会正好挡在它们大约一半军队的去路上。" [pc.isBimbo |哦不！原来他们是这样的…… 所有 是直接朝你冲过来的吗？ |哇，他们把所有能在战斗中获取的优势都集中用在了你身上。 ] 安妮点了点头。“没错。那些公牛们战斗得非常顽强。它们宁愿牺牲自己的生命也不肯退缩，因为这样做确实有意义——如果我们能够守住这个村庄，我们就相当于堵住了这个‘瓶颈’。那些被‘怨灵’影响的人就无法逃走了，我们也能够阻止它们去伤害其他生活在深处的善良人们。 那些奴仆一次又一次地发起攻击，用魔法冲击我们的护盾，试图打破我们的阵型，它们发出令人毛骨悚然的凶狠叫声，拼命寻找任何可以利用的弱点。每当它们的进攻失败，我们的战士们就会又有几人倒下。而在隧道的另一端，我们的敌人会以它们那众所周知的疯狂与执着，再次集结起来，继续发动攻击。" 三个小时后，尽管我们面前的地面上散落着无数惨烈的尸体，但我们手中未受伤的战士已经所剩无几。还有半数幸存的士兵甚至无法站立，更无法加入战斗队伍。连续不断的攻击正在一点点地消耗我们的兵力，下次进攻来临时，我们肯定已经无法再阻挡那条隧道了。她的眼睛失去了原有的光彩，蒙上了一层与此刻场景极为相称的阴影。当然，到那时，希勒斯已经和我们一起参加了好几场战斗；继续置身事外毫无意义，也没有任何命令是多余的，每个人都必须尽自己的一份力。 当那些被怨灵控制的奴隶们再次集结起来时，他也和我们一样咬紧牙关，准备做好自己必须做的事情。 就在那种混乱之中——在队伍接连溃败、近战厮杀声此起彼伏、阵型开始瓦解的时候——希卢斯杀死了那个曾经是狼人的生物。他停了下来，倾听片刻，然后用尽全力大声呼喊，告诉我们我们得救了，一切都会好起来的。而事实确实如此。因为在人群的最后方，在那些被奴役的士兵们身后，我终于看到了其他军团的旗帜，也看到了我的姐妹们翅膀散发出的光芒。 [party.has arona |干得不错嘛，”阿罗纳笑着说。 |"[pc.swornGod lumia nareva keros |由卢米亚出品 |作者：纳雷瓦 |作者：Keros |神明们 ]真是好险啊。 ] 是的，”她同意道，然后停顿了一下，“几秒钟后，一只奇美拉杀死了他。 [pc.isDK |哦，去他的。”你摇摇头，“你简直是在耍我。 [pc.hasRealCock |dick |腿 ]." |什么？”你惊叫道，“不可能吧……[pc.isBimbo |! |. ]" ] 她的脸色再次变得严肃起来，语气十分认真：“没错。如果有人告诉我这件事，我肯定会觉得它太牵强、难以置信。但这一切确实发生了，速度快得几乎让人眨眼间就结束了。他并没有分心，也没有受到任何干扰；那只奇美拉给了他一击，让他根本无法站起来——而他确实也没有站起来。只有我们那些站在他附近的人才知道这件事。直到战斗结束后我们清点伤亡人数时，其他人才得知了真相。 [pc.dcb |听起来简直就是一场血腥的大屠杀。唉，算了。他和他的团队赢了，这才是最重要的。 |你若有所思地闭上了眼睛。“不过，他和他的士兵们的牺牲并没有白费。 |哦，安妮。”你伸手拍了拍她的肩膀，“那太糟糕了。 ] "[pc.dcb |这才是最重要的。 |不，他并没有。 |它……它曾经是，亲爱的。但至少我们赢了。 ]是啊，”安妮卡苦涩地摇着头说道，“我们在前方，主力部队在后方，几乎没有一个‘幽灵奴隶’能够逃脱。这样的胜利，在战争中已经算是非常圆满了。就结果而言，这正是我们希望看到的。只不过，要是能用更少的生命来换取这样的胜利该多好……不过，唉……”她闭上眼睛，叹了口气，又缓缓睁开。“有很多东西，我真的希望能用更少的代价来获得。
rows.raw: ' "Ah," she murmurs, her grin turning to a bit of a grimace. "There's this one. I don't know if I can convince you that it really happened, but it did. I was there." [pc.dcb |"Really. A no-shit-there-I-was story from a valkyrie." "Oh, I like that," Anni laughs in her slightly singsongy, accented voice. "No shit, there I was. That's perfect! Vulgar, but perfect." "Yep. So: the story?" |"I wouldn't expect a Lumian warrior to begin her story with 'no shit, there I was'." You raise an eyebrow. "Must be a wild one." "Oh, I like that," Anni laughs in her slightly singsongy, accented voice. "No shit, there I was. That's perfect! Vulgar, but perfect." "What can I say? I've got my moments. But the story?" |"Gosh," you whisper. "I bet you've seen some really crazy things! But I'd believe the stories if you're telling them, Anni." "Aw. Thank you, sweetheart. I appreciate that." "Hee hee. Of course! Sooo? What's the story?" ] "Right. This was about ten, eleven years back. A particularly nasty group of Wraith-touched monsters was attacking outlying minotaur settlements, and I was sent to help figure out what was going on and work with the legions to push the enemy back. Turned out that it was a bigger job than we were expecting. Hundreds of the things swarming through the mountains, seeking all manner of openings and trying to find the minotaurs' weak spots. They raided and raided and finally the minos got so fed up with trying to defend everything that they launched an attack to try to snuff out the Wraithslaves' camps. It was a tough call, one with no easy solutions. You need to attack to win, but were these raids the bait for a trap?" "[pc.isBimbo |That does sound like a toughy." You frown. "War choices are haaaard. |Not the easiest of decisions to make ]." "[pc.isBimbo |They certainly are, sweetie. |No. ] Fortunately, I wasn't the one who had to make it — and I was able to send for backup. More valkyries and, once we figured out the extent of the task before us, more legions, too. We were all to take separate tunnels and unite on the battlefield, far south of Khor'minos at the ruin of an ancient Minoan queen's palace." [party.comp brint brienne |"Oh hey," Brint chuckles. "I've heard this story before. It's not just you who's got a 'no shit, there I was' story about this fight. Feels like half the legion does, too. I won't spoil the details — they're too fuckin' good." Annika nods gently. "I appreciate it... and yes, I'm sure they do. Enough craziness for a pale elven lifetime. |"Oooh!" Brienne says excitedly. "I know people who were there — well, other people who were there, counting you. The stories they had were crazy; I can't wait to hear what yours is! Don't worry, I won't spoil things for [pc.name]." Annika nods indulgently. "I appreciate it, sweetie. It's not an experience that anyone who went through it will soon forget. |You think you remember hearing about something like that somewhere, but everything you heard was shy on details. "Good," Annika says, the corner of her mouth curving up just a little bit more. "That way you won't be spoiled on what's to come. ] I spent my day with the Second Legion, marching hard, or in my case flying fast to cut off the Wraithslaves' retreat. The Minoan legate, a big, gruff bull by the name of Hillus, had his blood up and wanted to get into the fight as soon as possible, the better to save the forces fighting on the main front. He was a good soldier and a better leader, one who could claim his warriors' respect through a long history of service and comradeship, and they marched as fast and as far as he could ever reasonably ask for. We emerged from the tunnels right on the Wraiths' flank while the creatures' attention was mostly far away with the other legions. With the creatures distracted, it wasn't hard for us to push into the ruins of a village right astride their only escape tunnel from the fighting elsewhere in the caverns. "Which meant that we were right in the path of about half their army as soon as they realized that something was amiss." [pc.isBimbo |"Oh no! So they all came straight at you?" |"Wow. They just threw everything they could take away from the fight at the front right at you." ] Anni nods. "Yes. The bulls fought hard. They gave ground like misers, even at the cost of their lives, and for good reason; if we could hold the village, we would be the cork in the bottleneck. The Wraith-touched wouldn't be able to get out, and we could keep them from preying on any other of the good people of the deeps. So the thralls came on again and again, hurling magic against the shields to break the formation, howling with uncanny ferocity, searching for any vulnerability they could find. Every time their charge failed, we'd lose a few more of our warriors, and down the tunnel, our foes would rally up again with the desperate mindlessness that they're so known for." "After three hours, even though the ground before us was strewn with monstrous corpses, we were perilously low on uninjured warriors. Half of the soldiers still alive couldn't stand up to take their place in the line. The charges had whittled away at our numbers, little by little, and the next one would leave us unable to block the tunnel for certain." Her eyes lose a little of their glow, gaining shadows entirely appropriate for the scene. "By then, of course, Hillus had been in the line with us for several charges; there was no point in staying out of the battle, no orders to issue that wouldn't be superfluous, and everyone simply had to do their part. And when the Wraithslaves formed up again, he gritted his teeth just like we did and prepared to do what he needed to do. "It was in that charge, amid the crashing of line against line, the swirling of the melee as the formation started to lose cohesion, that Hillus slew a being that had once been a lupine, paused, listened, then shouted as loud as he could that we were saved, that everything was going to be all right. And it was. Because at the back of the pile, behind the thralls, I could finally see the other legions' horns, and the glow of my sisters' wings." [party.has arona |"Not a bad fuckin' job," Arona chuckles. |"[pc.swornGod lumia nareva keros |By Lumia |By Nareva |By Keros |Gods ], that was close." ] "It was," she agrees, before pausing. "And seconds later, a chimaera killed him." [pc.isDK |"Oh, fuck that." You shake your head. "You're pulling my [pc.hasRealCock |dick |leg ]." |"What?" you yelp. "There's no way[pc.isBimbo |! |. ]" ] Her face hardens again, all deadly serious. "Yes. Had someone sung of it, I'd have thought it too contrived to believe. But it genuinely happened, almost as fast as a blink. He wasn't distracted or anything; the chimaera simply landed a blow that he couldn't get up from — and he didn't. Only those of us who stood near him knew. Nobody else found out until we counted the dead and dying at the end of the battle." [pc.dcb |"Sounds like a fuckin' bloodbath. Ah, well. He and his guys won. That's all that really matters." |You close your eyes pensively. "He and his soldiers didn't die in vain, though." |"Oh, Anni." You reach out for her shoulder. "That's awful." ] "[pc.dcb |That was the important thing |No, he didn't |It... it was, sweetie. But at least we won ]," Annika says, grimly shaking her head. "With us in front and the main army behind, few of the Wraithslaves escaped. It was as close to a clean sweep as anyone's likely to get in war. As far as outcomes go, it's the one you hope for. If only it could have been purchased with fewer lives, but, well..." She closes her eyes, sighs, and slowly opens them again. "There are a lot of things that I wish could have been purchased at a lower price in blood." '
