rows.original: "Flying is the kind of advantage that most foes can't match. Some Wraith-touched can do it, but very few. And we don't fight harpies very often." She grins. "That narrows the field quite a lot. You know what kind of defense is really good against people who can't fly and absolutely awful at people who can?" "Walls[pc.isBimbo |, of course! |. ]" You pause. "And ditches.[silly | Can't forget the ditches. 'Where's your ditch? You need to dig a ditch.' The historians would kill me if I forgot. ]" "Exactly," Anni says. "There's not always very much call for it, but whenever valkyries — or harpies — attack a walled enclosure, enemies usually aren't really prepared for it. And even if they are, a few archers or mages are things we can handle. When fortresses are defended against ground attackers, there are often what we call layers to the defense: ditches, defenders, berms, more defenders, moats, more defenders, walls, more defenders, more walls. It's not often you see layers like that against a flying attacker. About ten years back, we stormed the ruins of Vithblainn, an elven city that was held by Wraith-touched, and didn't lose a warrior." "Wow... wait." You frown. "You said 'not often'." She nods ruefully. "There's always an exception. Sixty or so years ago, one of the princesses of Belhar — Belhar the city, since they don't have much of an empire anymore — didn't like how the succession sorted out. She took a bunch of followers off to an old fortress, commandeered it, and started scheming to get the throne, or get it back, depending on who you believed about the inheritance. Normally, that's not our problem. We fight the corrupted. We don't intervene in things like succession disputes, no matter what the local law is. Buuuuut..." [pc.isBimbo |"That sounds like a big but! Hee hee. Big butt. Oooh! Did the princess have a big butt?" |"Let me guess," you say. "She thought that Wraiths would give her a leg up." ] "[pc.isBimbo |I... I don't know, dear. We never got to meet her. |No, actually. ] She was fiddling with [var0|the Waystone|a magical portal] in the fortress to try to sneak into the city the back way, but accidentally let in something... not a Wraith. The way the Astrida explained it, it was unchanneled elemental chaos? The upshot was that instead of Wraiths, what came through were spirits of fire, ice, lightning, and so on. The whole fortress melted from the inside out, had a massive column of flame reaching into the sky[silly | like it was some kind of superhero movie or something ], was surrounded by a huge storm. By the time anyone found out about it, the princess and her soldiers were dead or hollowed out by the elemental powers, and unbound, angry spirits had started coming through. They had an army's worth, which made it a task the Astrida knew they couldn't handle alone. So some of us — Hjörr, Tayann, Teniya, two dozen others — flew south to join them and the army of Prince Firmus, and tried to assault the place as quickly as we could. "The thing was, you know how I said that it's hard to layer defenses against someone who can fly? Not only did these spirits have a decent idea, they had the advantage of being surrounded by one of the worst lightning storms in history. It took several mages of Sorra to hold the weather down enough for us to be able to fly. And there was this... net, sort of, made from fire, not rope, that kept us from landing on top of the fortress. And the spirits even conjured little mantlets of ice and rock to protect them from missiles." She grimaces. "We tried to bounce the walls and a quarter of us got knocked out of the sky before even reaching the net. Some of the sisters who went down stayed down. We had to fall back and regroup, but not even the gods knew what they were bringing in through the shattered portal... and the longer it stayed open, the more time for gods-know-what to come in." [party.has viviane |Viv taps her chin thoughtfully. "I've heard of this sort of thing. In fact, I think I've heard of this very incident. It's exceedingly rare for elemental magic to manifest this way; usually it comes through summonings, not portals. A portal... well,[viv.isDemon | I suppose ] you would have had to close it[viv.isDemon | posthaste |, with no time to waste ]." |[pc.isBimbo |"Uh-oh! So you couldn't, like, wait around or anything?" |"You didn't think you had time to lay siege." It isn't a question. ] ] "We [pc.isBimbo |knew |knew ] we didn't have time," the valkyrie says grimly. Her ice-eyes cloud over with memory, then refocus on something that isn't you. "We couldn't break through the fire, not with everything inside attacking us. The best we could do was be a distraction. Normally, you want to build a mole, get more of your army up high so they can attack down onto the enemy's walls; we didn't have that option, either. So, after conferring with Prince Firmus, we headed back up and tried to keep the spirits busy while the Heartlanders and the mages scaled the wall with ladders, and other mages and soldiers hit the gates from the front, trying to burn them down with magic." "That sounds [pc.isBimbo |really really tough! |like doing it the hard way. ]" "Yes. Those spirits came from another realm, another plane of existence, and they came powerful and in the raw, not the weaker spirits sometimes used to enchant weapons. Even with the Astridas' magic tamping down the spirits' raw elemental force, we lost a lot of people. Clearing the wall opposed..." She shudders. It's a deeply weird thing to see her do that. "Flying out in full view of dozens of enemies trying to kill you, dodging and weaving and firing off magic whenever you can, over and over and over again, while soldiers die underneath you and your sisters fall out of the sky next to you and you don't even know if it's working — I wouldn't wish that kind of battle on anyone. "In the end, we made it atop the walls at great cost. The Astrida and a few of my other sisters managed to find the portal, once we destroyed the net. Whatever they found, however they killed it, whatever else they did... it worked. But we left a lot of dead and wounded on the grounds. Teniya..." Her voice breaks a little bit, then all the way, and she closes her eyes. [pc.dcb |[annika.kissed |You reach for her arm and try to force some understanding into your hard eyes. "Sorry, Anni." Then, a beat later: "She sounds like the kind of badass who wouldn't have minded paying that price, though." |"That's what war is," you say cuttingly. "You do what you need to do." ] |[annika.kissed |You offer Anni a hug and a quiet "I'm sorry," and it seems like that helps. She still needs a little time, though, so you wait |Apart from a quiet "I'm sorry," you give her a little time, waiting ] until she opens her eyes again before you ask the follow-up question. "Do you have any regrets?" Then you pause again, this time more briefly. "Would she have?" |"Awww, Anni." You offer her a reassuring hug and plenty of pats on the back, quiet whispers of "I'm sorry, sweetie," and plenty of time. It takes a little while for her eyes to open again, and you wait as long as she needs. Only after she does manage to open them and nod do you keep asking: "Do... do you think there's another way it could've turned out better?" ] Annika shakes her head. "[pc.isDK |You're right. ]This was how it had to be done. The things we had to do, the things we couldn't allow — we didn't have time to lay siege, and there weren't any clever solutions that would actually help in the time we had. Prince Firmus understood what was at stake, and if any of us had been in command instead of him, we would have made the same choice. You can't win battles against enemy armies without fighting; against a prepared enemy, you can't win fights without taking losses.[silly | There's no One Weird Trick that'll win battles the clever way. ] You just have to adapt. All of us know it. All of us understand it." She breathes out again, long and slow, before finishing her thought. "A hundred years of it just... wear, is all."
rows.translation: 飞行是大多数敌人根本无法拥有的优势。有些被‘怨灵’影响的人也能飞行，但这样的人寥寥无几。而且我们也不经常与女妖战斗。”她笑着说，“这样一来，可选的对象就大大减少了。你知道，对于那些不会飞行、也无法飞行的人来说，什么样的防御措施才是真正有效的吧？而对于那些会飞行的人来说，这种防御措施就完全不起作用了。” “城墙。[pc.isBimbo |当然可以！ |. ]你停下了动作，然后离开了。[silly | 可不能忘了那些沟渠。“你的沟渠在哪里？你得挖一条沟渠才行。”如果我忘了这件事，历史学家们非得骂死我不可。 ]正是这样，”安妮说道，“虽然这种情况并不经常发生，但每当女武神或女妖攻击有围墙的围场时，敌人通常都毫无准备。而且，即使他们有所准备，我们也完全有能力对付那些弓箭手或法师。 当堡垒遭到地面攻击者的进攻时，防御措施通常会呈现出多层结构：壕沟、防御者、土堤、更多的防御者、护城河、更多的防御者、城墙、更多的防御者，还有更多的城墙。然而，面对空中攻击者时，却很少见到这种多层防御体系。 大约十年前，我们冲进了维思布莱恩的废墟——那是一座被怨灵侵蚀的精灵城市，但我们没有损失任何一名战士。 “哇……等等。”你皱起了眉头，“你刚才说的是‘并不经常’吧。” 她遗憾地点了点头：“总是会有例外的。 大约六十年前，贝尔哈尔城的一位公主——由于他们的帝国早已不复存在，所以这里指的是贝尔哈尔城——对当时的王位继承安排感到不满。她带着一群追随者来到一座古老的堡垒，占领了那里，然后开始密谋夺取王位，或者说是试图夺回属于她的王位，具体是哪种情况，这取决于人们对继承权问题的不同看法。 通常来说，那并不属于我们需要处理的问题。我们的职责是对抗那些被腐蚀的人或势力，而不会介入诸如继承权纠纷之类的事件，无论当地的法律规定如何。但是…… [pc.isBimbo |那听起来可真是个大问题呢！呵呵，就是那个‘大屁股’的问题。哦哦，公主的屁股是不是很大呢？ |让我猜猜看，”你说，“她以为那些幽灵会帮她一把吧。 ] "[pc.isBimbo |我……我不知道，亲爱的。我们从来都没有见过她。 |不，其实不是这样。 ] 她正在摆弄着什么。 [var0|路标石|一个神奇的传送门] 他们试图从堡垒的背面秘密进入城市，但却意外地引入了某种东西……并不是怨灵。按照阿斯特里达的解释，那是一种未被控制的元素混沌。结果就是，原本应该出现的怨灵，被火之灵、冰之灵、雷电之灵等等取代了。整个堡垒从内部开始被侵蚀，最终有一道巨大的火焰柱直冲云霄。[silly | 就好像这是一部超级英雄电影之类的。 ]那座城堡被一场巨大的风暴所包围。等到有人发现这一情况时，公主和她的士兵们早已死亡，或者被那些自然力量彻底摧毁；而那些失去束缚、充满愤怒的灵魂也开始涌现出来。它们的数量之多，相当于一支军队的规模，因此阿斯特拉达明白，他们单凭自己的力量是无法应对这一危机的。 所以我们中的一些人——Hjörr、Tayann、Teniya，还有另外二十几个人——飞往南方，加入了他们以及Firmus王子的军队，试图尽快发起攻击。 “问题就在于，就像我之前说的，对于那些会飞的人来说，要设置多层防御确实非常困难，对吧？ 这些精灵不仅想法巧妙，而且还处于历史上最猛烈的雷暴之中。多亏了索拉的几位法师设法控制住了天气，我们才得以顺利飞行。 还有那么一张……由火焰而非绳索构成的网，它阻止了我们降落在堡垒上方。那些精灵甚至制造出由冰块和岩石构成的小护盾，用来保护他们免受导弹的攻击。”她皱了皱眉头，“我们试图撞击那些墙壁，结果有四分之一的人在甚至还没碰到那张网之前，就被从空中击落了。 那些下山去的姐妹们中，有一些…… 留在了那里。 我们不得不撤退并重新整编队伍，但就连众神也不知道，那些通过那扇破碎的传送门进入的东西究竟是什么……而那扇传送门持续敞开的時間越长，那些未知的东西进入我们的世界的机会就越多。 [party.has viviane |薇芙若有所思地轻敲着下巴：“我听说过这种事情。事实上，我觉得我曾经听说过 exactly 这一事件。元素魔法以这种方式显现实在是极为罕见；通常情况下，它是通过召唤术而不是传送门来实现的。传送门……嗯，[viv.isDemon | 我想应该是吧。 ] 你当时就必须关闭它。[viv.isDemon | 尽快 |没有时间可以浪费了。 ]." |[pc.isBimbo |哦不！所以你没办法等着看后续发展之类的吗？ |你居然以为自己有时间去围攻他们？”这并不是在提问。 ] ] 我们 [pc.isBimbo |知道 |知道 ] 我们没有时间了，”女武神面容阴沉地说道。她的冰蓝色眼睛中浮现出回忆的阴影，但很快又将注意力转移到了与你无关的事物上。“我们无法突破那团火焰，因为里面的那些东西正在攻击我们。我们能做的，只是设法转移它们的注意力罢了。 通常情况下，你会选择建造地道，让更多的军队隐藏在高处，从而从上方攻击敌人的城墙；但我们也没有这个选择。因此，在与菲尔穆斯王子商议之后，我们重新返回战场，尽力让士兵们保持战斗状态，与此同时，那些来自心脏之地的战士和法师们正用梯子攀爬城墙，而其他的法师和士兵们则从正面攻击城门，试图用魔法将其烧毁。听起来不错。 [pc.isBimbo |真的太难了！ |宁愿走艰难的道路。 ]是的。那些灵魂来自另一个领域，另一个存在维度，它们降临时拥有强大的力量，与那些常被用来为武器施加魔力的弱小灵魂完全不同。即便阿斯特里达斯的魔法削弱了那些灵魂原始的元素力量，我们还是失去了很多人。 冲破那道障碍……”她颤抖着说道。看到她做出这样的举动，实在是一件非常奇怪的事情。“在数十名试图杀死你的敌人眼前飞驰，不断躲避攻击、抓住机会释放魔法，一遍又一遍地重复这样的动作，而你的士兵们正在下面牺牲，你的姐妹们也在你身边从天而降，而你甚至不知道自己的行动是否有效——我真不希望任何人经历这样的战斗。 最终，我们付出了巨大的代价才成功登上了那些城墙。在摧毁了那张网之后，阿斯特丽达和我的其他几位姐妹终于找到了那个传送门。无论她们找到了什么，无论她们是如何消灭那些东西的，无论她们还做了什么…… 成功了。但是战场上留下了许多伤亡者。Teniya……她的声音有些颤抖，最终彻底崩溃了，她闭上了眼睛。 [pc.dcb |[annika.kissed |你伸手抓住她的手臂，试图用坚定的目光让她明白你的意思。“对不起，安妮。”过了一会儿，你又补充道：“不过，她听起来像是那种不会介意付出这样的代价的人。 |战争就是这样的，”你冷冷地说道，“你必须做自己该做的事。 ] |[annika.kissed |你拥抱了安妮，轻声说道“对不起”，看来这确实有所帮助。不过她仍然需要一些时间，于是你选择等待。 |除了简短地说一句“对不起”，你给她一些时间，静静地等待着。 ] 直到她再次睁开眼睛，你才接着问道：“你有没有什么后悔的事？”然后你再次停顿了一下，这次停顿的时间更短：“她会有吗？ |哎呀，安妮。”你给了她一个安慰的拥抱，轻轻拍着她的背，低声说着“对不起，宝贝”，并且给了她足够的时间。过了好一会儿，她的眼睛才再次睁开，你耐心地等待着她准备好。直到她终于睁开眼睛并点了点头，你才继续问道：“你……你觉得有没有其他办法可以让事情发展得更好呢？ ] 安妮卡摇了摇头。[pc.isDK |你说得对。 ]就必须这样做。我们必须完成那些任务，那些绝不能放弃的事情——我们没有时间进行长期围剿，也没有任何巧妙的解决办法能在有限的时间内真正起到作用。菲尔穆斯王子明白其中的关键所在，如果换作我们中的任何一个人来指挥，也会做出同样的选择。不与敌人交战，就无法赢得战斗；面对一个有备而来的敌人，不承受任何损失，就根本不可能取得胜利。[silly | 没有任何一种神奇的技巧能够以聪明的方式赢得战斗。 ] 你只需要适应而已。我们所有人都知道这一点，也都明白这个道理。”她再次长长地、缓缓地呼出一口气，然后继续说道：“一百年的时间，只不过是让人逐渐适应而已……就是这么简单。
rows.raw: ' "Flying is the kind of advantage that most foes can't match. Some Wraith-touched can do it, but very few. And we don't fight harpies very often." She grins. "That narrows the field quite a lot. You know what kind of defense is really good against people who can't fly and absolutely awful at people who can?" "Walls[pc.isBimbo |, of course! |. ]" You pause. "And ditches.[silly | Can't forget the ditches. 'Where's your ditch? You need to dig a ditch.' The historians would kill me if I forgot. ]" "Exactly," Anni says. "There's not always very much call for it, but whenever valkyries — or harpies — attack a walled enclosure, enemies usually aren't really prepared for it. And even if they are, a few archers or mages are things we can handle. When fortresses are defended against ground attackers, there are often what we call layers to the defense: ditches, defenders, berms, more defenders, moats, more defenders, walls, more defenders, more walls. It's not often you see layers like that against a flying attacker. About ten years back, we stormed the ruins of Vithblainn, an elven city that was held by Wraith-touched, and didn't lose a warrior." "Wow... wait." You frown. "You said 'not often'." She nods ruefully. "There's always an exception. Sixty or so years ago, one of the princesses of Belhar — Belhar the city, since they don't have much of an empire anymore — didn't like how the succession sorted out. She took a bunch of followers off to an old fortress, commandeered it, and started scheming to get the throne, or get it back, depending on who you believed about the inheritance. Normally, that's not our problem. We fight the corrupted. We don't intervene in things like succession disputes, no matter what the local law is. Buuuuut..." [pc.isBimbo |"That sounds like a big but! Hee hee. Big butt. Oooh! Did the princess have a big butt?" |"Let me guess," you say. "She thought that Wraiths would give her a leg up." ] "[pc.isBimbo |I... I don't know, dear. We never got to meet her. |No, actually. ] She was fiddling with [var0|the Waystone|a magical portal] in the fortress to try to sneak into the city the back way, but accidentally let in something... not a Wraith. The way the Astrida explained it, it was unchanneled elemental chaos? The upshot was that instead of Wraiths, what came through were spirits of fire, ice, lightning, and so on. The whole fortress melted from the inside out, had a massive column of flame reaching into the sky[silly | like it was some kind of superhero movie or something ], was surrounded by a huge storm. By the time anyone found out about it, the princess and her soldiers were dead or hollowed out by the elemental powers, and unbound, angry spirits had started coming through. They had an army's worth, which made it a task the Astrida knew they couldn't handle alone. So some of us — Hjörr, Tayann, Teniya, two dozen others — flew south to join them and the army of Prince Firmus, and tried to assault the place as quickly as we could. "The thing was, you know how I said that it's hard to layer defenses against someone who can fly? Not only did these spirits have a decent idea, they had the advantage of being surrounded by one of the worst lightning storms in history. It took several mages of Sorra to hold the weather down enough for us to be able to fly. And there was this... net, sort of, made from fire, not rope, that kept us from landing on top of the fortress. And the spirits even conjured little mantlets of ice and rock to protect them from missiles." She grimaces. "We tried to bounce the walls and a quarter of us got knocked out of the sky before even reaching the net. Some of the sisters who went down stayed down. We had to fall back and regroup, but not even the gods knew what they were bringing in through the shattered portal... and the longer it stayed open, the more time for gods-know-what to come in." [party.has viviane |Viv taps her chin thoughtfully. "I've heard of this sort of thing. In fact, I think I've heard of this very incident. It's exceedingly rare for elemental magic to manifest this way; usually it comes through summonings, not portals. A portal... well,[viv.isDemon | I suppose ] you would have had to close it[viv.isDemon | posthaste |, with no time to waste ]." |[pc.isBimbo |"Uh-oh! So you couldn't, like, wait around or anything?" |"You didn't think you had time to lay siege." It isn't a question. ] ] "We [pc.isBimbo |knew |knew ] we didn't have time," the valkyrie says grimly. Her ice-eyes cloud over with memory, then refocus on something that isn't you. "We couldn't break through the fire, not with everything inside attacking us. The best we could do was be a distraction. Normally, you want to build a mole, get more of your army up high so they can attack down onto the enemy's walls; we didn't have that option, either. So, after conferring with Prince Firmus, we headed back up and tried to keep the spirits busy while the Heartlanders and the mages scaled the wall with ladders, and other mages and soldiers hit the gates from the front, trying to burn them down with magic." "That sounds [pc.isBimbo |really really tough! |like doing it the hard way. ]" "Yes. Those spirits came from another realm, another plane of existence, and they came powerful and in the raw, not the weaker spirits sometimes used to enchant weapons. Even with the Astridas' magic tamping down the spirits' raw elemental force, we lost a lot of people. Clearing the wall opposed..." She shudders. It's a deeply weird thing to see her do that. "Flying out in full view of dozens of enemies trying to kill you, dodging and weaving and firing off magic whenever you can, over and over and over again, while soldiers die underneath you and your sisters fall out of the sky next to you and you don't even know if it's working — I wouldn't wish that kind of battle on anyone. "In the end, we made it atop the walls at great cost. The Astrida and a few of my other sisters managed to find the portal, once we destroyed the net. Whatever they found, however they killed it, whatever else they did... it worked. But we left a lot of dead and wounded on the grounds. Teniya..." Her voice breaks a little bit, then all the way, and she closes her eyes. [pc.dcb |[annika.kissed |You reach for her arm and try to force some understanding into your hard eyes. "Sorry, Anni." Then, a beat later: "She sounds like the kind of badass who wouldn't have minded paying that price, though." |"That's what war is," you say cuttingly. "You do what you need to do." ] |[annika.kissed |You offer Anni a hug and a quiet "I'm sorry," and it seems like that helps. She still needs a little time, though, so you wait |Apart from a quiet "I'm sorry," you give her a little time, waiting ] until she opens her eyes again before you ask the follow-up question. "Do you have any regrets?" Then you pause again, this time more briefly. "Would she have?" |"Awww, Anni." You offer her a reassuring hug and plenty of pats on the back, quiet whispers of "I'm sorry, sweetie," and plenty of time. It takes a little while for her eyes to open again, and you wait as long as she needs. Only after she does manage to open them and nod do you keep asking: "Do... do you think there's another way it could've turned out better?" ] Annika shakes her head. "[pc.isDK |You're right. ]This was how it had to be done. The things we had to do, the things we couldn't allow — we didn't have time to lay siege, and there weren't any clever solutions that would actually help in the time we had. Prince Firmus understood what was at stake, and if any of us had been in command instead of him, we would have made the same choice. You can't win battles against enemy armies without fighting; against a prepared enemy, you can't win fights without taking losses.[silly | There's no One Weird Trick that'll win battles the clever way. ] You just have to adapt. All of us know it. All of us understand it." She breathes out again, long and slow, before finishing her thought. "A hundred years of it just... wear, is all." '

rows.original: "Well, there's always the popular one. Southerners still probably remember the Khushkan Horde, don't you? Mercenary army fifty years back, overpromised and underdelivered to their clients, made some deals with a leftover Wraith Nightmare to stay in the game, made themselves and half the tribes in the region into its husks, and ended up trying to reenact the whole Godswar across what's left of the Empire for five years until the Heartlanders finally figured out how to ally with each other and put them down. Does that sound familiar?" [pc.bgMulti arcanist barbarian soldier scholar acolyte slumrat hunter noblescion courtesan minstrel |"[pc.isBimbo |Uh, a li'l bit. Most of the things I learned about were magicky things, you know? |A little. It's not really my area... I mean, I know the name. ]" Annika nods. "That's fair. Well, the war was the worst it'd been in a century and a half. Huge battles that soaked fields with blood, whole cities razed, farmland destroyed, refugees slaughtered. Like one of the great imperial conflicts of old." Her ice-eyed gaze goes distant, and she takes a deep breath. "I was there at Pelissia, in the last big battle with the horde." |"[pc.isBimbo |Kinda? |A little bit, ]" you say hesitantly. "Fifty years ago, right? Back in the [pc.ora wyldelf |troupe |tribe ], a few of the elders had lived through it. Some of the other groups around us actually joined the horde, I think, and our people fought against them." "It was a very large war, embracing Heartland and wilderness alike," Annika agrees. "I don't think most city-dwellers remember the havoc wreaked out on the edges of their lands, where your people lived. But they certainly remember the towns sacked, the ones that were razed, the ones that were almost destroyed... and the ones saved by the allied victory." A lopsided smile, a wink, and then she continues: "If you ever want all the beer you can drink in a Heartlands tavern, tell them you stood at Pelissia against the Khushkans." |"[pc.isBimbo |Ugh, yeah |Where I'm from ]," you say ruefully[pc.isBimbo |. "I remember lots about them |, "everyone knows about the Khushkans ]." You fill in the blanks for her. After all, among your fellow warriors back south, those battles and sieges were names to conjure with. "I even knew a[pc.isBimbo | suuuuper old crusty soldier bean |n old graybeard officer ] who was at the Battle of Pelissia. You know, the last big fight." Annika grins. "So was I." |"[pc.isBimbo |Oooh, yeah! ]I know the history pretty well." You'd better, after all, given how much of it you had to study. Quickly and perhaps a little proudly, you outline the stories you can tell about some of the great battles and feats of derring-do. "Actually, my own arcane college sent[pc.isBimbo |, like, looooots of mages | battlemages, both faculty and students, ] to fight at Pelissia — you know, the really big battle near the end. They did [pc.isBimbo |well! |their part. ] There's still a statue of one of them in the main hall." "You're very well read," Anni says approvingly. "Thanks[pc.isBimbo |! Buuut... I bet you didn't have to read about it, huh? |." You pause. "If I had to guess, you didn't have to do book reading to learn about it. ] You lived it." A smile, then: "Oh yes. I was at Pelissia myself." |"Yeah, I remember. Some of the divine paladins who visited the local shrines would talk about the battles — the older ones, anyway." "It was a team effort," Anni reminisces, "but the clergy and divine warriors played a role, yes. We helped make sure the alliances could happen. So many of the Heartlanders were mistrustful of each other and needed diplomats from the various priesthoods to seal deals; others simply lacked the strength to make war from a standing start and needed godsworn and paladins to hold the line. Including me and many of [pc.swornGod lumia |our |my ] sisters. I was there at Pelissia with the other warriors of light and the rest of the allied array when the Khushkans made their last great attempt to destroy us." |"Not really. [pc.isBimbo |I kinda... didn't learn that much about history. It's history, right? |History wasn't really my strongest suit. ]" You shrug expressively. "[pc.isBimbo |Like, where I grew up, in the slums and all, it wasn't really a big deal for us. |I know the name, but I kind of had bigger concerns when I was growing up. There's not a whole lot from outside that matters in the slums. ]" "I can understand that." Anni nods. "It was the worst it'd been in a century and a half. Huge battles that soaked fields with blood, whole cities razed, farmland destroyed, refugees slaughtered. Like one of the great imperial wars of old." Her ice-eyed gaze goes distant, and she takes a deep breath. "I was there at Pelissia, in the last big battle with the horde." |"[pc.isBimbo |Uh-huh! ]I grew up on some of the stories." Before your parents left to seek adventure, stories of the Khushkan War were campfire stuff. Great battles at places with names to conjure with, like Kesh and Gaba; tremendous feats of derring-do, of secret missions and scouting and rescues. "I still remember them so well..." "Names to conjure with," Annika muses. "Yes, that sounds about right. Talk about the relief of Gaba to any heartlander, or a member of a dozen religious orders, and they'll know exactly what you want to evoke: the siege mages hammering away at the half-ruined old Belharan walls; the gathered horde shouting war-songs as they stood over the bodies of dead defenders, ready to assault; the frantic, doomed efforts of the city-dwellers to hold the line; and then, not long before first light, a glint of silver and bronze on the hills above the city. It was a terrible war, but it had to be fought, and it made many stories and even more heroes." [pc.dcb |"Subtle way of saying that you were one of those heroes," you chuckle. |You smile. "One of whom, I'm guessing, was you." |"Yeah," you murmur. "Wait — were you one of those heroes?" ] "I played my part," she says coolly. "And I was there at Pelissia, the horde's last great attack." |"[pc.isBimbo |Oooh, yeah! |Oh, yes. ]" Your own family was on the front lines of that war — along with half the old Empire. In fact, you could hardly avoid the family stories of all the cool fights from your grandparents' generation. Not just the ones they'd been in, but the ones they hadn't. "[pc.isBimbo |I've been a good [pc.boyGirl], so I remember them, too! Like all the stories about Pelissia and stuff... |They're still etched into my mind, like the Battle of Pelissia." ] That last name puts the ghost of a smile on Anni's face. "I was there at Pelissia." |"[pc.isBimbo |Aw, yeah! I remember the songs about that war |Oh, I'm more than familiar with the songs and the history ]," you say airily. After all, a well-educated escort needs to be familiar with such events, not least because the older clientele is liable to reminisce about the things that make them feel important, from back when they were young and strong. "[pc.isBimbo |Like, you could hear the same story about the war like four times in one evening sometimes! |One's liable to hear some stories about that war many times over throughout an evening. ]" "That sounds like it'd make for a long evening," Anni chuckles. "I almost feel guilty for bringing up my own Khushkan war story now." You turn a flattering smile on her. "[pc.isBimbo |Hee hee. It's okay! I asked, right? That means I wanna know. |It's more than fine. If I didn't want to hear, I wouldn't have asked. ]" "Well, I had my own role," she says modestly. "Fought in a few of the great battles and plenty of the smaller ones. And I was there at Pelissia, the last big Khushkan attack." |Oh, that calls for a bardic smile. "Gods, do I! It's great fodder for stories and songs." Anywhere in the Heartlands, a stirring rendition of 'The Death Ride' of Goar and his warriors will make a good minstrel's coin purse a lot fatter by evening's end. And in your experience, even younger folks like to hear about the great battles from their grandparents' day. "I'm glad to hear that the stories still have plenty of currency in the south," Annika says. "I know what short lives, and short memories, some people down there can have." "Oh, sure[pc.isBimbo |! |. ] They're classics." You pause. "[pc.isBimbo |Did you do something during the war? Oh! You did, didn't you? What was it? |What'd you do during the war? ]" "A lot of fighting, just like the rest of the Order. I was there for many of the smaller battles, and some of the big ones. I was even there at Pelissia for the last big Khushkan attack." ] [party.has arona |"Sounds like a damn good story," Arona whistles. "Was it?" |"Wow. That is the stuff of legends. What was it like?" ] "Awful," she says shortly. "What the Khushkans did was horrific: sacrificing whole towns to their Nightmare, trading souls for monstrous enhancements and raw power.[silly | It didn't have anything to do with being an ordu or ulus, at the very least. ] In battle, their array was as well-organized as the serried ranks of any holy order or Minoan legion. Humans and taeleer, minotaurs and goblins and elves: when the southerners stared across the field at the faces of their foes, they saw themselves. Mutated and twisted, but still very recognizably people who had once been like them. Also," she admits, "they saw horrific misshapen monsters, too, especially after the Nightmare got hold of them. But still. "To oppose them, we brought everybody. By that time, all of the armies defending the Heartlands were mixed. Contingents from every faith, and from most of the cities and realms of the southern half of Old Belhar. Taelian heavy infantry alongside humans and salamanders. Goblins and elves, orcs and centaurs, members of every single one of the religious orders, all intermixed. We built armies that could fight together, full of warriors bound by sentiment, skill, shared hardships, and most of all, sheer determination. And at Pelissia, we needed every ounce of determination we could muster, because it began as a close-gripped fight where the Khushkans slammed into our lines and ground forward for everything they were worth." [party.has quintillus |"Taelian heavy infantry..." Quin mutters. "Yeah. I know the stories, too. It's exactly the kind of fight the Alliance hates getting into." ] "[pc.isBimbo |If that's how it started," you guess, "does that mean it ended a different way? |Started out, though. That's not the same thing as how it ended. ]" "[pc.isBimbo |Yes |No ]." Anni's brow tightens. "[pc.isBimbo |Things changed very quickly |No, it wasn't ]. As the main lines jabbed away at each other, we and the Sorrans stayed in the skies, and from there we could see the Khushkans' mages. We saw exactly when they stopped throwing lightning bolts and blighted energy at our ranks and when they conjured a dozen giant fireballs to hurl onto the desiccated grassy fields at our feet. The whole battlefield turned to smoke and flame in less than a minute. Soon, we couldn't see the Khushkans except for the ones close enough to touch; we could barely see our own comrades. "Usually, if you want to do a trick like setting a battlefield on fire, you don't let your own army get into the middle of the blaze before you light up. I don't think any of us were quite expecting just how desperate they would get. The Sorrans did what they could, funneling away some of the smoke, stifling what flames they could, and trying to summon a storm to douse the blaze, but that all took time. And in the meanwhile, our army was stuck fast, too close to retreat in good order without turning the whole thing into a rout. We, the harpies, the vesparans all flew into the smoke as low as we dared, but we could barely breathe, let alone see anything. Just chaos. One of the few things I could see was some spiny-backed monstrosity and a younger valkyrie, Hilde, running each other through and disappearing into the sea of bodies below. She — I —" The valkyrie pauses, grimaces, and closes her eyes for a long, long time. You let her do it and wait [pc.isDK |patiently |sympathetically ] while she composes herself: the head-shake, the sigh, the deep breath, and then her eyes reopen. When she resumes, her voice quavers a bit, but picks up more solidity as she keeps talking. "Thank all the gods for Eira. Somehow she found us in the smoke and came winging in with a breathless message: the Khushkans were throwing everything into the center, and our lines were buckling. They were going after the mages, and thanks to the smoke and flame and confusion, the rest of the army didn't know — or couldn't do anything about it. We quickly gathered up Thrud, a dozen of our other sisters, several of the hornets, a few harpies, and all rushed after her as fast as we could. Somehow Eira didn't lose her sense of direction in the smoke and put us squarely above the Khushkans just as they broke through." "[pc.isDK |Close as shit," you mutter. "Sounds like you made it, though. |Just in the nick of time. ]" Annika raises an eyebrow. "It was still in doubt even when we showed up. They were still focused on the mages and their last remaining defenders, the Astrida and other warriors. That fight in the center, where Takanda Laskarina held off Respendius and his corrupted minotaurs? The one that makes it into all the songs? I could see the flashes of bronze and magic and Taka's flame-tail from where I was. I could see the shadows of mages behind her, trying to hold up wards, blow away the smoke, douse the flame. And from above, we supported them as best we could, some of us loosing arrows, others soaring overhead to cast long trails of holy sunfire on the Khushkans, all of us constantly dodging their own arrows and javelins and magic. It took a long time. It wasn't the instantaneous effect [silly |that you see in movies |you'll hear about in a bard's tale ]. There were a lot of foes to fight, even after we arrived. But we killed and wounded and distracted enough of them for the charge to gradually lose momentum." [pc.bg scholar hunter noblescion minstrel |For a few seconds, you marvel at the fact that Annika calls the Takanda Laskarina 'Taka' like it's no big deal. Then you remember what she was talking about: the Khushkan charge. ]"They got stuck." "Yeah. They got stuck." The valkyrie nods at the memory, and during the pause, her jaw sets a little more than it normally does. Grimly, she continues, "I don't remember exactly what happened first. Even in the sky, I couldn't see everything. It was just an endless rhythm of sunfire and stabbing, trying to charge whenever I saw an opening, dodging javelins and thrown axes and giant spines on the backs of some of the most mutated hordesmen. But somewhere in there, the smoke started to clear and the fires died down. At the time, I had no idea about what was happening in the other parts of the battle. They're for someone else's stories and songs, anyway. The part that matters here is that the Sorrans finally managed to call down a real storm. "At that point, thanks to all the lightning, we all had to land, but it was fine. Half of the Khushkans' forces were caught between all the different parts of our army. We could hit them from all sides and from above, and all the horrors that their Nightmare had gifted them couldn't save them. That's usually a sign of winning the battle... but it took a long, long time to do that. Each one of their warriors fought even harder, with greater frenzy, now that the end was near. They didn't try to surrender and we wouldn't have accepted one even if they did. Even after everybody in the battle knew that we had won, it was a difficult slog through the rain and the mud before the last Khushkans had either fled or been killed." "That's how it all ended? The biggest, most brutal war in decades?" "If only. There were other parts of the horde to fight, and their Nightmare was still at large. Fields still burned, farmers were still sacrificed to their dark powers, merchants were waylaid on the roads and left there in pieces. It took almost a year of hunting and a very stern chase to finally wipe them all out." The shadows around her eyes tell the tale of the exhaustion of those last months just as much as her words do. "The thing about great, glorious charges or heroic defensive stands... they matter, for sure. They make wonderful stories, they can rouse hearts, and a lot of the time, they really do change the world. But even for the most glorious, unambiguously good victories, there's always a lot more war, a lot more gruesome, painful, dangerous nastiness to go afterward."

But even for the most glorious, unambiguously good victories, there's always a lot more war, a lot more gruesome, painful, dangerous nastiness to go afterward." '

rows.original:
"The journey beyond the mountains?" Annika frowns. "Well, that wasn't supposed to become a war story, but it was kind of forced on us. Originally, the four of us — Thrisa, Randgrid, Shirin, and I — were just there to rededicate the temple to Lumia in Gapakoana, but the city was raided by a local warlord who carried off many men and women as slaves to work in her mines. So we offered our aid to the Xenaspan king in pursuing her. After all, what else could we do? We weren't in Xenaspa to defend the innocent, but doing that anyway is part of who we are. 
    
    "What we got was a master class on just how different that country was. Valkyries have been working in the Heartlands for hundreds of years. We know it, and heartlanders know us. Someone, somewhere in the Order is a person who has lived every life one can live down there. Farmer, shepherd, mercenary, noblewoman, priestess, the urban poor and the rural wealthy and everything in between. In Xenaspa, we had no one — poor Shirin was from Ariana, and those two realms don't always get along well. Randgrid was determined to do more than simply wait around, though, so we tried our hand at investigating and didn't get very far." She chuckles dismissively. "Made ourselves look like idiots doing it, too. Young Thrisa in particular — she meant well, but she was a hot mess, she and Randgrid tried to be friendly with the wrong person, and she nearly started a fight with half a village before Shirin was able to calm things down. After that, Randgrid told the Xenaspans that we'd be more helpful as armed muscle than investigators, and that's what we did."
    
    Not too terribly dissimilar from your own travails in Njorhaalt[flags.KM_ENTER| and Khor'minos], in their own way. If you didn't have Ryn[flags.KM_ENTER|[brint.recruited| and [bri.name]|[brienne.recruited| and [bri.name]]]] around, you'd have been even worse off. You follow up: "[pc.isBimbo
        |Sooo that means fighty bits, right?
        |And that's where the battle comes in?
    ]"
    
    "Yes." With her hands, Annika sketches out an enormous mesa in the air. "When they finally figured out where she had gone, it was grim. The mines were within a great plateau, a natural fortress, and she held her living bounty within. But it was a standoff, even with the hostages, because she had precious few warriors with her and we had half the Xenaspan royal army — chariots, infantry in full panoply, their far-seeing archers. Her whole plan was to delay until her allies could collect their own warriors and rush to break the siege. Maybe she thought that they would surprise the king. Ha. Not when he had valkyries to watch the skies and the earth both."
    
    [pc.isBimbo
        |"Hee hee! Definitely not![pc.swornGod lumia
            | Sun mommies like us are pretty good at the whole, uh, flying thing.
        ]" Then you pause. "Wait, didn't you say it was still tough? How come?"
        |[pc.swornGod lumia
            |[var0|With a flicker of effort, your own glowing magical wings emerge from your back; you give them a flex and grin.|You flex your own [pc.wings] and grin.] "Changes things, for sure. Didn't you say it was still a tough fight, though?"
            |"You said it was a hard-fought battle, though," you probe.
        ]
    ]
    
    "It was. Having warning meant that we weren't blindsided, but our foes yielded little to the king's army in numbers and ardor. Shirin kept busy — since she could both speak the language and fly, she was the best messenger available to the king despite her foreign heritage, and she earned her glory that day when she told the reserve forces where to march to hit the rebels where they were weakest. Thrisa, Randgrid, and I? We were already there, holding the line. Still, the lion's share of the day's praises went to the Xenaspan infantry. They went in, [silly
        |lochos by lochos
        |company by company
    ], each charge rushing in with the force of a sledgehammer. Some fell, of course, but fewer than you might think; though nearly all of us were wounded, none fled, and the chance to make a killing blow is small under such circumstances." She grimaces. "Even though we won the battle with few dead, even though the warlord surrendered herself and her captives as soon as it was over, the three of us were in... bad shape. Thrisa took... well, you probably don't want me to dwell on the details. Thanks to those injuries, it was many weeks of recovery before we could depart. Weeks of slowly working back up to normal activity, but as fast as we could was still too slow."
    
    "So you were hurt a lot worse than normal.[flags.ANNIKA_MASSAGE| I remember all of the scar stories...]"
    
    "It was bad, although it was worse for Thrisa than for the rest of us. For a few days, we weren't sure if she would make it. And to pass away in such a foreign land..." Anni's ice-eyes cloud over. "Dying in battle is something that can happen to any warrior, but passing away far from home and hearth so that your loved ones can't even say goodbye one last time, so that your mortal remains lie in a foreign land, forgotten by all? I wouldn't wish that on anybody. The Xenaspans, at least — they put up trophies. Memorials, monuments, symbols of victory. There was an ancient battle not that far away, with a trophy that included old Belharan war-gear: the helmets, the swords, even a few shields faced with silver. Maybe they came from the warriors who chose to settle in that land. We were glad to not have to leave Thrisa's arms and armor with them."
    
    She blows out her breath slowly and closes her eyes before continuing. "I would like to go back someday, if it's even possible. But not as a warrior. Not like that."

翻越山脉之后的旅程？”安妮卡皱起了眉头。“其实那本不该成为一个战争故事，但事情的发展却让我们不得不将其写下来。最初，我们四个人——特里萨、兰德格瑞德、希琳和我——只是想去加帕科阿纳将那座寺庙重新献给卢米娅，但那座城市遭到了当地一位军阀的袭击，他抓走了许多男女，把他们当作奴隶送到自己的矿场去劳作。 因此，我们向泽纳斯帕的国王提供了帮助，协助他追捕她。毕竟，我们还能做什么呢？我们来到泽纳斯帕并不是为了保护无辜的人，但无论如何，履行这一责任也是我们本性的一部分。 
    
    我们所了解到的是，那个国家与我们的世界究竟有多么不同。瓦尔基里们在心脏地带已经生活了数百年。我们了解那里的情况，而心脏地带的人们也认识我们。在那个组织中，肯定有某个人曾经在那里体验过人类可能经历的每一种生活。 农民、牧人、雇佣兵、贵族女性、女祭司、城市贫民以及乡村富人，各种各样的人都有。在塞纳斯帕，我们没有属于任何特定群体的人——可怜的希琳来自阿里亚纳，而这两个地区之间的关系并不总是那么融洽。 不过，Randgrid并没有选择只是坐以待毙，所以我们尝试进行了一些调查，但并没有取得什么成果。”她轻笑着，似乎觉得这件事很可笑。“我们自己也因此显得像个白痴。尤其是年轻的Thrisa——她本意是好的，但她的行为实在是一团糟。她和Randgrid试图与一些不合适的人交好，结果差点惹恼了半个村子的人，直到Shirin出面才平息了事态。 之后，Randgrid告诉Xenaspans，我们作为武装力量会比作为调查人员更能提供帮助，于是我们就这么做了。
    
    这与你在尼约哈尔特所经历的困境其实并没有太大区别。[flags.KM_ENTER| 还有霍尔米诺斯]它们以自己的方式存在着。如果你没有Ryn的话……[flags.KM_ENTER|[brint.recruited| 以及 [bri.name]|[brienne.recruited| 以及 [bri.name]]]] 不然的话，你的处境会更糟的。你接着说道：[pc.isBimbo
        |所以，这意味着会有战斗场面，对吧？
        |这就是战斗开始的地方吗？
    ]是的。”安妮卡用双手在空气中勾勒出一个巨大的平台。“当他们终于找到她去的地方时，情况非常糟糕。那些矿井位于一个巨大的高原上，那里就像是一道天然的堡垒，而她就把那些珍贵的资源藏在了那里。 但即便有人质在场，这也是一场对峙——因为她手下的战士寥寥无几，而我们则拥有半个泽纳斯潘皇家军队：包括战车、全副武装的步兵，以及那些目光远大的弓箭手。她的整个计划就是拖延时间，直到她的盟友能够集结自己的军队，然后合力打破包围。 也许她以为他们能够给国王一个惊喜。哈，但当他拥有那些能够监视天地万物的女武神时，这种想法就根本不可能实现了。
    
    [pc.isBimbo
        |嘻嘻！绝对不会的！[pc.swornGod lumia
            | 像我们这样的太阳妈妈们，其实挺擅长飞行的。
        ]然后你暂停了。‘等等，你不是说这还是很难吗？怎么会这样？
        |[pc.swornGod lumia
            |[var0|只需稍加努力，你自己的发光魔法翅膀就会从背后展开；你活动了一下这些翅膀，然后露出了笑容。|你展示自己的实力吧。 [pc.wings] 然后露出笑容。] 确实改变了局面。不过你之前不是也说过，这场战斗仍然非常艰难吗？
            |不过你说过，这是一场艰苦的战斗，对吧？”你问道。
        ]
    ]
    
    确实如此。有了预警，我们就不会措手不及，但我们的敌人在人数和战斗热情上依然远胜国王的军队。希琳忙得不可开交——由于她既懂那种语言又会飞行，尽管她有着外国血统，但她仍是国王手中最得力的信使。就在那天，她成功地将预备部队引向叛军最薄弱的防线，从而为国王赢得了胜利，也赢得了自己的荣耀。 特里萨、兰德格瑞德和我？我们早就到了那里，坚守在我们的位置上。不过，当天大部分的赞誉都归功于塞纳斯潘步兵。他们冲了进去， [silly
        |一个接一个地
        |一家一家地
    ]每一次冲锋都带着如大锤般的力量。当然，也有人倒下了，但倒下的人比你想象的要少；虽然我们几乎所有人都受了伤，但没有一个人逃跑。在这种情况下，想要给予致命一击的机会实在是微乎其微。她皱了皱眉头：“尽管我们这场战斗几乎没有人员伤亡，尽管战争结束后那位女军阀立即投降了自己和她的俘虏们，但我们三个人的情况还是……很糟糕。Thrisa受了……嗯，你大概也不想听我详细说明那些细节吧。 由于那些伤势，我们花了数周的时间进行康复，才得以出发。那几周里，我们一直在逐渐恢复到正常的活动状态，但即便我们已经尽了最大努力，速度仍然太慢了。”

“所以，你的伤势比平常要严重得多。[flags.ANNIKA_MASSAGE| 我记得所有那些关于伤痕的故事……]那真是太糟糕了，对特丽莎来说，情况比我们其他人更糟。有几天，我们都不知道她能否挺过来。而在这样一个陌生的地方离世……”安妮冰冷的眼神中浮现出哀伤。“在战斗中牺牲是任何战士都可能遭遇的事情，但远在家乡之外去世，让亲人们甚至无法再道一次别，让你的遗体被埋葬在异国他乡，被所有人遗忘，这样的结局未免太残酷了。 我绝不希望任何人经历这种事。至少，Xenaspans人会这么做——他们会竖立奖杯、建立纪念碑，用这些来象征胜利。在不太远的地方，发生过一场古老的战役，那里的奖杯中就包括了贝尔哈兰人使用的古代战具：头盔、剑，甚至还有一些银饰护盾。 也许他们来自那些选择在那片土地上定居的战士们。我们很庆幸不必把特丽莎的武器和盔甲也交给他们。

她缓缓地呼出一口气，闭上眼睛，然后继续说道：“如果有可能的话，我希望能有一天回到那里去。 但不是以战士的身份。不是那样的。

Whether you've a long career ahead of you or are staring death in the face, the point is that you fight smart and you fight hard if you want to finish the job and bring as many people safely home as you can." "[pc.isDK |Is that the goal, though?" Annika narrows her eyes. "It should be. |[pc.isBimbo |That sounds like a good goal! |That's the worthiest goal there is. ]" The valkyrie smiles gently. rows.translation: "[pc.bg soldier barbarian |你经历过很多战斗，所以应该也听说过那个老掉牙的笑话吧：“没有计划是能够成功的……”，对吧？ 你点了点头。[pc.isBimbo |是啊，很多呢！有时候你想做某件事，但总会有一些因素阻碍你。所以你得有备选计划，明白吗？而且即使没有计划，你也得能应付得来。比如，身边有好的朋友，擅长应对各种挑战，或许还能有点运气！然后你还会故作夸张地眨眨眼。“不过有时候，动动屁股也会很有用哦！而且这样会有趣得多，明白我的意思吧？ |很多时候，战斗其实就是一场赌博，大多数情况下，总会发生一些没人能够预料到的事情。你必须依靠自己的智慧、技巧、战友们的支持，以及诸神的眷顾，才能顺利度过难关。 ] "[pc.isBimbo |不是最后一部分，不过除此之外，没错，”她轻笑道。 |说得真像个真正的战士，”她赞许地说道。 ] 你说的对，当然。[pc.isBimbo |尤其是关于开头的那部分内容。 ]. 战斗开始了 [silly |迷雾与摩擦 |混乱与迷茫 ]没有任何计划能够完全消除这一问题。但是…… |战士们之间有这样一句俗话：没有任何计划能够在第一场战斗中就得以成功实施。无论你对事情抱有什么期望，无论你和你的同伴们正在努力做什么……总会有某些因素因为偶然性的原因而导致计划失败。即使是一个再周密的计划，也难免会遇到一些你事先根本无法预料到的问题。[pc.isBimbo |嗯，有点像性爱吧！有时候你开始的时候以为只是想简单地进行口交，但结果发现对方的阴茎非常敏感，你自然不会想让他们立刻达到高潮，所以你就得尝试其他方式，放慢节奏，让这个过程持续得更久一些，这样他们也能享受到乐趣！ |我注意到，有时候，确实是这样。 [silly |有时候，敌人会随机打出暴击，或者误击了“错误”的队友，于是各种不幸的事情就可能会发生。真是倒霉啊…… [pc.swornGod lumia |Lumia |众神 ] 是用来保存文件的，对吧？ |一个火球可以吸收更多的魔法能量，一次剑击可能会偏离目标，而一支箭则可能会被风吹向完全意想不到的方向。 ] ]" "[pc.isBimbo |一个……挺有趣的类比，不过你说得对，亲爱的。 |正是如此。 ]嗯，”她赞许地说道，“计划并不总是能够按预期进行。在战斗中，真正决定你能否成功的是你的战友们、你的训练、你的技巧、你的运气，以及神明的眷顾。不过…… ] 嗯？” “所以，任何战斗都是蒂拉个人的…… [silly |G |g ]《骨之怒》，当然：这完全取决于运气。但只要准备得当，你仍然可以改变胜算。出其不意地攻击敌人，通常会大大增加你的胜率。好好训练，从侧翼发动攻击吧。 根据你的需求来塑造战场。找出他们的弱点，然后用你手头上的一切手段——箭矢、长矛、火球、剑锋——去攻击他们。这些手段确实很重要。”安妮卡双臂一摊，继续说道，“不过它们并不能保证你一定会获胜，因为有时候，事情就是会出乎意料地发展。但是你更愿意选择成功率更高的选项，而不是那些失败几率更大的选择。 [party.has arona |[arona.isSub |嘿，说得真有道理。”阿罗娜用一种奇怪的眼神看着安妮，“你说起话来就像是个真正懂打架的人。既不废话，也不犯傻。 |哈，这才是真正的战士该有的作风。”阿罗娜的手搭在你的肩上，“你最好好好听着，这个测试版的菜鸟。虽然说了一大堆，但说的其实就是战斗的本质。 ] |[pc.isBimbo |所以，”你咬着嘴唇低声说道，“在战斗技巧上自作聪明…… |所以要聪明地战斗。 ] 这仍然是件好事。 ] 没错。”她说道。[party.has arona | 对你那些兽人族人点头致意。 [arona.isSub |测试版 |阿尔法 ]那么 ] 她开始更加生动、更快地说话，但并没有显得过于急促；显然，这个话题她已经讨论过很多次了。“记住，在任何一场战斗中，你都有很多目标。你想要获胜——无论获胜意味着什么。 拯救一些农民？击败坏人？保护一座神社？在任何战斗中，都要牢记自己的目标，并努力去实现它。但如果你能够做到这些，你肯定也会希望赢得下一场战斗，再下一场战斗……即使你的任务是为了保护你的姐妹们或那些你正在拯救的人们而牺牲，你也希望自己的牺牲能够发挥作用，延缓敌人的进攻，尽你所能地打击他们。 无论你面前是漫长的职业生涯，还是面临着死亡的威胁，关键就在于要明智地战斗。 以及 如果你想完成这项任务，并尽可能让更多的人安全回家，就必须全力以赴地战斗。[pc.isDK |是吗？ 那个目标，也是吧？” 安妮卡眯起了眼睛。“那是…… 应该 是。 |[pc.isBimbo |这听起来是个很好的目标！ |这才是最有价值的目标。 ]那位女武神温柔地笑了。“当然。 ] Lumia 保护毕竟，我们也应该这样做。更广泛地说，即使你击败了一个极其凶恶的敌人，但如果你没能拯救那些你试图拯救的人，或者你自己或你的同伴受伤过重甚至丧生，从而无法享受胜利的成果，那么这一切也都毫无意义。一名战士必须准备好赴死，但毫无意义地死去则是另一回事。因此，如果有机会的话，你就应该尝试制定计划。
rows.raw: ' "[pc.bg soldier barbarian |You've seen plenty of combat, so you've probably heard of the old 'no plan survives...' joke, right?" You nod. "[pc.isBimbo |Yeah, lots! Like, sometimes you wanna do a thing, but stuff gets in the way. You gotta have backup plans, you know? And you gotta be able to do okay without a plan. You know, like having good friendos with you, and bein' good at fighty stuff, and maybe getting a li'l bit lucky!" Then you ostentatiously wink. "But also, sometimes shaking your booty works too! And it's a lot more fun. Know what I mean?" |Many times. Battle's a roll of the dice, and most of the time, stuff just happens that nobody could plan for. You've got to rely on your wits, your skill, your comrades, and the grace of the gods to see you through." ] "[pc.isBimbo |Not the last part, but otherwise yes," she chuckles. |Spoken like a true warrior," she says approvingly. ] "You're right, of course[pc.isBimbo |, especially about the first bit ]. Battle is [silly |fog and friction |chaos and confusion ], and no plan can remove that entirely. But..." |There's a thing warriors say to each other: no plan survives the first blow of battle. Whatever expectations you might have built up for things, whatever you and your sisters are trying to do... something, in some way, is going to slip up through random chance. Even a good plan runs into problems that you couldn't reasonably have accounted for." "[pc.isBimbo |Mmm. Kinda like sex! Like sometimes you go in thinking you're gonna do a li'l bit of a blowjob, but then it turns out that the person's dick is suuuper sensitive and you don't wanna just make them cum right away, so you gotta go for other things and slow down and make it take a li'l longer so they can have fun too! |I have noticed that sometimes, yeah. [silly |From time to time, an enemy will get a random crit or hit the 'wrong' party member and all kinds of unfortunate stuff can happen. Thank [pc.swornGod lumia |Lumia |the gods ] for save files, right? |A fireball can get a little more magical energy fed into it, a sword-cut can go just a little awry, an arrow can catch the wind and go somewhere nobody was expecting. ] ]" "[pc.isBimbo |An... interesting analogy, but you're right, sweetie |Exactly ]," she says approvingly. "Plans don't always work out. In battle, it's your sisters — your comrades — and your training, your skill and your luck and the gods' favor that see you through. Except..." ] "Hm?" "So, any battle is Tira's personal [silly |G |g ]ame of Bones, sure: a roll of the ivory dice. But prepare the right way, and you can still nudge the odds in your favor. Surprise an enemy, and that's usually a good thing for your chances. Train up. Hit them in the flank. Shape the battlefield to your needs. Figure out what their weaknesses are and hurl every arrow, spear-blade, fireball, and sword point that you have at them. Those things matter." Annika spreads her arms wide. "Maybe they won't guarantee that you win, because sometimes, stuff just happens... but you'd rather have the better odds than the worse ones." [party.has arona |[arona.isSub |"Hey, that's good shit." Arona looks at Anni funny. "You talk like someone who knows how to fight real. No bullshit, but no bein' a fuckin' brainlet either." |"Ha. That's real warrior shit right there." Arona's hand lands on your shoulder. "You'd better be listenin', beta bitch. It's a lot of talkin', but it's about how fights actually are." ] |[pc.isBimbo |"So," you murmur, chewing on your lip, "being a smartypants about fighting |"So fighting smart ] is still a good thing." ] "That's right." She[party.has arona | nods at your orcish [arona.isSub |beta |alpha ], then ] starts to speak more animatedly and quickly without quite rushing herself; this is clearly a topic she's discussed frequently. "Don't forget, in any fight you've got lots of goals. You want to win — whatever winning means. Save some farmers? Defeat the bad guys? Protect a shrine? Remember your objective in any battle, and strain to achieve it. But if you can, you also want to win the next battle, and the battle after that... and even if the job is to die in place for your sisters or for the people you're saving, you want to make that death matter, delay your enemies, hammer them as hard as you can. Whether you've a long career ahead of you or are staring death in the face, the point is that you fight smart and you fight hard if you want to finish the job and bring as many people safely home as you can." "[pc.isDK |Is that the goal, though?" Annika narrows her eyes. "It should be. |[pc.isBimbo |That sounds like a good goal! |That's the worthiest goal there is. ]" The valkyrie smiles gently. "Of course. ] Lumia protects, after all, and we're supposed to do the same. And speaking more generally, even if you defeat a truly vicious foe, that doesn't matter if you fail to save the people you were trying to save — or leave yourself or your companions too hurt or dead to enjoy the fruits of victory. A warrior must be ready to die, but dying senselessly is another matter. And that's why you should try to plan if you have the opportunity." '

rows.original: "[party.hasCompanions |You travel with [party.manyCompanions |friends and allies |a friend and ally ], don't you? And you're the one who gives the orders, right?" [var0 |"When I let [pc.himHer]," Arona snorts. "[pc.HeShe]'s not even that shitty at it." |"[pc.dcb |Yeah. I've been doing it enough that I barely have to at this point. |More or less. I've been with my friends for long enough that they seem to understand what I'd like them to do anyway. |Kinda! I mean, they're all really smart cookies, and we've been together for a while! I don't need to do much telling or ordering or anything. ][silly | Manual mode definitely helps, though. ]" ] "That's good!" she says cheerfully. "Long-time comrades who understand how their friends think in battle are much stronger together than a grab bag. Valkyries often fight with allies we barely know, and it usually makes the job a lot harder. Allies you know well? Things go much more smoothly with them, and there's a reason for that. |You walk a lonely road[silly |, and I hope it's not the only one that you have ever known ]. It's important to have allies in a struggle like the one you face now, but I understand if being a leader isn't something that comes easily to you. Leadership is very, very difficult, after all." "[pc.dcb |That's why I can't be assed with it. Me against the world, that's how I like it." "There's only so far that can take you," she points out. "But you're not wrong. It's tough. |There's definitely a lot of pressure." "Yes," she says, nodding. "But even when the will is there, the technique might not be. |I bet it's tough to always be in charge of fighting people!" "Yes. It's difficult to muster the will to do it and it's also difficult to do the different parts of the job correctly. ] ] If you're in charge of other warriors, you don't just tell people what to do — you have to make them understand what you want to have happen. And those aren't the same thing at all!" "Sounds like you[pc.isBimbo | saw something like that happen! |'re speaking from experience. ]" She lets her head droop to one side and sighs theatrically. "Yes. I witnessed a screaming match between a Yvennese lord and his constable because the constable won a battle that he didn't know he was 'supposed' to lose. He was to be luring the enemy into a trap, but the lord never told him; he simply gave him too few soldiers to fight his battle, then left him to his own devices, assuming he'd put up a realistic amount of fight and then lose. The constable didn't get the message and inconveniently won the battle." "[pc.dcb |Nice job. |That doesn't sound so bad, honestly. |Good for him! ] A win is a win, right?" "Yes, but... it wasn't the lord's win, which made him very angry. And more of their enemies got away than the lord would have wished, which is, to be fair, a bit of a problem. Instead of wandering into a trap that might have led to a colossal, glorious victory, the enemies simply gave them an ordinary victory instead." Annika shrugs. "Ordinary victories are still fine, though, especially when won against such great odds. The real problem was that the lord never told his constable the whole plan. Perhaps he was holding something back to seem smarter when it all came off.[silly | Perhaps he was doing that for dramatic story purposes, withholding details from the audience to ramp up suspense. ] Or maybe he just thought that explaining things to a lowly constable was beneath him." [party.has arona |"Yeah," Arona grouses, "idiots who can't be assed to tell everybody else the plan don't last long. Fuckin' Argoth." You nod at the memory. [pc.isBimbo |"Oh, right! Your brother and stuff! Yeah. He really should've been better at telling people why he was doin' what he was doin', huh?" |"Being a little persuasive and cutting everybody in on his ideas might've helped him out." ] |[pc.isBimbo |You nod sagely. "And that's why you gotta tell everybody what you actually want to have happen!" |"So there's no shame in telling everybody the whole plan, then." ] ] [party.has arona |Anni chimes back in: ]"Exactly. That way, everybody can know the goal. And if something comes up, if reality intervenes, they can use their best judgment to figure out how to respond in a way that will help. That's where a team of truly worked-in warriors really shines. They trust each other's judgment, and they know the goals and each other. I miss fighting alongside my sisters, because we had just that sort of team[party.hasCompanions | — much like the one [party.compNames] have now ]." [pc.isBimbo |"So you gotta talk to people! I mean, I already, like, knew that, but I guess this is just more proof. Talking's pretty important for fighty stuff." |"It makes sense that communication is so important," you muse. "Calling out threats, setting up attacks from different angles — those are all big deals. But if you have a plan, a single agreed-upon plan is even more of a big deal." ] "Especially when you're moving dozens or hundreds of people at a time," she chuckles. "Three or four is hard enough![silly | There's a reason many people don't bother to play this game on full manual control... apart from the, mmm, one-handed parts of content, of course. ]"
rows.translation: "[party.hasCompanions |与你一同旅行的是…… [party.manyCompanions |朋友与盟友 |一位朋友和盟友 ]不是吗？而且下达命令的也是你，对吧？ [var0 |当我允许…… [pc.himHer]哼，”阿罗娜冷笑道。[pc.HeShe]其实它也没那么糟糕。 |"[pc.dcb |是的，我已经做了足够多的这类工作，现在几乎已经不需要再费心去做了。 |差不多吧。我和朋友们相处了这么久，他们似乎已经明白我想要他们做的事情是什么了。 |算是吧！我的意思是，他们都是非常聪明的人，而且我们已经在一起一段时间了。所以我其实不需要说太多话，也不需要发号施令什么的。 ][silly | 不过，手动模式确实能提供很大的帮助。 ]" ] 太好了！”她高兴地说，“那些真正了解自己在战斗中应该如何配合的战友，他们的协作效果肯定要比那些临时拼凑起来的团队强得多。女武神们经常要与我们几乎不认识的盟友一起作战，这通常会让战斗变得困难许多。而那些我们非常熟悉的盟友呢？与他们合作时，一切都会进行得顺利得多，其中当然是有原因的。 |你独自走在这条孤独的路上。[silly |我希望，这并不是你曾经认识过的唯一一个。 ]在当前这样的困境中，拥有盟友确实非常重要，但我也能理解，担任领导者可能并不是你容易胜任的角色。毕竟，领导力是一件极其困难的事情。[pc.dcb |这就是为什么我根本不愿意去处理那种事情。与整个世界为敌，这才是我喜欢的。” “你的坚持也是有限度的，”她指出，“但你说得没错，这确实很艰难。 |确实压力很大。” “是的，”她点头说道，“但即使有决心，技巧也可能不够。 |我敢说，总是负责与人战斗肯定很不容易吧！” “没错。既要鼓起勇气去执行这些任务，又要确保把工作的各个环节都做好，确实非常困难。 ] ] 如果你负责指挥其他战士，你就不能只是告诉他们该做什么，而是必须让他们真正理解你的意图。 希望某事能够发生那些根本就不是同一回事啊！” “听起来你……[pc.isBimbo | 我就见过这种事情发生！ |我是根据自己的经验来说这番话的。 ]她把头偏向一侧，夸张地叹了口气：“没错，我亲眼目睹了一位伊文尼斯领主和他的警卫发生了激烈的争执——因为那名警卫赢得了一场他本应输掉的战斗。 他的任务本来是诱敌入圈，但领主却从未告知他这一计划；他只给了他数量有限的士兵让他去作战，然后就任由他自行发挥，以为他至少会进行一番顽强的抵抗，最终才会失败。 那位警员并没有理解这个意思，结果反而不恰当地赢得了这场“战斗”。[pc.dcb |干得不错。 |说实话，这听起来还不算太糟。 |他真棒！ ] 赢了就是赢了，对吧？” “是的，但是……这次胜利并不是领主的期望中的那种胜利，这让领主非常愤怒。而且，他们的敌人中有太多人逃走了，这确实是个问题。本来他们本可以陷入一个可能会带来巨大胜利的陷阱，但结果敌人只是让他们取得了一场普通的胜利而已。安妮卡耸了耸肩，说道：‘普通的胜利也不错，尤其是当这些胜利是在如此艰难的条件下取得的。真正的问题在于，那位领主从未将自己的全部计划告诉过他的警长。也许他是想保留一些信息，以便在事情最终成功的时候显得自己更加聪明。[silly | 也许他这样做是为了增强故事的可读性，通过向观众隐瞒某些细节来制造悬念。 ] 或者，他只是认为向一个低级别的警员解释这些事情有失他的身份罢了。 [party.has arona |是啊，”阿罗娜抱怨道，“那些连告诉别人计划都懒得做的白痴，根本活不长久。该死的阿戈斯。” 你回忆起这段往事，点了点头。 [pc.isBimbo |哦，对了！你哥哥他们那些人……是啊，他真的应该更好地向别人解释自己为什么要这么做，对吧？ |如果他能多一点说服力，让大家都能了解他的想法，或许会对他有所帮助。 ] |[pc.isBimbo |你沉思地点了点头：“这就是为什么你必须告诉所有人你真正希望发生什么！ |那么，把整个计划告诉所有人其实并没有什么不妥吧。 ] ] [party.has arona |安妮回应道： ]正是这样。这样，每个人都能清楚了解目标。而当遇到意外情况，当现实情况干扰了计划时，他们就可以运用自己的判断力，来决定该如何采取行动才能达到帮助他人的目的。这时候，一支真正默契配合的团队才能发挥出真正的作用。他们信任彼此的判断力，也彼此了解、熟悉。我真的很怀念和我的队友们一起战斗的日子，因为我们就是这样的一个团队。[party.hasCompanions | — 和那个一模一样 [party.compNames] 目前已经 ]." [pc.isBimbo |所以你必须要和别人交流！我的意思是，我本来就已经知道这一点了，但这次的经历似乎更证明了这一点。在涉及冲突或争斗的情况下，交流确实非常重要。 |沟通之所以如此重要，确实是很有道理的，”你沉思道，“及时发出威胁，从不同的角度发起攻击——这些确实都是非常重要的措施。但如果你有一个共同的计划，一个大家一致认可的行动计划，那么这就更加重要了。 ] 尤其是当你一次需要调动几十甚至上百人的时候，”她笑着说，“三四个人就已经够麻烦了！[silly | 很多人都不愿意选择全手动控制模式来玩这个游戏，这是有原因的……当然，那些需要用一只手来操作的环节除外。 ]"

rows.original: "One of the first things a warrior learns is how to make her victories count. You can't just win the battle, after all. You have to chase the enemy down, force them to surrender or destroy them — otherwise they'll be back again to fight later or do other harm. And as valkyries, [pc.swornGod lumia |you and I a |we' ]re uniquely well suited to chasing down a defeated foe." The valkyrie spreads her magical wings wide to accentuate the point. "A stern chase is a long chase for those on the ground; being able to fly overhead makes things a bit faster." [pc.dcb |"Yeah, sounds about right. Fuck 'em all up. Or just fuck 'em. Whichever." Annika raises an eyebrow at you before continuing. "Well, that's the thing. |[pc.bg soldier |"Yeah, that all tracks." You cock your head. "Sometimes the goal isn't to kill 'em all, though." "You're right. |"Sounds awfully grim for a valkyrie." She nods ruefully. "Well, that's the thing. ] |"I bet! Still and all, what if you don't wanna, like, do all the grim stuff?" "Exactly, sweetie. ] Sometimes you don't want to destroy them. Sometimes you don't even need them to surrender. And sometimes there are other things that are more important. When valkyries win a battle, there are always some of us who stay behind — usually, after all, we fight with allies or to protect people, and they don't come through battle unscathed. Some of us are there to heal them, help clean them, or if they can't be saved, to comfort them in their last moments." [pc.dcb |"Sounds like a waste of time," you say sourly. |"That's not an easy balancing act to make." |"That sounds like a lot of things to worry about! Gosh, that's hard. I mean, no matter what you pick, it's going to feel bad!" ] "[pc.isBimbo |Yes, sweetie, but it's who we are. |It's who we are, [pc.name]. ]" Annika taps her sun necklace insistently. "Lumia protects. Some of us must pursue, if we can, so long as we avoid traps or ambushes along the way. And some of us must stay behind, hold a soldier's head in our hand, encourage him to keep speaking of the people and things he loves, and try to use our goddess's magic to mend his wounds. Pursuit is usually necessary, but having an army or a people to save at the end of the fight is, too. Sometimes warriors that don't pursue a broken foe do so because of indolence or exhaustion, and sometimes they do so because there truly are higher, or at least different, causes to serve." [pc.dcb |You have to admit it: "Even badasses get tired." |"[pc.bg soldier barbarian |Yeah, I can say from experience: a long fight exhausts you like nothing else |I can understand exhaustion being a huge part of things. A battle's got to be really tiring, especially the big ones that [pc.swornGod lumia |we |valkyries ] fight in ]." |"Yeah, I [pc.bg soldier barbarian |know |bet ] people get really tired. That[pc.bg soldier barbarian | makes |'d make ] chasing the bad guys even harder!" ] "[pc.dcb |They do |It [pc.bg soldier barbarian |does |is ] |It does ]. But your enemy has fought in the same battle. They're as tired as you are. What a chase is, is this: matching your determination against the enemy's fear. Can you make the most out of what energy you still have? Can you drive yourself onward, even though your whole body rebels against it?" The valkyrie sighs. "A lot of younger, less-seasoned warriors are prone to tiring themselves out during a fight and don't have much left to give at the end. Usually, it's down to women like me to pursue the broken foe. I'd rather help nurse the injured or ease a brave soldier's final breaths... but it is what it is." "What happens when they don't run away? You know, when they just lie there, squirming on the ground, showing their sexy parts, fluttering their eyes, saying 'Ooooh, I've been conquered by the mighty [pc.name]! Now [pc.heShe]'ll have [pc.hisHer] way with me!' Does that ever happen with you?" She stares at you for a few seconds before answering. "Well... yes, actually, that does happen. Some orcs [var0 |like you and your friend there |like your friend there |like yourself |like the ones from the islands ]; some siorcanna. Usually just loners or bandits. It's very strange. You'd think they could just ask instead of attacking you; if they're in it for the roleplay, it really does belong in the bedroom, instead of on the battlefield against a holy warrior bristling with sharps who doesn't share their fetishes." [arona.isSub |You know how fuckin' hot I get thinkin' about how [pc.name] put the smackdown on me for real? |Gets me hard, puttin' the smackdown on a slut like [pc.name] for real and actually taking my prize. ]" ] "To each their own," she says, shrugging. "S |"... Does that work?" "Sometimes," she says brightly. "Most are just disappointed, but I have made some very good friends that way, too. S ]ee, I'd rather fall in love first, and then if my special [annika.kissed |[pc.name] |someone ] wants me to go all muscle-domme in the bedroom afterwards, that's our business — and if [annika.kissed |you |they ]'d rather I just use these muscles to cuddle, even better. Conquest isn't really my style. "That's just me, though. Some of the other girls are more willing to indulge the men and women they fight who have that, mmm, particular fetish. Especially the siorcanna. Several of our siorc sisters got recruited into the Order by existing members who bested them in combat, decided to satisfy their new subs' needs, and fell in love. Three human valkyries in particular, Marla, Felicia, and Kristina, keep vast, willing harems of conquered shark-folk under the waves. They spend an awful lot of time tending to their needs, but I think they'd say that that's one of th[silly |em |ose ] good problems."[seastone.isABN | Then she winks. "Of course, there are a few girls who like it the other way — spend most of their time saving the world, go back to their siorc mistresses whenever they head underwater. Nothing wrong with that either, dear." | Then, grinning, she continues, "One that I hear you also have. Seastone herself, hmm? And every member of her harem, too. You don't think small, do you, dear?" ] '

rows.translation: 战斗结束后

rows.original: "If you're just talking about yourself? Yes, of course. Cleverer is usually better. When you're with a group, though, or Lumia forbid, in charge of one? I've known leaders who've thought they were very clever, but unfortunately, that cleverness usually got them into trouble." [pc.dcbc |"Blood and guts is a bigger deal, yeah." You chew on the inside of your lip for a little bit, then continue, "Still, outthinking the fuckers on the other side has gotta be nice, right?" |"Sometimes, brains aren't enough," you admit, "but being clever's gotta have some benefits, right?" |[pc.cunningRange 66 |"Hey, I work hard to be a smartypants sometimes," you object. "I think it's really good for winning fights and stuff." |"Yeahhhh. I mean, I think I do okay, and I don't always do great with thinky bits. But, like, other people with good... brain... stuff... um, are you saying that that's not good when you're fighting?" ] |"I don't know," you say lightly. "I think it's pretty nice." ] "It certainly helps," admits Annika, "but it only goes so far. You see, battle isn't a game, where all the pieces do exactly what they're told and the only things one must plan for are the minds of the two players playing it. There's the weather, the terrain, the minds and desires and frailties and brilliances of the hundreds or thousands of warriors serving you and your opponent. A commander might propose, but a million other things along the way dispose. Clever commanders sometimes come up with elaborate plans that fit with their cleverness, but the more elaborate a plan, the more chances for things to go wrong." [pc.isBimbo |"So, like, you do the one thing, and the next thing depends on the first thing, but what if the first thing goes bad, and then you have to do another other thing, and... oh wow. I'm already confused, and that's just... two things?" Your forehead gets all wrinkly, which is not usually your thing. "Wait, four things? Aaaaa!" |"Yeah, I can see how adding too many moving parts could screw something up pretty badly." ] "Exactly. And the fact that so many things could go wrong is special to war. The Red Prince once said that in a battle, even the simplest things are difficult. Under ordinary circumstances, a commander who sees his right flank buckle will send orders to reinforce it. But perhaps it's too dusty, and the commander can't see the problem quickly. When he finally does notice, he has to shout and repeat himself to the courier to make himself heard over the din of the battle. The courier gets stuck amidst marching troops for a while, and is delayed making his way to the reinforcements. The reinforcements misunderstand the order and march the wrong way for a few minutes before they realize their error. A million things add to each other and compound, each one of little consequence on its own, but when the sum is totaled, the reinforcements get there late and arrive in the midst of the collapse of the flank and the destruction of the army." [pc.isBimbo |"Ooof. That does sound bad. And that's one of the simple things, right? What if you try to do a really tricky thing?" |"And with a complex plan, there are even more failure points." ] "[pc.isBimbo |Disaster, usually |With the result that they usually end in disaster ]. Things just go wrong when you don't have a neat game board to play on. A clever feint, a series of ingenious countermarches, a maneuver to cut the enemy off: doable in theory, very difficult in practice." Annika frowns before continuing with a memory: "A few decades ago in the Heartlands, I met a man who survived the Battle of Arilat, and he had nothing but venom for the devious trap the generals tried to lay there. Splitting up the army, coming up with a precise timing for each group of soldiers to slam into the enemy, devising a series of interlocking effects to wear them down — everything needed to go exactly right and of course none of it did. The battle was lost and the army was almost massacred." [party.has arona |[arona.isSub |Your orcish beta coughs. "Nobody sings war songs about how fuckin' smart your plan was if it gets ballsed up. Damn, lady, I like you. I mean, you use ten words where five would be fine, but you actually know war. This is downright refreshing. Hey, mind if I add a stick to the fire?" "Go right ahead." "[arona.isMom|[pc.Name]|Boss]?" She turns to you. "All this shit about bein' smart but not too smart... I know you're the [pc.mf |king |queen ] of all badasses, but if a plan does go to shit for whatever reason, be ready to bail. Like I don't mean a little shit; anyone can fight through a little shit. Waist-deep, no problem. Lip-deep, whatever. I mean shit up to the eyeballs. You don't last long if you don't know when to fuck off and try another day." "Everybody has to retreat sometime," Anni agrees. "Not[silly | to the point of dumping their spice cargo ] at the first sign of trouble, but..." Arona grunts. "Yeah. So. Simple plan so you can't fuck it up, and if that plan gets fucked up anyway, bail. That's fightin' smart." |"Yeah, 'devious' is fuckin' stupid." Arona snorts derisively. "This elf has some real advice, beta bitch, even if she does take ten words to say somethin' that needs five. She's right, though. Keep it simple. Do one clever thing? Great, fine. Do six? That's not clever, that's bein' a dipshit." ] You place a finger on your chin. "[silly |So: keep it simple, stupid. |[pc.dcb |You're saying not to fuck around and be clever, just do the thing. |So it's best not to try to overawe the enemy with your tactical genius, then. |That sounds bad. I guess there really is a time to not be too-ooo smartypants, then! ] ]" Her singsongy answer: "Pretty much, yeah. Doing one clever thing can be a good idea. Doing many clever things is an awful idea." ]
rows.translation: 如果你只是在谈论自己的话，那么没错，聪明通常确实更有优势。但当你身处一个团队中，或者更糟糕的是，当你需要负责某个团队时呢？我认识一些自认为非常聪明的领导者，但不幸的是，他们的这种聪明反而常常给他们带来麻烦。 [pc.dcbc |勇气和决心确实更重要，没错。”你轻轻咬了咬嘴唇，然后继续说道：“不过，能够智胜对方那些家伙，那种感觉肯定也很棒吧？ |有时候，光有智慧是不够的，”你承认道，“但聪明总归会带来一些好处吧？ |[pc.cunningRange 66 |嘿，有时候我确实会努力表现得自己很聪明，”你反驳道，“我觉得这样在战斗中确实能帮助我们获胜。 |是啊，我觉得自己还挺不错的，不过在处理那些需要深思熟虑的任务时，我并不总是表现得很好。不过，嗯…… 其他 那些头脑聪明、思维敏捷的人……嗯，你是想说，在战斗中这样的能力反而没有用吗？ ] |我不知道，”你轻声说道，“不过我觉得它挺不错的。 ] 这确实有帮助，”安妮卡承认道，“但作用也是有限的。你知道，战斗并不是一场所有参与者都严格按照指令行动的游戏，在这种游戏中，人们只需要考虑参与战斗的双方的策略就可以了。 还有天气、地形，以及为你和你的对手效力的成百上千名战士们的思想、欲望、弱点与优点。指挥官可能会提出某种方案，但途中会出现无数其他因素来影响最终的结果。 聪明的指挥官有时会想出一些与他们的智慧相匹配的复杂计划，但计划越是复杂，出错的可能性也就越大。 [pc.isBimbo |所以，就是你先做一件事，然后接下来要做的另一件事又取决于第一件事的结果，但要是第一件事出了问题，你就得去做另一件事……哦，天哪，我已经搞糊涂了，而这其实才只是两件事而已啊？”你的额头都皱成了一团，真是…… 不是 通常这都是你的强项吧。‘等等，四件东西？啊…… |是啊，我明白如果加入太多的活动元素，很可能会把事情搞砸。 ] 正是如此。而在战争中，恰恰存在着太多可能出错的因素。红王子曾经说过，在战斗中，即使是最简单的事情也会变得极其困难。在正常情况下，如果指挥官发现自己的右翼出现了危机，他一定会下令增援那里的部队。 但也许这里积满了太多灰尘，指挥官无法迅速发现这个问题。当他终于注意到时，不得不大声呼喊、反复重复自己的指令，才能让信使在战斗的喧嚣中听到自己的声音。而信使在行进中的军队中滞留了一段时间，因此前往增援部队的路上也耽搁了时间。 援军误解了命令，朝着错误的方向行进了几分钟，才意识到自己的错误。许多看似微不足道的小事叠加在一起，最终导致了严重的后果——援军没能及时赶到，反而是在敌军侧翼防线崩溃、军队遭到重创的时候才抵达战场。" [pc.isBimbo |哎哟，那听起来可不太妙啊。而且这本来就是件挺简单的事情吧？要是你尝试去做一件真正复杂的事情呢？ |而一个复杂的计划，往往会带来更多的失败隐患。 ] "[pc.isBimbo |通常来说，灾难就是灾难。 |结果往往是，这些事情最终都以灾难告终。 ]如果没有一个整齐的游戏棋盘来玩耍，事情就会出错。一个巧妙的佯攻，一系列精心的反击策略，一个切断敌人退路的战术：理论上可行，但实际上却非常困难。”安妮卡皱了皱眉头，然后继续回忆道：“几十年前，在心脏地带，我遇到过一个在阿里拉特战役中幸存下来的人，他对那些将领们设下的那些狡猾陷阱充满了愤恨。 将军队分成几组，为每组士兵制定精确的进攻时间，设计一系列相互配合的战术来削弱敌人——所有这些都需要完美地执行，然而事实上，没有一样是顺利进行的。 这场战役失败了，军队几乎全军覆没。 [party.has arona |[arona.isSub |你的兽人同伴轻咳了一声，说道：“如果计划彻底失败了，根本没人会歌颂你的计划有多么高明啊。该死，女士，我其实挺喜欢你的。你说吧，明明用十个词来说这件事，用五个词也完全够用，但你确实真正了解战争。这种态度真的让人耳目一新。嘿，我能不能再往火里添根木棍啊？” “当然可以。[arona.isMom|[pc.Name]|首领]？”她转向你说道，“关于‘聪明但不能太聪明’这种鬼话……我知道你就是那个…… [pc.mf |国王 |女王 ] 在所有厉害的人当中，但如果是某个计划的话…… 做 无论出于什么原因，事情变得一团糟时，你都必须准备好及时撤退。我说的可不是那种小麻烦——那种小问题，任何人都能设法解决。但当情况严重到几乎无法应对时，你就必须知道什么时候该及时退出，改天再试。 “每个人都有可能需要退缩的时候，”安妮同意道，“不是吗？[silly | 甚至不惜丢弃那些香料货物。 ] 一遇到麻烦就立刻撤退，但……” 阿罗纳哼了一声：“没错。就是这么个简单的计划，这样你就不会搞砸事情了；而如果计划还是失败了，那就赶紧逃跑。这才是明智的做法。 |是啊，用‘狡猾’这种词来形容她简直太蠢了。”阿罗娜讥讽地哼了一声，“这个精灵给出的建议其实很有道理，虽然她总是用十句话来说清楚本来只需要五句话就能讲清楚的事情。不过她说的没错——简单点就好。做一件聪明的事？很好。但做六件呢？那就不是聪明了，那就是犯傻了。 ] 你把手指放在下巴上。[silly |所以：简单点就好，别太复杂了。 |[pc.dcb |你是说别胡闹了，认真点，赶紧把事情做完。 |所以，最好的做法就是不要试图用你的战术天赋来震慑敌人。 |那听起来不太妙。我想，有时候确实应该别太自作聪明了！ ] ]她那带着轻快节奏的回答是：“差不多吧，是的。做一件聪明的事情可能是个好主意，但做很多聪明的事情反而会是个糟糕的主意。 ]
